https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Giles Richards at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Kimi Antonelli closed out with the cool command of the greats to win the Formula One world championship by taking third place in the Mexican Grand Prix, a race won after no little drama by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, from the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton who was left fuming with his teammate Charles Leclerc, who finished fourth.
In taking his debut F1 title for Mercedes, the 20-year-old Antonelli has etched his name into the record books as the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953. It is Mercedes’ first drivers’ championship since Hamilton last won in 2020 and the team’s 10th.
Antonelli brought what has been a hugely successful campaign to a close as the sport’s 36th world champion at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to claim the title in only his second season in F1 and with a full four meetings still to go. Sebastian Vettel was the previous youngest winner of the drivers’ championship, aged 23 in 2010, when Antonelli was just four years old.
The Italian has been leading from the front for almost the entire season, having taken the lead after the third round in Japan. With the Mercedes proving to be the class of the field in the opening half of the season under the new regulations, Antonelli made the most of it and established a dominant lead. He won five of the first six races, outracing his teammate George Russell, who had been the pre-season favourite.
Antonelli went on to take nine wins in a season where he failed to score points only twice, on both occasions because of mechanical failures. Even as Mercedes were pushed by Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull, Antonelli retained a stranglehold on his lead, including sealing a win from 19th on the grid at his home grand prix at Monza.
Russell and Hamilton were his nearest contenders but neither was able to significantly narrow the gap to the Italian. They had to win in Mexico to keep the title alive but Antonelli’s third would have clinched it even had they done so.
Antonelli did exactly what was required of him here, kept his cool and did not put a foot wrong in a race that was run at a frenetic pace. Leclerc made a great start and tried to pass Hamilton for the lead at turn four but cut the corner to do so.
He did not give the place back and was investigated, with Hamilton furious his teammate had cost them a one-two in the race and let Verstappen ultimately into the lead. The stewards found Leclerc had gained an advantage in leaving the track and he was given a five-second penalty to take during his pit stop.
A decision with which Hamilton was unhappy. “The problem is he’s got clean air, and doesn’t have to manage like the rest of us. He should just give the place back,” he said. “The stewards are basically handing Charles this win.”
Later when the race was stopped he made his displeasure clear again. “We’ve got big problems. Big, big problems,” he said. A lively debrief at Ferrari is in store.
The race was red-flagged after Valtteri Bottas crashed out with a big impact at turn one. His left front suspension broke at high speed and he was helpless as the car hurtled into the wall. He took some time to climb out of the car but was able to do so unaided and was responsive on the radio.
It prompted a restart from which a feisty Hamilton moved up to second and Antonelli up to third, typically not willing to quietly do the minimum to take the title, which allowed him to seal the title with a podium place. Verstappen took an impressive win but Antonelli the crown.
The victory might be something of cold comfort to Verstappen given Antonelli secured the title, but comfort it will be to the Dutch driver and his team who will be buoyed by what was a hugely impressive run from fifth on the grid to the flag as they look to enter next season strongly. On this form the car is more than a match for Mercedes, potentially setting up the mouthwatering prospect of Verstappen and Antonelli competing consistently at the very front in 2027
The title for Antonelli represents a vindication of the enormous faith Mercedes had placed in the kid from Bologna, whom the team brought into their young driver program when he was 12. He was promoted to take Hamilton’s place last season, which proved a difficult year for the rookie, but since which he has adapted to competing at the very sharp end with alacrity and great skill.
He went into the race in Mexico needing only ninth place or better and despite only qualifying in fourth, delivered a nerveless drive indicative of the form he has shown across the year, to close out his first title with the same control he has exhibited all season. A deserved and popular champion.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.
The longest multi-day truce between Russia and Ukraine, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, has come to an end with no violations reported by either side, but also no sign of an extension.
The truce, which ended on Sunday night, allowed hundreds of besieged residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky to be evacuated in a rare joint operation between Kyiv and Moscow.
Russian strikes elsewhere in Ukraine on Sunday left hundreds of thousands of households without power, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. In Russia, meanwhile, authorities reported major damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks on the Nizhny Novgorod region.
The six-day localised ceasefire in the front-line Oleshky and the surrounding area was reached after mediation efforts by United States First Lady Melania Trump and with the involvement of Pope Leo XIV. It was set to expire at 10:59pm Ukraine time (20:59 GMT).
On Sunday, Ukraine’s military said it evacuated 167 more people from threatened areas of the southern Kherson region, including 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility requiring special assistance.
“Units of civil-military cooperation of the ‘South’ group of forces, in cooperation with representatives of local authorities, evacuated 167 civilians to safer points in the Kherson region,” Ukraine’s General Staff wrote on Telegram.
An estimated 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the temporary truce took hold. They were offered the choice to evacuate to Kyiv-controlled territory of Ukraine or territory occupied by Russia, or to remain in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.
“The ceasefire across Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region has provided residents with the freedom to move, access to food, clean water, medicine, plus a renewed sense of dignity without the constant threat of attack,” Melania Trump said on social media. “Let Oleshky become the starting point for lasting peace.”
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, quoted by Russian news agencies, said Moscow had a positive view of how the operation was conducted in Oleshky, as well as of the coordination between the two countries’ human rights commissioners.
A Ukrainian official, however, told the AFP news agency that Russia reportedly refused an offer to extend the ceasefire after Kyiv’s Foreign Ministry proposed it.
Since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022, Moscow’s forces have occupied most of the eastern Ukrainian regions of Donetsk and Luhansk, as well as the majority of territory in Ukraine’s southern Kherson and Zaporizhia regions.
Residents urged to remain vigilant
Kherson Governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged residents to be vigilant as the expiry of the ceasefire neared on Sunday.
“I also strongly urge you not to visit the so-called ‘red zones’ – areas and settlements near the Dnipro [River],” Prokudin wrote on Telegram. “The intensity of Russian strikes there remains high, and the threat to life is extremely high.”
Residents in Kherson city, one of the remaining areas of the region still controlled by Ukraine, remained calm, despite knowing the quiet of the localised ceasefire would soon end.
“Don’t be afraid, keep holding on,” Oleksandr Knyha, head of the Mykola Kulish Kherson Regional Academic Music and Drama Theater, told the audience as he opened a concert.
Knyha is from Oleshky and used to commute from there to Kherson for work. He has not given up hope of returning home.
“That’s also what keeps me here,” he told the Associated Press news agency.
Fighting elsewhere
Elsewhere, Moscow and Kyiv have continued air strikes, with Zelenskyy saying on Sunday that Russia continues to target Ukraine’s energy systems before winter. Attacks on power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight cut electricity to hundreds of thousands of households, he said.
A Russian attack also killed three people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Ukrainian region of Vinnytsia, when a drone hit the grounds of a vocational school, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said. Four others were wounded.
Russian drone attacks targeting Ukraine’s Kyiv region for a second consecutive day wounded a woman and damaged homes, energy infrastructure and a retail establishment, regional authorities said.
In its daily report on Sunday, Ukraine’s Air Force said that Moscow’s forces attacked Ukraine with 433 drones overnight, of which 371 were destroyed or suppressed.
Meanwhile, more than 100 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the skies of Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow, Governor Gleb Nikitin said on Sunday.
The attack sparked a blaze at the Kstovo oil refinery, Russian media outlets reported, sharing images of black plumes of smoke over the horizon.
Zelenskyy said Kyiv also struck a factory for missile components and air defence facilities in Russia’s southern Rostov region.
“We are justly defending ourselves against Russian aggression and doing everything to reduce Russia’s capability to continue it,” Zelenskyy said.

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/genocide-a.title: Gaza : l’armée israélienne tue huit personnes dont un enfant
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/genocide-a.author: La rédaction avec AFP
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/genocide-a.text:
Huit personnes, dont un enfant, ont été tuées dimanche dans plusieurs frappes sur la bande de Gaza, ont indiqué dimanche les services de secours du territoire palestinien et les hôpitaux locaux. De nouvelles frappes ont touché la bande de Gaza, dimanche, faisant huit morts. Plus de 1 500 Palestiniens ont été tués depuis le cessez-le-feu établi il y a un an.
Huit Palestiniens, dont un enfant, ont été tués ce dimanche, après plusieurs bombardements israéliens sur la bande de Gaza, ont déclaré les services de secours du territoire palestinien et les hôpitaux locaux.
Au total, cinq personnes ont été tuées à Khan Younès, et trois autres dans la ville de Gaza, a précisé dans un communiqué la défense civile palestinienne. Les hôpitaux locaux ont confirmé avoir reçu les corps, ainsi que plusieurs blessés.
« Des avions de l’occupation (israélienne) ont ciblé plusieurs policiers en service » à Khan Younès, a affirmé le ministre de l’Intérieur de la bande de Gaza. Sollicitée, l’armée israélienne a indiqué à l’AFP avoir ciblé « un terroriste » dans le sud du territoire « et plusieurs autres dans le nord », et être « en train d’examiner le résultat des frappes ».
Un an après le cessez-le-feu signé entre Israël et le Hamas, censé mettre fin à la guerre à Gaza, la paix demeure hors de portée, dénonçait l’ONU dans un rapport du 15 octobre. « Les bombardements israéliens se poursuivent, la reconstruction est au point mort et les négociations politiques piétinent », précisaient les Nations unies.
La guerre génocidaire israélienne, lancée à Gaza après l’attaque terroriste du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023, a déplacé quasiment toute la population gazaouie et a fait plus de 74 500 morts, selon le ministère de la Santé du territoire, dont les chiffres sont jugés fiables par l’ONU.
Avant de partir, une dernière chose…
Contrairement à 90% des médias français aujourd’hui, l’Humanité ne dépend ni de grands groupes ni de milliardaires. Cela signifie que :
- nous vous apportons des informations impartiales, sans compromis. Mais aussi que
- nous n’avons pas les moyens financiers dont bénéficient les autres médias.
L’information indépendante et de qualité a un coût. Payez-le.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: NFL roundup: Cardinals’ comeback stuns Cowboys; Lamar Jackson’s season could be over
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Arizona Cardinals 33–30 Dallas Cowboys (OT)
Chad Ryland kicked a winning 42-yard field goal in overtime after missing a PAT that would have won the game with six seconds left in regulation, and the Arizona Cardinals rallied for a wild victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The Cardinals beat Dallas for the fifth consecutive time and improved to 5-0 at AT+T Stadium, the home of the Cowboys that opened in 2009.
This was by far the most crushing of those for the Cowboys (3-5), who didn’t trail until the final kick and led by two touchdowns early in the fourth quarter. Arizona (3-5) were still in the game because Tyler Allgeier had a 63-yard touchdown run, a career long, followed by a 50-yarder to set up his second touchdown on a five-yard catch, all in the second half. He had 191 scrimmage yards (147 yards rushing, 44 receiving), all but seven coming after half-time.
The Dallas defense was having its best showing of the season before buckling in the last 16 minutes, particularly the final minute. The Cardinals went 80 yards in eight plays after taking over with 1:05 left in regulation, tying the score at 30-30 on Gardner Minshew’s 14-yard touchdown to Michael Wilson with six seconds to go. Ryland was wide left on the PAT kick after making his previous 58.
Baltimore Ravens 10-36 Buffalo Bills
Josh Allen set the franchise record for career touchdown passes and also rushed for a score and the Buffalo Bills took advantage of multiple Baltimore quarterback injuries to notch victory over the Ravens. The Ravens (4-4) lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler “Snoop” Huntley (right toe) in the first half while dropping their third straight game. Jackson missed the previous three games with a left ankle injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said after the game that Jackson needs surgery on the injured thumb and his season could be over. That’ll be a surgery deal. He’ll go to [injured reserve],” Minter said. “That’s a tough deal.”
Allen’s 11-yard scoring pass to DJ Moore with 12:18 left in the game was the 259th of his career, a mark that includes postseason play. The previous record was held by Hall of Famer Jim Kelly, who threw 237 in the regular season and 21 in the postseason for the Bills. Allen later threw a second touchdown pass and was 21-of-34 passing for 289 yards and one interception as Buffalo (6-1) won their third straight game. James Cook III rushed for 80 yards and a touchdown for Buffalo.
Minnesota Vikings 15–19 Detroit Lions
Jared Goff threw a go-ahead, seven-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:35 left and the Detroit Lions beat the Minnesota Vikings, handing the NFL’s last undefeated team their first loss. The Lions (5-2) have won three straight, including their first two division games in the tight NFC North. The Vikings (6-1) had a chance to stay unbeaten, but the league’s stingiest defense couldn’t hold on to a late lead, and they lost for the first time since 30 November 2025. The Lions lost All-Pro linebacker to a neck injury and he was taken to hospital. Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter. Lions coach Dan Campbell said he did not have any additional information after the game. “We’re thinking about him,” he said.
Atlanta Falcons 0-16 Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell’s rushing on a wet, sloppy field. The Buccaneers set a team record for yards rushing in a game with 324, and became the first team to have zero completions since Buffalo in September 1974. Irving ran for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, Gainwell ran for 140 on 25 carries and Chase McLaughlin kicked three field goals to stay perfect this season. Mayfield was 0 for 3 passing. Atlanta’s Michael Penix Jr threw four interceptions. Both teams are 3-5.
Cleveland Browns 6–27 Pittsburgh Steelers
Jaylen Warren tied a career high with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown on his 28th birthday to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the Cleveland Browns. The Steelers moved into first place all alone at 6-2 after beating the Browns at home for the 23rd straight time in the regular season, tying an NFL record. The Steelers dominated the line of scrimmage, rushing for 200 yards, including 160 in the first half alone. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson spent most of the day under heavy pressure. The Steelers sacked Watson eight times to drop the Browns to 5-3.
Tennessee Titans 36–43 Cincinnati Bengals (OT)
Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes in regulation and then scrambled untouched for a nine-yard score in overtime as the Cincinnati Bengals rallied for a thrilling victory over the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati have won three straight and are 5-2 for the first time since the 2021 season, when they reached the Super Bowl. The Bengals got the ball first in OT and went 70 yards in five plays. Tennessee took over but could not get a first down. Cam Ward had the first 300-yard passing game of his two-year career but threw incomplete on fourth down to end the contest. The Titans (1-7) took an early 13-0 lead, and the fourth quarter featured three lead changes and a tie.
Indianapolis Colts 7–42 Jacksonville Jaguars
Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes, including one to the previously benched receiver Brian Thomas Jr, and the Jacksonville Jaguars dominated the Indianapolis Colts in the rain to extend their home winning streak in the series to 12. Lawrence also connected with Bhayshul Tuten in the third quarter and rookie Nate Boerkircher on a 31-yarder in an opening half filled with big plays for the 5-2 Jaguars. It came five days after the 2-6 Colts traded two of their best players, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and longtime guard Quenton Nelson, to kickstart a rebuilding effort.
Las Vegas Raiders 38–33 New York Jets
Kirk Cousins threw two of his three touchdown passes in the second half and ran for another score to lead the Las Vegas Raiders to a comeback victory over the New York Jets. Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards as the Raiders (4-4) stopped a four-game skid, erasing a pair of nine-point deficits by scoring 17 of the game’s final 20 points. Las Vegas ended a streak of 12 straight losses when trailing at half-time. The Jets (2-6) scored on their first six possessions but frequently stalled in the red zone

https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.title: Mort de Jean-Claude Passeron, sociologue et co-auteur avec Pierre Bourdieu des « Héritiers » et de « La Reproduction »
https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.author: Jean-Louis Fabiani
https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.text:
Le professeur à l’EHESS, coauteur avec Pierre Bourdieu des « Héritiers » et de « La Reproduction », est décédé le vendredi 30 octobre 2026, à l’âge de 96 ans. Fondateur du département de sociologie de l’université de Nantes, il a contribué à asseoir cette discipline comme science. Son confrère Jean-Louis Fabiani lui rend hommage pour « l’Humanité ».
Né à Nice en 1930, Jean-Claude Passeron, très tôt orphelin de père, était le fils d’une institutrice engagée dans le combat pour la laïcité. Il aimait évoquer la mémoire de cette femme courageuse et déterminée qui lui avait inculqué les valeurs républicaines aussi bien qu’une forme d’optimisme athée.
Brillant élève, il monta à Paris pour entrer dans la khâgne du lycée Henri-IV et fut reçu à l’École normale supérieure en 1950 à sa première tentative. Il s’orienta d’abord vers la philosophie (il avait été reçu premier à l’agrégation). Comme beaucoup de jeunes de sa génération, il fut attiré par le Parti communiste avant de s’en éloigner.
Appelé en Algérie, il fut un militant anticolonialiste déterminé. Professeur de philosophie à son retour en France, il enseignait au lycée Périer à Marseille quand la concierge l’interrompit au milieu d’un cours pour lui dire que le professeur Aron l’appelait de Paris pour lui proposer un poste d’assistant à la Sorbonne.
Raymond Aron comptait sur ses jeunes assistants, tous philosophes, au nombre desquels Pierre Bourdieu et Roger Establet, pour donner à la sociologie, qui se constituait alors comme discipline, une dimension empirique qu’il n’avait jamais abordée. La nouvelle génération s’engagea avec enthousiasme.
Classiques de la sociologie critique
Bourdieu et Passeron choisirent d’abord le domaine de l’éducation : les deux hommes devaient tout à l’institution scolaire, mais leur analyse décapante montrait la puissance de l’éducation familiale dans la réussite scolaire.
Les deux ouvrages qu’ils publièrent à ce propos sont aujourd’hui des classiques de la sociologie critique, Les Héritiers (1964) et La Reproduction (1970). Le succès public de ces livres fit leur réputation mais ne saurait résumer la puissance de leurs œuvres respectives, d’autant plus qu’ils se séparèrent peu après la publication du second.
Passeron fut un bâtisseur d’institutions : il créa le département de sociologie de l’université de Nantes, appelé à devenir un lieu d’innovation. Surtout, il fut le moteur de la décentralisation de l’EHESS à Marseille, où il créa, avec quelques collègues un peu aventuriers et souvent provinciaux, une unité de recherche du CNRS, le Shadyc (Sociologie, histoire, anthropologie des dynamiques culturelles), clairement orientée vers la Méditerranée et l’Afrique.
Il ne pouvait pas se résoudre à ce qu’il appelait le « légitimisme » de Bourdieu : avec Claude Grignon, il publia Le Savant et le Populaire (1989), où il réhabilitait, dans le sillage de son ami anglais Richard Hoggart (La Culture du pauvre), qu’il avait fait traduire en français, la puissance du « style » populaire. Il ne faisait pas de doute que le Niçois, amateur de petits farcis, de socca et de tapenade, avait trouvé à Marseille, largement indifférente à la tyrannie de la légitimité culturelle, son lieu d’élection.
Audace et inventivité théoriques
La contribution la plus importante du Passeron de la maturité fut d’ordre épistémologique. Avec Bourdieu et Chamboredon, il avait proposé dès 1968 un programme très ambitieux de reconstruction sociologique dans le Métier de sociologue, qui fut pour plusieurs générations un précieux vade-mecum.
En 1991, il publia son maître livre (révisé en 2006), Le Raisonnement sociologique, qui revenait aux sources wébériennes de la sociologie : le point de départ de la description épistémologique réside dans l’historicité de l’objet des sciences sociales.
Histoire et sociologie ont en effet la même base empirique, qui n’est autre que le cours historique du monde. La nature de cet objet empirique commande l’ensemble des particularités épistémologiques de ces disciplines.
Les conditions de prélèvement de l’information sur le monde déterminent la nature des énoncés des sciences historiques : pour que l’on puisse dire s’ils sont vrais ou faux, il est impossible de les désindexer des contextes dans lesquels les informations sont prélevées.
Grâce au travail de son ami Jacques Revel, nous avons la chance de disposer de mémoires d’un genre particulier : Un itinéraire de sociologue (Éditions de l’EHESS, 2025) est construit à partir de longs entretiens où il décrit son parcours sans ostentation.
On y retrouve la verve du méridional, mais surtout l’audace et l’inventivité théoriques de Passeron, qui enjambe allègrement les frontières disciplinaires. Les jeunes gens de sa génération étaient de grands curieux, d’arrogants touche-à-tout qui se croyaient tout permis.
Leur impertinence et leur désinvolture élégante, au sens de la sprezzatura de Baldassare Castiglione, nous font largement défaut aujourd’hui. Ce livre, paru quelques mois avant sa mort, peut susciter la mélancolie qu’entraîne la confrontation brutale avec un monde perdu. Il est cependant possible d’envisager une lecture spinoziste de ces entretiens, contribution joyeuse et sereine au pur plaisir de savoir.
Le journal des intelligences libres
« C’est par des informations étendues et exactes que nous voudrions donner à toutes les intelligences libres le moyen de comprendre et de juger elles-mêmes les événements du monde. »
Tel était « Notre but », comme l’écrivait Jean Jaurès dans le premier éditorial de l’Humanité, le 18 avril 1904. 122 ans plus tard, il n’a pas changé.

All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway.
Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for the airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
“This is definitely a tragedy,” he said.
He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD.
Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.
The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach county sheriff’s office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.
A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.
The circumstances of the crash remained under investigation.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: ‘We have effing unbreakable love’: how the maverick Natalie Nakase led the Valkyries to WNBA glory
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Bryan Armen Graham
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
The mighty, miserly Golden State Valkyries won their first WNBA title on Saturday night with a point guard Dallas had given up on and cast aside, a starting forward who had been waived five times and a late-blooming All-Star once passed over by every team in the league. That made them a fitting match for their coach. Natalie Nakase has pieced together a basketball life on making small openings count, turning a walk-on place at UCLA into a scholarship and an unsolicited scouting report into a coaching job in Japan’s top men’s league.
The Valkyries’ nerve-shredding 68-63 fightback over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 did more than make them the fastest expansion team in major North American professional sports history to win a championship – as 45-1 preseason longshots in their second season of existence. It was proof of concept for an organization that gave overlooked players the resources, responsibility and trust to become champions – and enlisted a leader whose own circuitous journey had taught her what those things could unlock.
“We have unconditional love that’s fucking unbreakable, guys,” a keyed-up Nakase said during the trophy ceremony at a Chase Center that remained packed to the rafters, where Golden State’s 53rd home game had delivered their 53rd sellout crowd on a night that will be long remembered in the Bay Area as Ballhallaween.
“This is for all the people that have been underrated, misunderstood,” she said. “This is for all y’all, because this is proof: if you put all your heart and all your soul, you fucking win championships!”
From the first game in franchise history to a title in 534 days: the speed was extraordinary but the foundation was deliberate. Golden State had built a place where players could expect investment, opportunity and the trust of their coach – and were expected to give something back. The 46-year-old Nakase’s declaration of love came with demanding basketball obligations: defend, compete and accept whatever role helped the team win.
Veronica Burton, their starting point guard, had been waived by the Dallas Wings two years earlier, returning home to work out at the West Suburban YMCA in Newton, Massachusetts, with her high school coach while waiting for another chance. Connecticut signed her, then left her unprotected in the expansion draft. With Golden State, she became the league’s most improved player.
Kaila Charles had been cut five times in five seasons. Back at her parents’ home, training with her brother and mulling her professional future, she was preparing to visit Trinidad for her grandmother’s 94th birthday when the Valkyries offered a seven-day hardship contract. Now she was starting in the WNBA finals.
Kayla Thornton went undrafted, was shown the door by two different teams and spent years establishing herself as a dependable supporting player before becoming a first-time All-Star with Golden State at 32. Cecilia Zandalasini had started only six WNBA games before joining the Valkyries and starting 44 across the team’s first two seasons. Kaitlyn Chen, a relatively unheralded third-round draft pick, found a role backing up Burton and as the bench’s chief vibes officer. Tiffany Hayes, a former sixth woman of the year, had played more WNBA games without winning a title than anyone else in history – until Saturday night.
These were careers transformed by opportunity – by a team willing to explore what its players could become. Gabby Williams, the newly minted WNBA finals MVP and Golden State’s closest thing to an incandescent star, put it another way.
“All it took was good people,” Williams said. “All we heard last year was we don’t have no stars. We don’t have no talent. Yeah, right! We got good people. We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game.”
Nakase understood what it meant to have more to offer than others could see. She had spent much of her own career proving it.
A 5ft 2in point guard from a basketball-obsessed Japanese-American family in southern California, she turned down a scholarship to UC Irvine to walk on at UCLA, her dream school. A torn ACL delayed her start, but she earned a scholarship there anyway, became a starter and captained the Bruins for three seasons.
She never did make a WNBA roster. Phoenix cut her in 2007, before another knee injury while playing in Germany spelled the end of her playing career. She began coaching the Wolfenbüttel Wildcats of the Damen-Basketball-Bundesliga before moving to Japan, where she initially found a foothold watching Tokyo Apache practices. A scouting report she prepared earned her a volunteer assistant’s job under former NBA coach Bob Hill, before she eventually became the first woman to lead a team in Japan’s top professional men’s league when she took charge of the Saitama Broncos.
Then came a return to California and an internship in the Los Angeles Clippers’ video department. She spent a decade in the organization, working through video, development and coaching roles before Becky Hammon brought her to Las Vegas in 2022. Two championships as a bench coach followed, giving her a front-row seat for one of basketball’s great dynasties.
Her intensity can work against her. Nakase nearly fainted in the closing minute of the first-round decider against Dallas, prompting her to pay closer attention to rest, hydration and nutrition. During the semi-finals, she took the unusual step of giving herself a full day off. The coach who constantly urged her players to “empty the tank” had run up against her own limits. Nakase traced both that relentless drive and her instinct to invest in people to her late father.
“He’s the reason why I’m built the way I am. I am crazy. I am obsessive. I am a workaholic,” she said. “But it’s more just pouring into people, believing in people, helping people, that’s all come from my dad.”
Her extended apprenticeship mattered for a roster assembled largely from other franchises’ spare parts. Nakase and general manager Ohemaa Nyanin looked for competitiveness and character, studying even how players behaved when they returned to the bench. They needed people who wanted more for themselves and could still accept what the team required.
They worked at those relationships. On an early two-week road trip, the Valkyries organized dinners and games built around open, honest questions. Basketball, Nakase said, was the last thing they wanted to discuss.
“I love to learn about people, so I can push their buttons and go crazy when I have to,” she said.
Williams remembered evenings nobody wanted to end. “I knew we had something special on that trip.”
“Strength in numbers” was one of Nakase’s recurring messages, alongside “Empty the tank”. She backed it with her rotations, sometimes trusting the eighth or ninth player to finish games. Shared responsibility gave Golden State the depth to sustain their suffocating defense – the best in the league by some distance – and made a larger role a real possibility for everyone on the active roster. That extended to closing an elimination game with a rookie (Chen) while her starting point guard (Burton) watched from the bench. Opportunity depended on what the game demanded, while established players had to trust that the same principle applied to everyone.
The finals tested that bargain. Trailing Atlanta 2-1, Nakase moved Charles and Tiffany Hayes into the starting lineup, bringing Thornton and Zandalasini off the bench. Golden State won the next two games, holding Atlanta to 62 and 55 points. Trust had a practical application: players could lose their starting places without the team losing them.
There was individual greatness, too. Williams poured in 28 of her 30 points after half-time in Saturday’s deciding game, the highest-scoring half in WNBA playoff history, and was the no-brainer pick for MVP. Her explanation began with her coach.
“Nat told me to stay patient. I trust her with my life,” Williams said.
Williams had taken her own peripatetic journey to the summit, building a decorated career in Europe and with France while her WNBA progress came in interrupted stretches in Chicago and Seattle. “I may have done things the hard way, took my own route, but I loved it,” she said. “It built character, it built me into the person I am, and it landed me here. It landed me with the best group of people I’ve ever been around.”
The newly minted finals MVP explained Saturday what made Golden State different. “I showed up new to the team, the team already had a culture and relationships established but I walked into a group full of love and that just changed the entire trajectory of my career,” she said.
The conditions for all this mattered. Nakase linked up with an owner whose impatience matched her own and whose ambitions came with a pledge to provide the resources needed to fulfill them. Joe Lacob’s requirement during her interview was straightforward: whoever took the job had to win a championship within five years.
“I’m impatient,” Nakase said after delivering it in two. “I’m obsessive but it’s because he pushes me.”
She spoke, too, about the value of Lacob’s presence, of an owner who kept showing up throughout the playoffs. His investment gave the expectation substance. “Someone who invests in women’s sports,” she said, “this is a result.”
As the curtain falls on the WNBA’s milestone 30th season, the pattern is becoming impossible to miss. Las Vegas paid Hammon $1m a year to leave the NBA and constructed a $40m training facility, backing a championship core with the infrastructure to flourish. New York’s revival began when Joe and Clara Wu Tsai rescued the Liberty from willful neglect in Westchester, moved them to Brooklyn and invested in everything from recruitment to nutrition. Golden State have followed the same principle: invest deeply in the conditions for success, then demand it.
Money alone cannot create the trust that lets a coach change her starting lineup midway through the finals, but culture needs material backing. Players notice the quality of their facilities, the support around them and whether ownership’s ambitions extend beyond a speech. Increasingly, the WNBA’s championship race is being shaped by which organizations understand that connection. Golden State’s achievement is the most accelerated demonstration yet.
And this is hardly an exercise in altruism. The Valkyries recently became the first women’s professional sports team to exceed $100m in annual revenue, according to Sportico. The demand was reflected on the secondary market: Game 7’s cheapest available ticket was $364 roughly 24 hours before tipoff, outstripping every NFL and college football game this weekend, according to ticketing analyst Keith Smith. Turns out taking women’s basketball seriously is good business.
Lacob’s own accounting of the championship began with three women: Nakase, Nyanin and team president Jess Smith. “Those three women made this happen,” he said during Saturday’s trophy ceremony, before turning his thanks to the supporters who had embraced the franchise before it had a single player – and filled the 18,064-capacity arena in Mission Bay to capacity one night after another.
The culture belonged to that whole enterprise. Ownership supplied resources and expectations. The front office identified players hungry for responsibility. The coach created space for them to grow while demanding they make room for one another. The fans gave a new franchise an immediate sense of belonging. In the end Nakase was uniquely suite to connect those ambitions. She had spent her career asking people to look beyond the obvious credentials, then rewarding their faith with the work. She recognized that same hunger in the players Golden State brought together and it’s paid off faster than anyone could imagine.
The result was a championship in 534 days, built by people who knew how long a chance could take to come.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom
Canadian PM Carney announces progress in Canada-US trade deal talks ahead of US midterm elections on November 3.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced progress towards a future trade deal with the United States, which could help ease tensions between the two North American neighbours.
The Sunday announcement came just two days before the November 3 US midterm elections, which will determine control of the US Congress.
“Good conversation with US President Donald Trump on the future of Canada-U.S. trade,” Carney posted on X on Sunday.
Ties between Ottawa and Washington have been strained by an escalating trade war, with Canada and the US imposing billions of dollars in tariffs on each other’s goods in recent months.
“Teams from both countries will be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome,” Carney said. “This builds on recent constructive discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal.”
In his second term, Trump has upended global trade by imposing tariffs on many of the US’s allies, including Canada – one of the US’s biggest trading partners.
In August, high-level trade talks between Ottawa and Washington broke down, and Trump imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn of Canadian goods, or 5.5 percent of its exports. Canada responded with equivalent tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.
Trump said last week that he expected a new trade agreement with Canada to be reached “pretty soon”, but offered no details.
The trade tensions with Canada have become an issue in the midterm elections, particularly in Michigan and Maine, where Republican candidates have faced pressure over tariffs that have hurt local businesses.
Canada has sought to diversify its trade options and recently welcomed a European Union offer to become an “associate member”.
Carney praised the proposal’s ambition, describing his goal as a “unique alliance” rather than conventional EU membership.

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: Forget maxxing your life. 2027 must be the year we relax – and start minning | Polly Hudson
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Polly Hudson
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
Public service announcement: fellow citizens, we have maxxmaxxinged. It has been close for a while, but now we have gone over the edge – reached, and passed, maximum maxxing. The tipping point was a week in which we saw reports of Namemaxxing. If you can’t decide between two baby names, pick them both. Suggestions included blending Maeve and Avery to create Mavery, or Leo and Giovanni to make Leovanni – Futupid. Then Dictionary.com revealed its word of the year and, yes, you guessed it: maxxing. It’s fully exhausting, in every way, but mainly in that -maxx has been fully exhausted. For the good of us all, 2027 has to be the year of minning. (The second “n” is important, otherwise pits may be deluged.)
Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile – surely nobody who ever set out to funmaxx achieved it (see: New Year’s Eve), not even Dua Lipa. Minning is much more noble: it’s about making the world, rather than only yourself, better. Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, it means doing them less, if at all.
Andy Burnham could have leapt ahead of this trend when he unveiled his crackdown on headphone dodgers by declaring that he was loudcastminning. Other plagues against society with the potential to be similarly addressed are slow walking (dawdleminning), noisy eating (chewminning), not indicating when driving (mindreadminning), and absent-mindedly checking your phone mid-conversation (scrollminning). And let’s not forget dropping litter (binminning), turning up to a friend’s without warning (pop-inminning) and being over competitive (winminning.) Overall, this movement is about being as good a human being as possible (sinminning) but it’s also an opportunity to cut out habits such as drinking too many spirits (ginminning) and even negative familial relationships (kinminning).
Back in the days when all of this was fields and we only used one x in “max”, it was clear that max volume is too loud, max capacity too crowded, and max power too draining. Somewhere along the way we lost sight of that. Let’s take a deep breath, and enjoy the relief of leaning into minning. First person to suggest they’re doing maxxminning will be taken to the tower and made an example of.
Polly Hudson is a freelance writer

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Why did Democrat Haley Stevens just endorse a Republican for US Senate?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Why did Democrat Haley Stevens just endorse a Republican for US Senate?
Stevens’s endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers comes after a bitter dispute with Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed.
A Democratic congresswoman has thrown her support behind a Republican in one of the most closely watched races in the US midterm elections, just two days before voters head to the polls.
Haley Stevens, who lost Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary in August, announced on Sunday that she was endorsing Republican Mike Rogers over her own party’s nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.
The decision follows weeks of tension between the two Democrats over Israel and has provoked a backlash within the party as it fights to win control of Congress and limit President Donald Trump’s power.
Here’s what we know.
Who is Haley Stevens?
Stevens is a Democratic congresswoman from Michigan who narrowly lost the party’s Senate primary to El-Sayed, a former public health official who could become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.
Despite a bitter primary battle, Stevens promised to support El-Sayed and said as recently as Wednesday that she still wanted him to win.
That was despite her fiance, Jason Turkish, a Jewish Democrat and civil rights attorney, announcing that he would vote for Rogers. Turkish – who, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) reports, has donated nearly $250,000 to both Democrats and Republicans during this midterm cycle – accused El-Sayed of anti-Semitism, saying his rhetoric about Israel and the war in Gaza had made Jewish voters feel unsafe.
But on Sunday, Stevens changed her position.
Why did Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers?
The decision followed weeks of tension over Israel that became increasingly public in the final days of the campaign.
Stevens is a strong supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed has been an outspoken critic of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza and US military aid to the country.
Their differences were also a major issue during the Democratic primary, when a super PAC affiliated with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) spent tens of millions of dollars to back Stevens.
But the latest dispute began last week, when an independent group backing El-Sayed, Rebellion PAC, released an advertisement linking US military aid to Israel to Americans’ struggles with the cost of living.
The ad shows a couple shopping for groceries who decide to put back a carton of eggs because they need to save that money for “killing Palestinians”.
Stevens called the ad anti-Semitic and demanded that El-Sayed condemn it. She also accused him of making similar arguments by suggesting that money spent on Israel could instead go towards schools, healthcare and childcare.
El-Sayed said the ad was not produced by his campaign and that he disagreed with its message, adding that Stevens was trying to relitigate their primary rather than focusing on defeating Rogers.
The tensions came to a head on Sunday, when Stevens and El-Sayed were supposed to attend a church service together in a show of Democratic unity, but Stevens was uninvited.
“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” she said in a video on X, announcing she was going to endorse Rogers.
“And he’s right. And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”
But Democratic Congresswoman Debbie Dingell, who helped organise the event, said she was the one who asked Stevens not to attend, telling The Associated Press that “it had become way too distracting”.
Stevens also criticised El-Sayed’s association with political streamer Hasan Piker, whose uncle, Cenk Uygur, founded the PAC that released the ad.
Stevens told reporters on Sunday, with Rogers standing beside her: “We can’t stand with hate. We can’t stand with Hasan Piker”.
She insisted she was still a Democrat and planned to vote for Democratic candidates in 90 percent of the races on her ballot, but said her Senate vote would go to Rogers.
How have Democrats reacted?
Her decision has drawn an angry response from Democrats, including some of the party’s most senior figures.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called the endorsement a “despicable betrayal”, saying Senate Democrats remained united behind El-Sayed.
He brushed off questions about whether Stevens had betrayed the Democratic Party, saying he was more concerned about the issues facing Michigan voters.
“At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens,” he told reporters. “I’m just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all.”
He urged voters to focus instead on healthcare, civil rights and the differences between his campaign and that of Rogers, who is backed by Trump.
The Democratic National Committee (DNC) issued a blistering statement in response to what the organization described as Stevens’ “last-minute political stunts”.
“Haley Stevens’ disappointing decision to endorse Mike Rogers, a Trump ally who would join Republican efforts to sell out working families, is a betrayal of the values of the Democratic Party,” DNC Chair Ken Martin said. “At a moment when Democrats are united in fighting for Michigan families and standing up to Trump’s agenda, we reject these efforts to sow division within our party.”
The local arm of the DNC, the Michigan Democratic Party (MDP), also had strong words for Haley’s endorsement of Rogers.
“Haley Stevens’ decision to campaign with Rogers … shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about”, MDP Chair Curtis Hertel said. “We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum, and will not allow these eleventh-hour distractions deter us”.
Stevens’s decision also prompted resignations within her own team. Her chief of staff for eight years, Justin German, announced that he and several other staff members had stepped down over the endorsement.
“We are shocked and heartbroken by Congresswoman Stevens’s decision to support Mike Rogers,” German said in a statement first shared by CNN.
Trump, meanwhile, celebrated her decision.
“Wow, this is BIG!” he wrote in a social media post on Sunday before saying, during a rally in Iowa later in the day, he’d “love” if Stevens joined the Republican Party.
“Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump added. “It’s a thing called bravery.”
Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson, who flew with Trump to Iowa, also celebrated Stevens, telling reporters he sent the congresswoman a note after her “courageous” endorsement.
“Haley’s a good person. She’s always been very thoughtful”, Johnson said as he described Michigan’s Senate race as a “contrast” election. “She loves her state. She’s served it as best she could. She’s speaking the truth.”
Could Stevens’s endorsement affect the Michigan Senate race?
El-Sayed and Rogers are competing to replace retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters, in a closely contested race that could help determine which party controls the US Senate.
Republicans currently control both chambers of Congress, and Democrats are hoping to win enough seats to challenge Trump’s agenda and increase scrutiny of his administration.
Stevens defeated El-Sayed in Wayne County, which includes Detroit, and neighbouring Oakland County, drawing support from Black and Jewish Democratic voters. Both counties are Democratic strongholds where turnout could help determine Tuesday’s result.
The question now is whether Stevens’s endorsement could convince some of her supporters to back Rogers, or discourage them from voting altogether.
Polling suggests El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support, according to Reuters.
Early voting began on October 24, before the latest dispute erupted.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Mike Lawler flipped a New York district red in 2022. But his ties to Trump might bite him in the midterms
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Ariana Baio in New York
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
The Republican congressman Mike Lawler is in danger of losing his seat next week. Again.
In the last two elections, Lawler, 40, has defeated Democratic opponents in New York’s 17th congressional district – one of the closest-run battlegrounds in this year’s midterms – with moderate policies.
But with polls pointing to a tight race, and Donald Trump’s declining approval ratings piling pressure on Republicans nationwide, Lawler is not banking on re-election.
“Everybody who thinks they know what’s going to happen in November I think is fooling themselves,” the congressman told the Associated Press recently. “This is not like any normal midterm.”
Lawler’s tough-on-crime and affordability messaging helped him defeat a powerful Democrat in 2022 and flip the district, an area in the lower Hudson valley that leans more favorably for Democrats than Republicans, for the first time since the mid-1980s.
His reputation as a Republican willing to work across the aisle earned him key labor unions’ support in 2024 and convinced voters to keep him in office. Even Joe Biden, the former Democratic president, praised Lawler in 2023 for being “the kind of Republican I was used to dealing with” and “not one of these Maga Republicans”.
“What does it take for a Republican to win in NY-17?” an unnamed former Republican party leader was quoted asking in City & State New York, a local news outlet, in October. “You need to be Mike Lawler.”
Lawler is facing a new set of challenges this time around, as sustained frustration over the cost of living, tied to the impact of Trump’s war with Iran, looms large.
Lawler voted against a resolution that aimed to rein in Trump’s military action in Iran three times. He also supported Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was expected to cause half a million New Yorkers to lose health insurance and cut funding for a hospital in the 17th district.
He defended Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers’ actions after being confronted by angry constituents during a town hall in February and highlighted his working relationship with Trump while rallying with the US president in Rockland county in May.
Cait Conley, Lawler’s Democratic opponent, has pointed to the Republican lawmaker’s proximity to Trump throughout her campaign, hoping to capitalize on voters disgruntled with the US president.
“What we have seen under this administration – enabled by my opponent, Mike Lawler, who continues to vote with Donald Trump on every issue that matters 100% of the time – is he has made lives for Hudson valley families harder, not better,” Conley told voters during a debate with Lawler earlier this month.
“You deserve a patriot, not a puppet,” she added.
Lawler was already facing a tough contest. The Cook Political Report moved New York’s 17th congressional district from “lean Republican” to “toss-up” in January. While it leans +1 toward Democrats, polling has been unable to paint a clear picture.
In an Emerson College Polling/PIX 11 survey of 400 likely voters, 48% said they’d vote for Conley while 46% said they’d vote for Lawler. But another 7% were undecided. A McLaughlin & Associates poll, sponsored by Republicans, put Lawler at 50% and Conley at 47%.
Both parties have poured millions of dollars into the race.
Conley, a veteran and former national security official, consistently posts online reminding people that Lawler is allied with Trump.
Lawler has broken with the president on some issues. Last year, he fought Trump to raise the cap for state and local tax (Salt) deductions. He urged the White House to extend temporary protected status for Haitian immigrants; New York’s 17th district is home to a large population of Haitian immigrants. Most recently, he publicly opposed Trump’s diesel deal with Russia, stating that “not one penny” should go to Vladimir Putin.
“When I agree with the president, I’m willing to say it,” Lawler told reporters after a campaign event earlier this year. “And when I disagree with him, I’m willing to say it.”
Lawler has tried to toe the line between challenging Trump on certain policies while remaining largely supportive of the US president’s agenda. But his real strength as a candidate in previous elections was connecting with his constituents, who are also his lifelong neighbors, consistently hosting in-person town halls – even when they turn contentious.
Lawler knows his constituents well. In a district with a large population of Orthodox Jewish people, he has toured kosher shopping centers and introduced legislation to fight antisemitism. “I’ve seen Lawler more times than I’ve seen my rabbi,” Yossi Gestetner, a registered Democrat in the district, told the New York Times in 2024.
Such strategies worked for Lawler in 2022 and 2024. He’s seemingly leaning on it again this time around. On Monday, he took a page from Trump’s campaign book to work as a McDonald’s employee in Haverstraw for a few hours.
But should a blue wave sweep the country on Tuesday, Lawler’s district will be front and center. Whether his reputation is enough to convince voters to keep him in office remains to be seen.

https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.title: The best beauty advent calendars of 2026 in the US are already here and selling out
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.author: Lauren Gould
https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us.text:
Throughout the Halloween season, retailers flooded their shelves with candy canes, cozy flannel pajamas and holiday decor. The month prior, before autumn had even begun, luxury beauty retailer Liberty London launched its massive holiday Advent calendar, kicking off the season’s forthcoming influx of gift sets and the like.
These days, you can get an Advent calendar for everything from the viral Needoh toys to Redbull. But beauty Advent calendars can actually be a good buy. Unlike the humble, milk chocolate-filled ones, beauty Advent calendars such as Liberty London’s are stocked with typically high-priced beauty items at steep discounts, from viral lipsticks to luxurious moisturizers. Many are valued at more than $1,000.
- In the UK? Check our UK beauty Advent calendars guide here
Not all of them are worth your money – but others can make great gifts. Throughout the holiday season, we’re testing the most coveted calendars from brands such as Sephora and Charlotte Tilbury to find out which are worthy of your dollar – and we’ll be updating this list with the latest finds, as these items often sell out before fall is even over.
Have a beauty Advent calendar you think we should try? Email us at thefilter@theguardian.com
How we tested
I obtained samples of each Advent calendar to evaluate the packaging, quality of the products included and value overall.
I personally tested about half of the items in each calendar. I also crowdsourced feedback from friends with various skin types (and beauty interests) who tried the products. When it came to packaging, I looked at design and sustainability, and I tested how easily I could open each calendar’s doors.
Finally, I calculated the total prices of each product to check the accuracy of the calendar’s claimed value. I also tracked how many bestsellers were in each calendar, using data from Sephora, Ulta Beauty and other retailers.
Maison Louis Marie 12-day Advent calendar
Listed value: $306
Filter calculated value: $332 (excluding prices of exclusive items)
Packaging: Recyclable
Full-size items: Eight
Bestsellers: Two
Standout items: No.15 Vanille Infinie Votive Candle, No.04 Bois de Balincourt Mini Perfume Oil
What we loved
If your worst fear is smelling bad, then this is the calendar for you. It has a surprisingly vast selection of products, including a perfume oil and a candle, in a wide range of scents, from their bestselling No.04 Bois de Balincourt to No.14 Icila. The calendar’s packaging feels expensive, with a creamy white box that looked more luxe and felt more durable than most of the other calendars I tested.
It’s a shame that … there are no full-sized perfume sprays, just perfume oils and travel-sized rollerballs. It could also be a risky gift, as some people are picky about fragrances. However, each item is packaged in a small white box so you don’t have to designate this calendar to one recipient.
Revolve 25 days of beauty
Listed value: $953
Filter calculated value: $960
Packaging: Reusable suitcase
Bestsellers: Seven
Full-size items: 13
Standout items: Summer Fridays Dream Lip Oil, Illia Face Milk, Tower 28 SOS Daily Rescue Facial Spray, Ouai Detox Shampoo, Foreo Mini UFO Device + Call It A Night Mask Pack, Salt & Stone Black Rose & Oud Body Lotion, Abbode Sleep Mask, Dr Barbara Sturm Glow Drops
What we loved
More than half the items are full-sized, including the milky toner I swear by for smooth skin. After calculating the true value of the calendar, we can confirm that you would spend about $750 more if you purchased each item separately. The reusable pink suitcase packaging is a thoughtful touch and each beauty product comes in a separate pink box, making it easy to gift products individually.
 
It’s a shame that … there were a few real misses, including the Lemme Mini Debloat Daily Digestive Gummies and lavender dry shampoo. And, skincare newbies may be intimidated by a few of the pricier inclusions, such as Foreo’s high-tech UFO mask and Dr Dennis Gross’s skin peel.
Revolve 12 days of beauty
Listed value: $409
  
Filter calculated value: $534
Packaging: Reusable suitcase
Bestsellers: Five
Full-size items: Six
Standout items: Ilia Limitless mascara, Summer Fridays Cloud Dew moisturizer, Mutha Exfoliating Detox Body Bar
What we loved
There are plenty of bestsellers, including Sol De Janeiro’s Bum Bum Cream and Illia’s Limitless Lash Mascara. Just like the 25-day version, it’s packaged in a pink suitcase that would make a great gift.
 
It’s a shame that … Revolve’s 25-day beauty Advent calendar offers $540 more in value while only costing $60 more. If you don’t use peptide or lactic acid serum, its value reduces to $265. It’s also not a great option for makeup lovers, as it’s primarily filled with bath and skincare items.
Elf Beauty Advent calendar
Listed value: $153
Filter calculated value: $136.60 (excluding prices of exclusive items)
Packaging: Recyclable
Bestsellers: 11
Full-size items: 18
Standout items: Sheer lip and cheek tint, Eye cream, Liquid blush brush, Beauty sponge
What we loved
This calendar’s large range of products makes it a great gift for a teen new to makeup. There’s a liquid blush brush I use daily and a full-sized eyeshadow palette. I appreciated the high number of bestsellers included. One of my all-time favorite products is the liquid lip and blush tint, which I use nearly every day for a healthy flush of color. I also adore the beauty sponge, which is a lifesaver for quickly applying cream products in my gym’s bathroom.
It’s a shame that …  you’re only saving about $50 by purchasing the calendar compared with buying the items individually. The calendar’s doors are also hard to open, which cheapens the look.
 
Liberty London Men’s Advent calendar
Listed value: $1,185.81
Filter calculated value: $1,099.46 (excluding prices of exclusive items)
Packaging: Reusable drawstring bag, recyclable box
Bestsellers: Two
Full-size items: 14
Standout items: Bibbi House of Arthur Eau de Parfum
What we loved
There’s something for everyone here, from bath salts to eye cream. Our testers were impressed by the quality of most of the items, like Mz Skins’ calming moisturizer that one Guardian staffer said “felt very posh to have in my bag as my post-gym moisturizer and feels light and gentle”, and a cologne another tester (my brother) said smelled great and was long-lasting.
It’s a shame that … like the women’s version, this calendar is quite heavy. A few of the items also felt out of place for a beauty-focused advent calendar, such as the playing cards and socks. Testers also found the items to be quite frivolous and unnecessary, such as the hand pomade, which another Guardian staffer said wasn’t worth the money: “Why do people care so much about how their hands look? And if you do, why not rub something into them that doesn’t cost $35 for a 60ml tube?”
Revolution Beauty Advent calendar
Listed value: $135
Filter calculated value: N/A (many products not available)
Packaging: Recyclable
Bestsellers: Two
Full-size items: 10
Standout items: None
What we loved
The vibrant pink packaging and large selection of items would delight a younger tween dipping their toes into makeup. There are ample full-sized products for someone starting to build their collection, including a translucent powder and eyeliner.
It’s a shame that … I was unimpressed with the quality. The mascara didn’t add any lift to my lashes, and the lip oil felt sticky rather than hydrating. It was also hard to pry open each door, which made the packaging look messy.
Amazon beauty Advent calendar
Listed value: $525
Filter calculated value: $521.96
after newsletter promotion
Packaging: Recyclable
Bestsellers: Nine
Full-size items: 19
Standout items: Summer Friday’s Lip Balm, Biodance Eye Patches, Touchland Hand Sanitizer, Beauty of Joseon eye cream
What we loved
This Advent calendar has the most diverse range of brands compared with any other I tested. From drugstore skincare to high-end hair products, I appreciated that you could discover a slew of new products at a range of price points. Some of our favorite items included two tween-favorite products (Summer Fridays’ Lip Butter balm and Touchland’s hand sanitizer). The Beauty of Joseon eye cream was another favorite and is beloved by Karen Yuan, the Filter commissioning editor, who said her under-eyes felt “instantly soothed and hydrated after using”.
It’s a shame that … it’s currently out of stock. We also weren’t fans of some of the selections, such as Boy Smells’ Hinoki Fantome candle, whose scent Yuan likened to “burning leather and toxic men”. The box is also bulky and, unlike Liberty London’s calendars, doesn’t make up for it with an elegant design.
 
Anthropologie 24 Days of Beauty
Listed value: More than $300
Filter calculated value: $274.93
Packaging: Recyclable shell, recyclable mini boxes
Total items: 24
Full-size items: None
Standout items: Caudalie Vinoperfect Serum, Manicurist Active Shine nail polish, Living Proof Hair Gloss
Bestsellers included: Five
What we loved
This beauty Advent calendar is my favorite way to buy stocking stuffers. Each item comes in its own cardboard box, so you can easily gift the products individually (although I’d suggest covering the date on each box with a gift tag). It hits diverse beauty categories: skincare, haircare, nail accessories, perfume, bodycare and makeup.
I purchased the 2023 version when I worked at Anthropologie , and I still use some of the samples to this day (such as this magnesium body lotion with a relaxing lavender scent I love applying before bed). I was happy to see that a few of my favorites from that year were included in the 2026 version – including the Sunday Riley Lactic Acid Serum and Caudalie’s Vinoperfect, which I attribute to clearer and smoother skin.
It’s a shame that … the sparkly hair clips and press-on nails felt like throwaway items that I couldn’t see myself using, though they could delight any tweens in your life. The lineup also didn’t feel as universal as Liberty London’s or Charlotte Tilbury’s, as I don’t enjoy hair masks and am very picky when it comes to shampoo.
And for a calendar that purports to deliver 24 days of beauty, there are only three beauty items, and two are lip products – a liner and a glossy balm.
Liberty London Beauty
Listed value: More than $1,700
Filter calculated value: $1,722
Packaging: Reusable drawstring bag, cardboard and while some of the items came in separate packaging, others did not
Total items: 29
Full-size items: 21
Standout items: Sunday Riley CEO Vitamin C Serum, Ilia Limitless Lash Mascara, Violette FR Lip Nectar, MZ Skin Eye Cream
Bestsellers included: Seven
What we loved
Weighing in at just over 11lb, Liberty London’s Advent calendar makes quite the statement. It is one of the most storied beauty advent calendars, selling out every year for over a decade.
As a skincare fanatic, I enjoyed the number of high-end skincare products included (the vitamin C serum and eye cream that I sampled costs $300 by itself). Testers enjoyed the products they tried, including the Joonybyrd Haze Body Scrub and the Zelens Emulsion D fortifying moisturizer, which one tester said was lightweight and ideal for her combination skin.
I appreciated the vast number of full-sized products, and that many came in separate packaging, which allows you to individually gift an item. The brand also offers a robust men’s Advent calendar with colognes, pomades and even socks.
It’s a shame that … it’s primarily catered towards skincare lovers, as only five of the 29 items are makeup. Some of the products contain retinol, an ingredient that may irritate sensitive skin, though it’s a benefit for mature skin and those concerned with fine lines.
And its trifold design, while beautiful, is bulky and not ideal for smaller spaces. If you have the space for it in your home, though, it could make a wonderful display piece.
Charlotte Tilbury Hollywood Beauty Wonderland
Listed value: $400
Filter calculated value: $395
Packaging sustainability: Reusable chest of drawers
Total items: 12
Full-size items: Four
Standout items: Lip oil, Unreal Blush Glow Stick, Pillow Talk lip liner
Bestsellers: Four
What we loved
The packaging is lightweight, but still feels durable – and unlike the three others that we have tried, it’s reusable as a toiletries case for travel or just organization. It wasn’t too big, and it would fit nicely on a small vanity table. Aside from foundation and concealer, which it doesn’t include, you could do an entire makeup look with solely these products. If you’re restarting your makeup collection from scratch (or know someone who is) this is the calendar for you.
It’s a shame that … one-third of the items in this calendar are lip products, so you may want to skip if you’re partial to just Aquaphor.
And, while Pillow Talk comes in three shades (light, medium and deep), only the medium shade is included. One tester also found that the Lip Cheat contour liner rubbed off easily, although she did also note that she felt like Sabrina Carpenter while wearing it.
Lush 29 ½ High Street
Listed value: Not disclosed
Filter calculated value: $205
Packaging: Recycled plastic bottle ribbon and 100% recycled board fibers, biodegradable and compostable packing peanuts
Total items: 25
Full-size items: 25
Standout items: Christmas tree bath bomb, Swirly Sticky Dates Bath Bomb
Bestsellers included: Five
What we loved
While festive, the calendar also has year-round options such as Luna’s Butterfly and Butterball. The adorable shapes, such as Christmas Penguin, make this a perfect gift option for any tweens or teens in your life. These also smell wonderful, with scents including lemon and rosewood and strawberry.
It’s a shame that …. this calendar is quite messy. The bath bombs’ bright colors easily transferred onto the table as I took them out of their doors. However, the upside of this is less packaging. The calendar is also quite heavy and tall, making it difficult to store in smaller bathrooms. And, unlike the other ones on our list, you may not be getting a value. We totaled up the price of each items (using an average for the gift-exclusive ones) and found that it would be only $10 more to purchase the items individually.
What you need to know about beauty Advent calendars
Are beauty Advent calendars a good value?
This depends on the calendar. If you don’t plan to use a majority of the items, your money is better spent on individual products. In general, though, they offer a significant discount on the products as a bundle. We have confirmed the calendars recommended in our list do save you as much as they claim.
Are beauty Advent calendars sustainable?
When the Guardian asked this very question last year, Sali Hughes, a longtime beauty columnist, offered sage advice: “I think it’s worthwhile imagining all the products in a pile, without the seductive packaging. If it consequently loses its allure, then you’re paying all that money for something pretty ephemeral that will, if it’s even been designed responsibly in the first place, just go into recycling after Christmas.” You can also split the items with loved ones – reducing waste and ensuring everyone in your life has smooth, moisturized skin for the new year.
When do beauty Advent calendars sell out?
There’s no hard data around Advent calendar sales overall, but because these items are quite popular, they can go fast. If you see an Advent calendar that appeals to you, it’s probably prudent to buy it when you see it.
Megan Reynolds contributed research

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Bulgaria’s acting President Iotova leads in run-off exit polls
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Bulgaria’s acting President Iotova leads in run-off exit polls
Iliana Iotova would become the nation’s first elected female president if results confirm her win on Monday.
Bulgaria’s acting President Iliana Iotova is leading the presidential election run-off, according to exit polls in the race overshadowed by drone attacks on ships off the country’s Black Sea coast.
Iotova, who advocates for dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won just over half the vote in Sunday’s run-off, according to three exit polls, reported Bulgaria’s official news agency, BTA.
Iotova had 51 percent compared to about 44 percent for her rival, Andrey Gyurov, who is backed by the pro-Western opposition.
Exit polls put voter participation at about 27 to 29 percent, slightly higher than the first-round race last week, which had a record-low turnout of 23 percent.
Official results are expected on Monday as ballots are counted for the presidency which is largely ceremonial.
If confirmed, Iotova would become Bulgaria’s first elected female president.
The 61-year-old took over as acting president in January, when her longtime ally Prime Minister Rumen Radev resigned to run in, and win, a parliamentary election.
“I don’t like either of the two candidates,” Krassimira Kostova, a 64-year-old teacher in the capital Sofia, who voted anyway, told the AFP news agency.
Petar Doitchinov, a 67-year-old retired engineer, said he had skipped the first round last week because he expected a run-off. He said he voted for “the lesser evil”, as neither candidate matched his “vision of democracy”.
The vote comes as 21 people remain missing following a series of drone attacks last month on commercial vessels off the country’s Black Sea coast. They are suspected to be spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.
PM Radev has said that the attacks appear to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, though his government said there was no evidence directly linking them to Moscow.
Both presidential candidates have condemned the attacks and called for a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine.
Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister, criticised Iotova in a television debate for not explicitly blaming Russia. “Russia must stop its aggression so that the next steps can be taken,” he said.
Iotova said “peace can come only through negotiations”. After voting, she said she wanted “Bulgaria to be strong in a strong Europe” and “sovereign in its decisions”.
In the first round of voting last week, Iotova won 35 percent, with Gyurov on 32 percent – a much narrower gap than the 20-point lead predicted by opinion polls for Iotova.
Political analyst Teodor Slavev told AFP that voters were passing judgement on “Iotova’s unconvincing response regarding Russian threats in the Black Sea”.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Trump slams ex-lawyer’s $50m deal with pardoned banker’s family
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Trump slams ex-lawyer’s $50m deal with pardoned banker’s family
Alina Habba Mildon signed the lucrative contract while working at the Justice Department, before Trump pardoned the bank
US President Donald Trump has criticised one of his former lawyers for signing a contract worth more than $50 million with the family of a Venezuelan banker whom Trump later pardoned.
Alina Habba Mildon reportedly signed the lucrative deal while working as a federal prosecutor and later began working for the banker’s family while still being employed as an adviser to the US Department of Justice.
“I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous, and it’s not acceptable,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Saturday.
“Not acceptable at all,” he added.
According to The New York Times, Habba Mildon signed a four-year contract in October 2025 with a company owned by the family of Julio Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan banker who was seeking a presidential pardon.
Herrera was accused of bribing former Puerto Rico Governor Wanda Vazquez Garced in exchange for removing a financial regulator who was investigating his bank. He was facing federal bribery charges in the US before reaching a plea deal with prosecutors in August 2025.
Habba Mildon’s contract with his family’s company guaranteed her more than $50 million over four years, including an annual salary of $10 million and bonuses.
When she signed the deal, Habba Mildon was the acting US attorney for New Jersey, a position Trump had appointed her to after working as his personal lawyer.
She left that position in December after a court ruled she could not legally serve in the role. She then immediately took another job at the Justice Department as a senior adviser to the attorney general.
On January 1 , Habba Mildon officially began working for the banker’s family while still employed by the Justice Department.
Two weeks later, on January 15 , Trump granted Herrera a full presidential pardon.
The arrangement has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, given Habba Mildon’s government position and her ties to Trump.
The company that hired her, Concord Partners, has no public profile and its business activities remain unclear, according to The New York Times.
Habba Mildon has denied having any role in securing Herrera’s pardon.
Last week, she said she had never been paid to obtain a pardon, had never discussed one with anyone at the White House or the Justice Department and had never worked to secure a pardon for anyone.
Trump was reportedly furious when he learned about the size of her contract.
The New York Times reported that he told aides and allies that Habba Mildon should donate some of the money to his future presidential library or another Trump-related organisation.
He also reportedly told at least one ally that Herrera’s family should stop paying her the remainder of the contract.
Speaking on Saturday, Trump said he told Habba Mildon he did not want her to be paid, describing the situation as “terrible”.
The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
