https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Hybrid events help turn up Art Week Tokyo’s buzz
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: The Art Newspaper
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
A sure sign of an event’s arrival in the international art calendar is the number of collateral programmes it attracts. This year is a watershed for Art Week Tokyo in that regard, with multiple partners set to amplify the city’s November buzz.
Leading the way is a new project by the founders of the alternative art fair Basel Social Club. Tokyo Jazz Club, which takes place from 1 to 8 November in a former capsule hotel in the Jimbocho neighbourhood, will combine contemporary art, performance, music and food to create a hybrid space between an immersive exhibition, a social environment and a reimagined marketplace. According to co-founders Robbie Fitzpatrick and Yael Salomonowitz, the event is inspired by the history of jazz culture in Japan. “Jazz offers us a mode of thinking—a language of improvisation, listening and collective presence,” says Salomonowitz.
Also exploring notions of hybrid space is Project O+O: Gabriel Orozco at Higashi-Yama Tokyo. Orozco is collaborating with designer Shinichiro Ogata to turn a restaurant into an extension of his home from 6 to 29 November. Billed as a “living exhibition where artworks, specially designed objects and culinary experiences converge”, the project is co-presented by Mexico City’s Kurimanzutto and Tokyo-based producer Jam Acuzar.
Meanwhile, Serakai Studio, backer of the new Hong Kong cultural space Gold, is hosting a durational performance and installation by Taiwanese artist Liang-Jung Chen (4-5 November) as part of Certainly Tokyo, its pop-up exhibition at Path Omotesando.
These events reflect the global scope of Tokyo’s creative scene. Not to be outdone, homegrown media art and VJ duo MES is curating a lineup of DJs and performers for AWT x Shibuya Parco Art Night on 4 November.
• Visit the Events page on Art Week Tokyo’s website for more listings

https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.title: High Stakes and High Costs: NY Voters Hit the Polls as Hochul Faces Blakeman
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.author: Katie Honan
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.text:
New York City voters head to the polls Tuesday after a surge in early voting, capping a high-stakes campaign where affordability was one of the defining issues.
More than 690,000 voters had cast their ballots in New York City since early voting opened Oct. 24, up from more than 432,000 in the 2022 governor’s race.
Gov. Kathy Hochul, a Democrat, is hoping not just for a win but a more definitive victory than the one she eked out four years ago, focusing on affordability amid cost-of-living increases.
Her Republican challenger, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, has positioned himself as the savior of a state he says is overrun by crime and sky-high taxes.
The race, and Hochul’s possible margin of victory, will be closely watched by Mayor Zohran Mamdani and his team as they prepare to push the next governor to raise taxes on the wealthy to fund housing and childcare in New York City.
Both candidates spent the weekend on the stump, criss-crossing the state to urge voters to the polls.
Blakeman campaigned throughout the city and Long Island, telling supporters at a rally Saturday in Middle Village in Queens that “help is on the way.”
“I feel like a winner,” he told The City Reporter about the days heading up to Tuesday’s election.
Hochul was joined by top Democrats including Mayor Mamdani, who accompanied her at the Queens Night Market on Saturday and watched a Buffalo Bills game at an Astoria bar on Sunday, alongside Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
The governor was confident that she’d sail to victory on Tuesday, just like her beloved Bills.
“When you’re focusing on affordability and what we can do to help lift up New Yorkers, that is the message that is resonating,” Hochul said during the game.
Late Polls Boost Hochul
A late October poll by Marist University found Hochul was up 11 points against Blakeman, with 4 percent of voters undecided. A Siena University poll had Hochul up 14 points.
The biggest issue for voters is the economy and cost of living, according to an October Quinnipiac University poll. That’s shown in ads from both of the candidates, with Blakeman focusing on increases under Hochul.
At Blakeman’s rally Saturday in Middle Village, U.S. Army soldier Juan Nieves, 32, said his top priority was safety.
“I you don’t have law and order, we would have nothing,” he said.
Peter Kauffmann, a Democratic strategist, said Hochul’s re-election campaign was notably stronger than her 2022 effort, and with more emphasis on voter concerns.
“It’s great to see that she’s actually responding to issues that people care about, she seems really focused,” he told The City Reporter.
Hochul’s relationship with Mamdani has also energized her campaign and voters, even if Blakeman has tried to use it against his opponent.
“I think they will continue to govern well with one another,” Kauffmann said.
State Attorney General Letitia James is also up for re-election, and has been challenged by Republican Saritha Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor.
Recent polling showed James up by at least 15 percentage points.
The state Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli also faces Republican Joseph Hernandez, who ran for New York City mayor last year.
New York City voters will also decide on five ballot proposals that the mayor says will, if passed, cut bureaucracy around how the city builds bike and bus lanes, contracts with small businesses and sells and leases some properties.
Democrats across the country are hoping to reclaim the House of Representatives and the Senate with pivotal races in states like Texas, Maine and Michigan. The issues nationally match those in New York City: the rising cost of living, which is felt acutely in the five boroughs.
If Democrats prevail nationally, two Brooklynites could wind up running Congress: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. (New York City’s House races were largely decided in the June Democratic primary. Schumer and Democratic Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand are not up for reelection this year.)
A recent AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll found just 25% of polled adults approved of how President Donald Trump was handling the economy — down from 32% in July.
L. Joy Williams, the president of the New York State NAACP Conference of Branches, said affordability is the biggest issue “across the board.”
“I don’t think it matters in terms of race, ethnicity,” she said.
“Even though wealthier people are making money hand over fist, everybody else is not. That’s what’s driving people.”
Kristin de Guzman, a marketing strategist, met Hochul outside the Chambers St. stop on West Broadway on Monday, sharing that she’d voted for the governor the day before. As a small business owner, she was focused on the cost of living.
“I think she’s done a great job,” de Guzman said. “We care about the economy and affordability, like everybody on the planet.”

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: Will Trump relaunch his war on Iran after the midterm elections? | Mohamad Bazzi
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Mohamad Bazzi
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
Will Donald Trump decide to resume a large-scale war against Iran after the US midterm elections?
That question has loomed over the campaign for weeks, as officials leaked plans for a new round of joint US-Israeli military strikes that would target Iran’s underground nuclear facilities, missile arsenals and civilian infrastructure.
If Trump was reluctant to restart the war before the elections – fearing an even bigger loss for Republicans who are facing widespread voter anger over rising energy prices and other costs – he would have less to lose once the country got past 3 November.
But even if the president can avoid deeper losses for his party, would a renewed bombing campaign bring Trump any closer to a deal that would enable him to declare victory and move past the disastrous conflict he started eight months ago? That’s unlikely.
Trump can’t bomb his way out of the mess he created in Iran. One of the central rationales being floated by the Pentagon is that an “intensive” multi-day attack would force Iran to make new concessions in stalled negotiations. But this is the same folly that dragged the US into a senseless war in the first place, when Trump seemed to be convinced that the Iranian regime would fall within a few days of a surprise attack that killed its top leadership.
And Trump shows little sign that he has learned from the mistakes that led him into this quagmire, especially after he repeatedly promised his supporters that he would not start new wars in the Middle East. The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, spent months persuading Trump to join Israel in a war aimed at regime-change in Tehran. Netanyahu is at it again, urging Trump in a phone call on Saturday to restart the bombing soon after the midterms. Netanyahu wants a renewed war with Iran as he fights for his political survival, after his rightwing governing coalition failed to secure a majority in Israel’s parliamentary elections last week.
The president might still opt for a deal with Iran, instead of a wider war.
Over the past week, negotiators from Qatar organized multiple rounds of talks with Iranian officials, trying to avert a new round of intense fighting. Those talks reportedly led to progress on an interim deal, with Iranian leaders offering to reopen the strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to lift a blockade on Iran’s ports and release billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets. After the US and Israel attacked in late February, Tehran largely closed the critical waterway, through which more than a fifth of the world’s oil supply passed each day.
But an interim agreement reached in June to reopen the strait of Hormuz collapsed, and other negotiations led by Qatar and Pakistan stalled for months. The US and Iran mistrust each other deeply – and Trump makes it worse by vacillating between wanting a deal and repeatedly threatening to “annihilate” Iran.
“Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?” Trump asked in his speech at the UN general assembly in September. “Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly … Do I drive them into hell?”
While Trump’s threats are usually dismissed by the media as part of his bluster, the president’s vows to “wipe out” Iran naturally sow more distrust among Iranian leaders. And Trump could use a Republican defeat in the midterms as an excuse to exact revenge on Iran’s leaders, whom he blames for rising prices and his historically low approval rating that fell to 30% in early October.
If Republicans lose badly, Trump’s impulsiveness and thirst for vengeance could make him more inclined to order a large-scale attack that targets not only Iran’s nuclear facilities, but also its civilian infrastructure, including power plants, oil refineries, bridges and factories.
And if Trump follows through on his repeated threats to destroy Iran’s infrastructure, those attacks could further devastate the Iranian economy and would likely constitute war crimes under international law.
“If he feels embarrassed or disenfranchised he will do something bold,” one US official told Axios last week, explaining the possibility of Trump lashing out after a humiliating loss in the midterms. What might that humiliation look like? Democrats winning control of both houses of Congress and securing larger majorities than expected, especially in the Senate.
At a rally in Florida last month, Trump said he was considering “another little Epic Fury”, referring to the weeks-long US and Israeli bombing campaign against Iran that started on 28 February. In the war’s early hours, US and Israeli airstrikes killed dozens of senior Iranian military and political officials, including the supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
At first, Trump was seduced by the prospect of a quick victory, thinking he and Netanyahu could topple the Islamic regime that rose to power after Iran’s 1979 revolution.
But the Iranian regime was prepared to fight for its survival, despite the assassination of its top leaders: Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes against US military bases across the Middle East; it closed the strait of Hormuz; and it destroyed oil pipelines and gas fields in neighboring Gulf countries, driving up global energy prices.
Iranian leaders also quickly appointed Khamenei’s son, Mojtaba, as the new supreme leader, and expanded the influence of hardliners within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the country’s most powerful military force.
Trump’s war ended up trading one Khamenei for another – and emboldening Iran’s leaders to use their control over the strait of Hormuz to demand new concessions. And Iranian officials say they would retaliate for any new US military campaign that targets their country’s infrastructure with large scale attacks on American bases and the energy infrastructure of neighboring Gulf countries.
On Saturday, Mojtaba Khamenei warned that Iran’s response would be “immediate” and “without any geographical limitations” – hinting that Tehran could strike targets beyond the Middle East.
In the coming days, it will become clear if Trump can swallow his pride, and his quest for vengeance, and make a deal with Iran. Or if he will repeat the same mistakes – and hubris – that led him to launch this catastrophic war in the first place.
- Mohamad Bazzi is a Guardian US columnist. He is also director of the Center for Near Eastern Studies, and a journalism professor, at New York University

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Responsabilidade da esquerda dos EUA é acabar com o imperialismo, diz dirigente socialista sobre eleições de meio de mandato
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Lucas Estanislau
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Apesar do ceticismo em relação ao poder do Congresso diante dos arroubos imperialistas de Donald Trump, os Socialistas Democráticos da América (DSA, na sigla em inglês) acreditam que as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, marcadas para esta terça-feira (3), podem ser uma via para conter as agressões externas do republicano. Na visão da organização, o fortalecimento de candidaturas progressistas faz parte da construção de uma alternativa política que se oponha a Trump e ao sistema bipartidário estadunidense.
Em entrevista exclusiva ao Brasil de Fato, Luisa Martinez, integrante da direção nacional da organização, afirma que a disputa eleitoral é apenas uma das frentes de atuação do movimento, que também busca enfrentar o imperialismo dos Estados Unidos e fortalecer a organização da classe trabalhadora.
“A responsabilidade da esquerda estadunidense é acabar com o imperialismo, porque todos nós nos beneficiaremos de sua destruição. Assim como na Palestina, a libertação das pessoas neste país está diretamente ligada à libertação dos palestinos, cubanos, iranianos e de todos os outros países bombardeados ou estrangulados economicamente pelo governo dos Estados Unidos, liderado tanto por presidentes democratas quanto republicanos”, disse a cidadã estadunidense de origem chilena.
O DSA reúne militantes, ativistas sindicais e movimentos populares que defendem ampliação de direitos sociais e o enfrentamento do poder econômico das grandes corporações. Embora apoie e organize campanhas eleitorais, o movimento não constitui um partido político independente e não mantém vínculo formal com o Partido Democrata, legenda pela qual concorrem diversos de seus candidatos.
Nas eleições de 3 de novembro, o DSA e suas seções locais apoiam 131 candidatos em 30 estados e no Distrito de Columbia, segundo levantamento da plataforma de informações eleitorais Ballotpedia. Desse total, dez disputam cadeiras na Câmara dos Representantes, 52 concorrem a legislativos estaduais e 69 buscam cargos municipais. Entre os nomes apoiados estão Chris Rabb, candidato pelo 3º distrito da Pensilvânia, na região da Filadélfia, e Angela Gonzales-Torres, que disputa o 34º distrito da Califórnia, em Los Angeles. A organização também apoia candidaturas em Nova York, Michigan e Colorado, entre outros estados.
Apesar da possibilidade de avanço eleitoral, Martinez demonstra pouco otimismo em relação a uma eventual retomada do controle do Congresso pelo Partido Democrata. Para a dirigente socialista, os votos na legenda devem ser interpretados principalmente como uma manifestação de rejeição ao governo Trump, e não como um sinal de confiança em suas lideranças.
“Os votos a favor dos democratas devem ser entendidos como votos contra Trump. Nossas expectativas em relação às lideranças do Partido Democrata continuam baixas, independentemente de recuperarem ou não o controle do Congresso”, afirmou.
Martinez também denunciou a influência do lobby sionista na política estadunidense, vetado dentro do DSA pelo estatuto do movimento. “Como movimento socialista nos Estados Unidos, nunca tivemos dinheiro. O que temos são pessoas batendo de porta em porta e fazendo telefonemas para apoiar candidatos e campanhas que tragam dignidade à vida das pessoas e ponham fim aos genocídios que acontecem na Palestina e em Cuba, além de acabar com as sanções”.
Leia a entrevista na íntegra.
Brasil de Fato: Quais são as expectativas do DSA para as próximas eleições de meio de mandato? Quantas cadeiras vocês esperam conquistar e quais disputas ou cargos oferecem as melhores chances de vitória?
Luisa Martinez: Aspiramos vencer as disputas dos candidatos que apoiamos, como Chris Rabb e Angela Gonzales-Torres. Nossos candidatos assumiram um compromisso com nossa plataforma, que inclui rejeitar qualquer vínculo com organizações sionistas e um compromisso explícito com a solidariedade à Palestina e com o BDS, apoiar os sindicatos e uma semana de trabalho de 32 horas, taxar os ricos, garantir saúde universal (Medicare for All), habitação social federal, defender a polícia e abolir o ICE.
Quanto ao Partido Democrata, com o qual não temos nenhuma filiação formal, seu possível sucesso será uma expressão da raiva e da frustração popular contra o governo Trump. Os votos a favor dos democratas devem ser entendidos como votos contra Trump. Nossas expectativas em relação às lideranças do Partido Democrata continuam baixas, independentemente de recuperarem ou não o controle do Congresso. Acredito que exista um entendimento equivocado na América Latina sobre o poder do Congresso. No papel, existe potencial, mas, na prática, praticamente ninguém desafia o status quo. Há inúmeros exemplos, mas vou mencionar um. Uma das campanhas que organizamos depois que o presidente Nicolás Maduro foi sequestrado foi tentar pressionar pela aprovação de uma Resolução sobre Poderes de Guerra (War Powers Resolution) para impedir que o presidente Trump realizasse novos ataques militares contra a Venezuela.
Tecnicamente, o presidente dos Estados Unidos não tem o poder de invadir nenhum país sem a aprovação do Congresso, portanto, nesse sentido, uma Resolução sobre Poderes de Guerra é redundante. Foram os democratas que votaram com os republicanos para barrá-la. Com exceção dos candidatos federais que apoiamos, aos quais confiamos a tarefa de dar voz aos nossos objetivos populares, nós, como organização, não acreditamos, nem jamais acreditamos, que um Partido Democrata profundamente sionista, capitalista e reacionário vá melhorar significativamente as condições materiais de vida das pessoas pobres nos Estados Unidos e acabar com o imperialismo. Se esse fosse o caso, não seríamos socialistas.
Estamos no processo de construção de uma alternativa política, e o socialismo nunca foi tão popular nos Estados Unidos. Temos esperança no futuro porque as pessoas comuns estão despertando para a compreensão de que o capitalismo não é a única opção disponível.
Como o DSA tem enfrentado a influência do lobby sionista tanto no Partido Democrata quanto no Partido Republicano e como pretende continuar essa luta?
Na última conferência do DSA, os membros votaram pela aprovação de uma resolução que condiciona nosso apoio a candidatos ao compromisso com a libertação da Palestina e à rejeição da ideologia e do financiamento sionistas, R:22: Por um DSA Antissionista Combativo [texto abaixo]. Com esse compromisso explícito, vem o apoio material do DSA, que fornece material de propaganda para os candidatos e apoio na forma de voluntários. Como movimento socialista nos Estados Unidos, nunca tivemos dinheiro. O que temos são pessoas batendo de porta em porta e fazendo telefonemas para apoiar candidatos e campanhas que tragam dignidade à vida das pessoas e ponham fim aos genocídios que acontecem na Palestina e em Cuba, além de acabar com as sanções.
Quais são as principais estratégias que a esquerda estadunidense pode utilizar para enfrentar Trump e o movimento MAGA?
Somos um movimento, não um partido. Ainda acreditamos que as urnas podem ser um espaço de luta de classes, mas também lutamos em múltiplas frentes. Na realidade, a atuação eleitoral representa uma fração do trabalho que realizamos como organização. Por exemplo, trabalhamos em campanhas como a Trabalhadores por um Embargo de Armas (Labor for an Arms Embargo), que acaba de ser lançada. Estamos pressionando fortemente por um embargo de armas. Não se trata apenas de retórica: estamos trabalhando estrategicamente para interromper materialmente os carregamentos de todas as formas possíveis, em cada luta local que pudermos travar. Você pode encontrar os detalhes aqui. Outras campanhas que estamos liderando são a luta contra os centros de dados e as câmeras Flock, que são muito impopulares à medida que os Estados Unidos se tornam cada vez mais um Estado de vigilância administrado por bilionários do setor de tecnologia. Também apoiamos ou lideramos iniciativas estaduais, como a legalização do aborto, a restauração do direito de voto de pessoas condenadas por crimes, a energia elétrica de propriedade pública e o café da manhã gratuito nas escolas, para citar algumas. Se tudo o que o DSA fizesse fosse trabalhar em disputas eleitorais, não seríamos tão populares nem atrairíamos tantos jovens quanto atraímos.
A vitória de Lula e a derrota da extrema direita no Brasil dão impulso às lutas e campanhas do DSA nas próximas eleições de meio de mandato?
A lei que acabou com a escala 6×1 e foi aprovada representou uma conquista extraordinária para Lula e para a coalizão de esquerda no poder. Sua aprovação melhorará drasticamente a vida dos brasileiros pobres, e a importância desse esforço para a verdadeira virada na campanha de Lula não pode ser subestimada. Ainda estamos construindo a base necessária para aprovar uma legislação tão poderosa em nível federal, mas tivemos vitórias nos níveis local e estadual. Além disso, é uma prova de que o trumpismo pode ser derrotado.
A atuação de Erika Hilton como mulher trans negra também nos inspira em um momento em que a comunidade trans está especialmente sob ataque nos Estados Unidos.
Qual deve ser o papel da esquerda estadunidense na denúncia e no combate ao imperialismo dos Estados Unidos contra a América Latina e outros países do mundo?
A responsabilidade da esquerda estadunidense é acabar com o imperialismo, porque todos nós nos beneficiaremos de sua destruição. Assim como na Palestina, a libertação das pessoas neste país está diretamente ligada à libertação dos palestinos, cubanos, iranianos e de todos os outros países bombardeados ou estrangulados economicamente pelo governo dos Estados Unidos, liderado tanto por presidentes democratas quanto republicanos. Neste mês, Cuba recebeu mais uma vez o apoio da maioria na ONU pelo fim do embargo genocida que matou muitos cubanos ao longo de gerações. Todos os anos, há 34 anos, essa votação é aprovada, mas nenhum país teve o poder e a vontade de desafiar seriamente o governo dos Estados Unidos quando se trata de Cuba e da Palestina. Até que esse dia chegue, cabe à esquerda estadunidense conquistar o apoio popular e democratizar o sistema político dos Estados Unidos.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Comment | There is cautious optimism surrounding the contemporary art market—but will it last?
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Tim Schneider
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
There is an irony to trying to gauge the health of the art market, as so many in the industry are doing now, with New York’s marquee auctions, the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi and the latest Art Collaboration Kyoto ahead this month. On the one hand, the trade is endlessly driven by emotion. On the other, few broad-based, rigorous read-outs can be found of how the participants actually feel about the state of play.
But one exception that proves this rule was published recently: the September edition of ArtTactic’s report on confidence in the contemporary art market. It adds quantitative heft to the sentiment that has emerged from more and more reporting since the spring. Although the market has not caught fire yet, the findings indicate that significant segments of it have certainly thawed. More importantly, a cross-section of experts with skin in the game expect the (modestly) good times to continue for the foreseeable future.
Confidence game
So what is the Contemporary Art Market Confidence Report? Twice a year, the study asks a cross-section of collectors, advisers, auction house professionals and other market participants whether they feel positive, negative or neutral about aspects of the art trade and the wider economy in the US and Europe. ArtTactic then converts the ratings into a single score, from zero (essentially, no confidence) to 100 (essentially, absolute confidence), for each question, offering a quantified, collective evaluation.
The main takeaway is encouraging but measured. The overall confidence indicator rose from 43 (slightly pessimistic) in March 2026 to 56 (slightly optimistic) in September. It marks only the third time the rating has reached positive territory in more than four years.
However, both previous moments of optimism were short-lived. After hitting a rowdy 75 in February 2022, the rating dropped to 42 that July. And the January 2025 score of 54 plunged to a frightening 30 six months later.
Anders Petterson, the founder and chief executive of ArtTactic, thinks the current bout of positivity is more durable than the last one. In January 2025, he points out, 39% of the survey respondents expected Donald Trump’s return to the White House to produce economic policies that would boost the art market. “Instead, he introduced tariffs and a significant amount of uncertainty, which pulled down confidence for the July 2025 reading,” Petterson says. The difference now is that the “confidence seems to be grounded in a real recovery in sales, rather than just a belief”.
Steady state
Still, the experts polled by ArtTactic are nearly as wary as they are optimistic. Asked whether sales would rise, fall or stay flat over the six months to come, 60% chose the last of these options.
That may not sound great, but it isn’t bad. Remember, a confidence indicator of 56 means most of the respondents believe things are good right now, even if only just. In this context, Petterson says that a flat outlook for the next half year “suggests stability rather than deterioration”.
Some parts of the market appear steadier than others, however. Confidence in the auction market—up to 78 from 69 in March, spurred on by results at the top end—far surpassed confidence in the primary market, which nudged up to 51 from 45. Although this is good news for the trade at large, the visibility of strong hammer results tends not to boost all sellers equally.
“Most of the recovery at auction is still concentrated in the above $1m segment, which is likely to benefit galleries/artists operating at the top end,” Petterson says. “What is less clear is whether, and how quickly, that confidence will make its way down to lower-price-point galleries and artists.”
Galleries may need to do more to help themselves. On the eve of Frieze week, the American adviser Adam Green said he has seen “a noticeable shift” among many of his clients. Offputtingly high and persistent prices for new works have pushed several collectors who often used to buy from primary market dealers toward auction houses and private resellers, both of which “can provide a better opportunity to acquire works closer to their true fair market value”.
Although Green believes market recovery is “broadening to some degree”, he also suspects its full reach will take until the end of the year to become clear. If you wanted to translate the ArtTactic report data into one simple sentiment, it would be hard to do it more efficiently than in that sentence. Now we know this sentiment really is shared by more than just a few industry figures that we journalists happened to ask for comment.

https://taz.de/Handy-am-Steuer/!6226896/.title: Bußgeld bei Smartphones: Bilger für bundesweite Einführung von Handy-Blitzern
https://taz.de/Handy-am-Steuer/!6226896/.text:
Bußgeld bei Smartphones: Bilger für bundesweite Einführung von Handy-Blitzern
Telefonieren am Steuer kann zu schweren Unfällen führen. Handy-Blitzer sollen entsprechende Handhaltungen erkennen, doch die Bußgelder sind eher gering.
dpa | Bundesverkehrsminister Steffen Bilger will sich für eine bundesweite Einführung von Handy-Blitzern starkmachen. Der CDU-Politiker sagte der Deutschen Presse-Agentur: „Mehr als tausend Unfälle passieren jedes Jahr durch elektronische Geräte wie Handys am Steuer – Tendenz steigend. Das ist eindeutig zu viel. Innovative Technologien wie Handy-Blitzer können erkennen, ob sich ein Fahrer während der Fahrt ablenken lässt und ein Mobiltelefon in der Hand hält. Sie helfen, konsequenter zu ahnden und die Verkehrssicherheit spürbar zu steigern.“
In Rheinland-Pfalz habe man mit den sogenannten Monocams bereits sehr gute Erfahrungen gemacht, sagte Bilger. Für eine bundeseinheitliche Lösung brauche es nun eine Regelung im Straßenverkehrsgesetz. „Auch auf Wunsch der Bundesländer werde ich mich dafür starkmachen.“
Zuvor hatte die Rheinische Post über ein Papier zur Verkehrsministerkonferenz in Hohenschwangau in Bayern vor knapp zwei Wochen berichtet. Darin heißt es zu Handy-Blitzern, das Bundesverkehrsministerium stehe einer Prüfung offen gegenüber, eine bundesgesetzliche Regelung im Straßenverkehrsgesetz zu schaffen. Das Ministerium teile die Ansicht, dass moderne Überwachungstechnologien ein erhebliches Potenzial besitzen, um die Verkehrssicherheit zu erhöhen.
Laut ADAC wird an einer Autobahnbrücke eine hochauflösende, schräg nach unten gerichtete Kamera angebracht, die durch die Frontscheibe in das Auto hinein fotografiert. Das Monocam-System achtet auf Mobiltelefone im Bereich des Fahrenden und auf dessen entsprechende Handhaltung. Werden beide Kriterien erfüllt, löst die Kamera aus. Anschließend bewerten geschulte Polizisten die Bilder.
Bußgelder ab 100 Euro
Wer am Steuer beim Telefonieren mit dem Handy erwischt wird, muss laut ADAC mit einem Bußgeld von 100 Euro und einem Punkt in Flensburg rechnen. Bei einer Gefährdung oder dem Verursachen eines Unfalls steigt das Bußgeld auf 150 beziehungsweise 200 Euro an. Hinzu kommen zwei Punkte sowie ein einmonatiges Fahrverbot.
Telefonieren während der Fahrt ist laut ADAC nicht grundsätzlich verboten. Telefonate über eine Freisprechanlage, ein fest installiertes Fahrzeug-System oder ein Bluetooth-Headset sind erlaubt. Verboten ist es aber, das Handy während der Fahrt in die Hand zu nehmen oder ans Ohr zu halten.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. So viele unterstützen freiwillig und regelmäßig. Noch nicht dabei? Werden Sie jetzt Teil der Community! Jetzt unterstützen

https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/c.title: Can Bus Riders Form A Voting Bloc? We’re About To Find Out
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/c.author: Dave Colon
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/c.text:
The riders on the bus say, “Fast and free.”
Transit activists want to turn bus riders into their own constituency and voting bloc that can support Mayor Mamdani and other elected officials who install bus lanes and fund free service — and punish politicians who favor their car-driving counterparts.
Earlier this year, Mamdani embedded his 2025 campaign vision for fast and free bus service in an official city plan that promised to dramatically change the layout of streets across the city. 
To steer that vision, advocates with the Riders Alliance hope to organize bus passengers as a powerful political force.
“We’re really thinking about how to grow our organizational membership and build organizing hubs across the city that can really push bus rider organizing forward and create a more militant base of bus riders,” said Divya Sundaram, the campaign manager with the newly announced Fix the Bus campaign.
The Fix the Bus campaign represent a slight course correction for the Riders Alliance, Sundaram told reporters on Thursday.
Rather than encouraging bus riders and residents to support specific bus lane projects, the organization will instead focus on activitating riders in three key locales where the city wants to execute its ambitious bus rapid transit plans: Tremont Avenue and Fordham Road in the West Bronx; Northern Boulevard in Queens; and on Flatbush, and Church and Utica avenues in Brooklyn.
Beyond building new constituencies of bus riders to support faster buses in those neighborhoods, the campaign will also promote the mayor’s related goal of fare-free buses. That will require finding a durable funding stream that enables fare-free, frequent and reliable bus service. 
The promise of better buses drove Mamdani’s electoral success, and Gov. Hochul endorsed a joint city-MTA plan to speed up city buses. Both developments signal a rare opportunity for bus riders to secure dramatically improved service.
After two previous mayors touted bus priority plans that failed to liberate buses from traffic or reverse ridership declines, organizers said they’re not assuming this one will work without a good push from the public.
“Buses are of particular importance in outer borough communities, Black and brown communities, low-income and working class communities, so there needs to be more organizing, more energy of activation than to fix something high-profile, like for example Penn Station,” said Riders Alliance Director of Policy and Communications Danny Pearlstein. 
“We have a mayor who ran for office on fixing the bus, we have a governor who’s working closely with him, and they’re poised to take bus riders more seriously,” Pearlstein added. “But they still need that extra push to keep buses and bus riders at the top of the agenda. We need to make sure that we achieve the plan to the utmost because we’ve seen plans before.”
The campaign will offer operational support to bus riders who want to organize for better services, and Riders Alliance plans to hold events for riders to share their commuting frustrations and meet each other, assigning a lead organizer to each of the three geographic focus area. 
The ultimate idea, Sundaram said, is to help riders find, speak with and organize each other, and begin to think of themselves as people who ride the bus and deserve world-class bus service — not as people who have no other choice. She likened the vision to that of labor unions or the tenant rights’ movement, whose members explicitly “identify as tenants.”
“We’re trying to change how bus riders themselves actually feel and think about taking the bus,” she said. “I think a lot of bus riders see the bus as, frankly, an inconvenience, something that they have to ride, not that they want to ride. It’s a real marker of class in New York City, and what we really want to do is replicate and build on some of the lessons that we’ve seen from tenant organizing or union organizing.” 
Riders Alliance is not the first member-based organization to show interest in supporting the mayor’s transit goals. 
Before he took office, leaders from some of Mamdani’s most prominent left-wing backers — including the Working Families Party and the New York City Democratic Socialists of America — said that supporting the mayor’s bus plans went hand-in-hand with supporting the rest of his agenda. And the NYC-DSA’s Transit Working Group recently began its own bus rider outreach efforts to marshal support for both fast and free buses.
The task of persuading the city’s bus-dependent areas to support faster buses — and streets that prioritize buses over cars — is somewhat new territory for transit organizing. 
Subway-rich neighborhoods have typically presented the strongest opportunities for previous efforts to pass congestion pricing and secure dedicated MTA funding. Indeed, a neighborhood’s proximity to subway stations mechanically predicted the geography of Mamdani’s electoral success in 2025.
“The subway map maps very closely onto the places where the mayor did incredibly well in the primary last year,” said Pearlstein. “The bus map is a little bit different. Bus-dependent neighborhoods looked a little bit different, and that’s where we want to go. … It’s also places where there are a lot of people who drive, and bus riders’ invisibility is compounded by that fact.”
Skeptics in these neighborhoods have argued that bus upgrades only cater to transplants, a line of argument that has fueled reactionary backlash. 
Even though bus riders largely hail from non-white, working class populations, everyone from Holocaust-minimizing media outlets and neighborhood cranks to City Council members and the previous mayor have tried to stymie faster buses by saying bus lanes are for newcomers instead of the established community.
Sundaram said the Riders Alliance won’t avoid those conversations about change, but plans to focus its messaging on the ways that the bus specifically serves working class communities.
“I think there are a lot of valid concerns around how are our communities changing and who is New York really for,” she said. “And I think we have a lot of shared commitments and focus on [keeping] New York affordable for the people who actually built and keep the city running. Bus riders are nurses and home care workers and teachers and students, and the bus is getting those people the places they need to go.”

https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.title: Hoe de zaak-Reynders ons democratisch bestel op de proef stelt
https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.author: Tom Cochez
https://apache.be/2026/11/03/hoe-zaak-re.text:
Het fraudeonderzoek naar Didier Reynders heeft alles in zich om uit te groeien tot een Belgisch politiek schandaal zonder weerga. Nieuwe documenten tonen hoe verschillende dossiers waarover de schaduw van Reynders hangt, ons democratisch bestel ondermijnen. Om welke dossiers gaat het ook al weer? En wie dreigt meegesleept te worden?
Recent gelekte versleutelde whatsappberichten tussen Didier Reynders, een (toenmalige) topman van de Belgische Staatsveiligheid én een edelman die spioneert voor de Russen en de Chinezen tillen het gerechtelijk onderzoek naar witwas en fraude tegen de gevallen toppoliticus naar een ander niveau.
Ze geven aan dat Reynders niet enkel zichzelf zou hebben verrijkt, maar bevatten ook ernstige aanwijzingen dat een van Belgiës machtigste politici in de afgelopen decennia zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden.
Reynders zou niet enkel zichzelf hebben verrijkt. Er zijn ook aanwijzingen dat hij zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden
De mogelijke gevolgen daarvan zijn verregaand. Niet enkel voor de gewezen liberale topman zelf en voor zijn directe entourage, maar mogelijk ook voor andere politieke partijen waarmee Reynders decennialang direct of indirect zaakjes regelde.
Het hoeft dan ook geen betoog dat het onderzoek kreunt onder gigantische druk. De belangen zijn groot en bij een eventuele val dreigt Reynders anderen met zich mee te sleuren. Een overzicht van wat er op het spel staat.
Video-interview met Nicolas Ullens
In 2019 sprak Apache uitgebreid met voormalig inspecteur van de Belgische staatsveiligheid Nicolas Ullens. Bij die gelegenheid maakten we ook beelden van zijn getuigenis. We beslisten toen om de beelden niet te gebruiken en enkel te schrijven over zaken die we na verder onderzoek konden aantonen en hardmaken. Vandaag liggen de kaarten anders.
Didier Reynders en zijn eeuwige rechterhand Jean-Claude Fontinoy zijn in verdenking gesteld voor witwaspraktijken, en gelekte whatsappberichten tonen dat Didier Reynders zijn netwerk gebruikte om de voormalige inspecteur van staatsveiligheid die op kwalijke dossiers rond Reynders en Fontinoy stuitte, het werken onmogelijk te maken.
Daarom stofferen we dit overzicht met korte fragmenten uit het interview van 2019 wanneer die meer duiding geven bij de beschreven feiten.
Hoe kwam Didier Reynders in beeld bij het gerecht?
In 2022 meldde de Nationale Loterij dat Didier Reynders jarenlang spelen van de Nationale Loterij zou hebben gebruikt om zwart geld wit te wassen. De speurders focussen op ruim 1 miljoen euro aan verdachte transacties. Het gaat grotendeels – voor ongeveer 836.000 euro – over cashgeld dat Reynders gespreid over vele jaren stortte op een bankrekening van ING en over ruim 200.000 euro voor kansspelen bij de Nationale Loterij.
Moest ING dergelijke verdachte transacties niet aangeven?
Zeker en vast. Hoewel de stortingen al jarenlang aan de gang waren, meldde de bank de verdachte stortingen pas in 2023 aan de Cel voor Financiële Informatieverwerking, betere bekend als de antiwitwascel. Onderzoek van de Nationale Bank en de Centrale Dienst voor de Bestrijding van Corruptie geeft aan dat de bank effectief medeplichtig was aan witwas. Het parket sloot afgelopen voorjaar een minnelijke schikking af met ING. De bank betaalde 1,6 miljoen euro – het maximumbedrag om betrokkenheid bij witwassen te sanctioneren – om een rechtszaak te vermijden.
Hoewel de stortingen al jarenlang aan de gang waren, meldde ING de verdachte stortingen pas in 2023 aan de Cel voor Financiële Informatieverwerking
Vorig jaar werd de ex-politicus officieel in verdenking gesteld, enkele maanden gebeurde hetzelfde met zijn rechterhand en een bevriende antiquair
Werd Didier Reynders intussen in verdenking gesteld?
Het voormalige kopstuk van de MR werd een jaar terug – op 16 oktober 2025 – officieel in verdenking gesteld. Vier maanden later gebeurde hetzelfde met Jean-Claude Fontinoy en Olivier Theunissen.
Fontinoy was decennialang de rechterhand van Didier Reynders en kreeg in die rol allerlei cruciale posities toegemeten. Vooral binnen de Regie der Gebouwen die het overheidspatrimonium beheert en bij de NMBS zat Fontinoy op de juiste plek om grote vastgoeddeals met overheidsgebouwen en terreinen van de NMBS te overzien.
Olivier Theunissen zou als antiquair een sleutelrol spelen bij het witwassen van geld via antiek en kunst. Fontinoy was jarenlang kind aan huis in de antiekzaak van Theunissen en zou er op zeer geregelde basis antiek hebben gekocht met cashgeld. Er volgden huiszoekingen bij zowel Theunissen als Fontinoy. Eerder getuigden verschillende bronnen aan Apache dat de woning van Fontinoy propvol antiek staat waarbij “alles te koop is” voor bezoekers.
Maar het onderzoek gaat verder dan enkel witwas via spelen van de Nationale Loterij, cashstortingen en witwas via antiek en kunst?
Waar de speurders exact naar kijken is onduidelijk. Wel zeker is dat ze de hand wisten te leggen op de eerder vermelde whatsappberichtjes tussen Reynders, een (toenmalige) topman van de Belgische Staatsveiligheid en een edelman die spioneert voor de Russen en de Chinezen.
Waarom zijn die belangrijk?
Omdat ze erop wijzen dat Reynders mogelijk decennialang zeer nauw samenwerkte met vijandige buitenlandse mogendheden.

Waarom wijzen ze in die richting?
Daarvoor moeten we terug naar verklaringen die Nicola Ullens al in 2019 aflegde. Ullens was inspecteur van 2007 tot 2018. In essentie komen zijn verklaringen erop neer dat Didier Reynders verschillende onderzoeken die binnen de Belgische Staatsveiligheid liepen in de kiem smoorde.
Het gaat om onderzoeken die gebeurden zowel binnen de afdeling economische contraspionage als binnen de afdelingen Rusland en China, waarin Reynders en zijn rechterhand Fontinoy opdoken. Meer informatie over de concrete dossiers volgt verderop.
Reynders creëerde een nieuwe directeursfunctie bij staatsveiligheid en dropte daar een voormalige kabinetsmedewerker
Reynders creëerde een nieuwe functie – een soort derde directeur – binnen de staatsveiligheid en plaatste er zijn voormalige kabinetsmedewerker Hugues Brulin. Een andere vertrouweling van Reynders kwam aan het hoofd te staan van de eerder genoemde afdelingen waar het bezwarend materiaal rond Reynders circuleerde.
Finaal werd de dienst economische contraspionage opgedoekt. Nicolas Ullens werd het werken onmogelijk gemaakt en stapte op.
En hij getuigde over de mistoestanden?
Ullens klopte eerst, nog als dienstdoend inspecteur, aan bij het Comité I – dat toeziet op het correct functioneren van de inlichtingendiensten – om de mistoestanden aan te kaarten. Toen hij na twee bezoeken een derde keer terugkwam om de verslagen van zijn getuigenissen te ondertekenen, zou er een verregaande intimidatiepoging zijn geweest.
“Tot mijn grote verbazing zei Frank Franceus (chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I en ex-kabinetschef van Geert Bourgeois, red.) me dat het ondertekenen van de verslagen van mijn getuigenis levensgevaarlijk zou zijn”, zei Nicolas Ullens daarover indertijd aan Apache.
“Franceus zei dat ik vier kinderen had en dat het ook voor hen gevaarlijk zou zijn. Net als voor mijn vrouw. Ik was in shock. Die nacht heb ik verschillende brieven geschreven aan een aantal naaste vrienden, met de vraag ze openbaar te maken mocht me iets overkomen.”
Nicolas Ullens diende een klacht in bij het federaal parket wegens doodsbedreigingen door de chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I
Nam Ullens nog andere initiatieven?
Hij diende een klacht in bij het federaal parket wegens doodsbedreigingen door de chef enquêtedienst van het Comité I en wegens belaging binnen de staatsveiligheid door vertrouwelingen van Didier Reynders. Die klacht liep in 2021 af met een sisser.
Ook een ander opsporingsonderzoek tegen onder meer Jean-Claude Fontinoy bij het Brussels parket werd in oktober 2019 geseponeerd. Dat gebeurde vijf dagen voor Reynders als toenmalig kandidaat EU-commissaris voor Justitie en de Rechtstaat, door het Europees Parlement op de rooster zou worden gelegd en hij een hangend opsporingsonderzoek kon missen als kiespijn.
Samen met de seponering leken de getuigenissen van Nicolas Ullens een stille dood te sterven. Didier Reynders en Jean-Claude Fontinoy konden herademen. Daar alludeerde Hugues Brulin duidelijk op in zijn whatsappconversatie met Didier Reynders:
“Goed Nieuws .. Een single malt op uw gezondheid mijnheer de minister en ter uwer beschikking voor de tegenaanval als u dat opportuun acht … Met respect. Hugues”, klonk het op 27 september, de dag van de seponering.
“Veel dank Hughues, ook voor de vriendschappelijke steun deze voorbije dagen, Didier”, appte Reynders terug.
Het is maar een van de berichten die aangeven hoe nauw Reynders – op dat moment nog Belgisch minister – rechtstreeks samenwerkte met een topman bij de Belgische staatsveiligheid.
Tot wanneer stuurden Brulin en Reynders berichtjes naar elkaar?
De gerechtelijke politie heeft minstens berichten onderschept tot april 2023. In de laatste berichten bespreken Brulin en Reynders de dood van Myriam Ullens, de stiefmoeder van Nicolas Ullens die door Nicolas Ullens zelf werd doodgeschoten.
Het sterk gemediatiseerde assisenproces daarover hervat woensdag (4/11). Brulin en Reynders tonen zich opgelucht dat Nicolas Ullens nu definitief van het toneel zal verdwijnen. “Il nous aura quand même fait souffrir l’animal”, schrijft Brulin aan Reynders: “Hij heeft ons erg doen afzien, de smeerlap”.
De mannetjes van Reynders moesten het Nicolas Ullens (en anderen binnen de staatsveiligheid) onmogelijk maken om verder onderzoek te doen in concrete dossiers die richting Reynders of Fontinoy wezen. Over welke dossiers gaat het?
Wellicht het belangrijkste dossier waar Nicolas Ullens als inspecteur bij de staatsveiligheid tegenaan liep, is Kazachgate. België keurde in 2011 versneld de fameuze afkoopwet goed. Die wet liet toe dat verdachten hun proces konden afkopen. Naast een aantal grote diamantprocessen kwam daarbij vooral de steenrijke, in België residerende Oezbeekse oligarch (die vaak onterecht als Kazach wordt omschreven) Patokh Chodiev in beeld. Als een van de eersten maakte hij gebruik van de afkoopwet.
Chodiev betaalde amper een half miljoen euro om een rechtszaak te vermijden over de fameuze Tractebel-smeergeldaffaire. Die draaide rond pogingen van het bedrijf Tractebel om een concessie te verkrijgen voor een gaspijpleiding in Kazachstan. Chodiev zou zijn commissies gebruikt hebben als smeergeld voor politici om de deal te beklinken.
Kazachgate was wellicht het belangrijkste dossier waar Nicolas Ullens als inspecteur bij de staatsveiligheid tegenaan liep.

Kazachgate draait rond het versneld wetgevend werk (de afkoopwet) op maat van Chodiev en op vraag van toenmalig Frans president Sarkozy. Frankrijk wilde in 2010 een belangrijke exportdeal beklinken met de Kazachse dictator Nazarbajev. Die eiste in ruil dat de strafklacht tegen zijn vriend en medestander Patokh Chodiev (en bij uitbreiding het Kazachse trio) in België zou vervallen. De afkoopwet was het vehikel dat daarvoor moest dienen.
Hoe komt Didier Reynders daarbij in beeld?
De entourage van Sarkozy ging voor de operatie op zoek naar medestanders binnen de MR waar Didier Reynders op dat moment nog oppermachtig was. De advocate van Chodiev maakte (onder meer) ruim 700.000 euro over aan voormalig Kamervoorzitter en MR-minister (wijlen) Armand De Decker en eveneens forse bedragen aan Étienne des Rosaies, een naaste medewerker van Nicolas Sarkozy.
In een vertrouwelijke nota schreef Des Rosaies onder meer dat hij zich via Armand De Decker verzekerd had van de unanieme steun van MR voor de afkoopwet en van de bevoegde ministers, waaronder Didier Reynders. Étienne des Rosaies had ook meermaals contact met Reynders’ rechterhand Jean-Claude Fontinoy.
Ondanks een rits zeer concrete aanwijzingen en harde documenten besliste de parlementaire onderzoekscommissie-Kazachgate, meerderheid tegen oppositie, dat er geen ongeoorloofde beïnvloeding van de wetgeving was geweest. Reynders en Fontinoy konden opnieuw gerust adem halen.
Maar ook ander onderzoek binnen de Belgische Staatsveiligheid werd afgeblokt?
Het eerste dossier waar Nicolas Ullens binnen de afdeling economische contraspionage mee te maken kreeg, was het dossier over de verkoop en de verhuur van het Rijksadministratief Centrum in Brussel (RAC). Het reusachtige gebouw aan de Brusselse Pachecolaan, in de schaduw van de Financietoren, was lang eigendom van de overheid.
De constructie die werd uitgewerkt voor de verkoop en verhuur maakte de Belgische schatkist vele tientallen miljoenen lichter, terwijl vastgoedontwikkelaar Breevast drie keer langs de kassa passeerde: de overheid verkocht het RAC voor veel te weinig geld, betaalde vervolgens een te hoge huur en liet enkele jaren later de federale politie het RAC voor 18 jaar huren, opnieuw tegen een veel te hoge huurprijs.
Nota’s van de staatsveiligheid die Apache kon inkijken, tonen hoe verschillende bronnen vele jaren terug al waarschuwden voor een systeem van verregaande corruptie dat in de steigers werd gezet door de omstreden vastgoedlobbyist (wijlen) Koen Blijweert en Jean-Claude Fontinoy, rechterhand van Didier Reynders.
