Ook dat dossier werd volgens Nicolas Ullens afgeblokt door Didier Reynders. Finaal werd Ullens overgeplaatst naar de afdeling salafisme. Maar ook daar botste hij op dossiers waarin Didier Reynders een hoofdrol speelde. Het belangrijkste daarvan is het dossier van de bevroren Libische tegoeden.
Vele jaren terug al waarschuwden bronnen voor een systeem van verregaande corruptie dat werd opgezet door vastgoedlobbyist Koen Blijweert en Fontinoy
Welke rol speelde Reynders daarbij?
In maart 2011, na de val van Kadhafi, werd op vraag van de VN-Veiligheidsraad 12,8 miljard euro, afkomstig uit Libië, bevroren op rekeningen bij Euroclear Bank in Brussel. Jaarlijks verdween 300 miljoen euro aan interesten op dat bedrag naar Libië.
Via een informant kreeg Nicolas Ullens te horen dat Didier Reynders kamp koos in de strijd tussen de twee rivaliserende Libische clans en Libische tegoeden zou overmaken in ruil voor smeergeld. Grote bedragen zouden via tussenpersoon Robert Claushuis richting Reynders en Fontinoy zijn gestroomd.
De zaak kwam aan het licht in de nasleep van het faillissement van GSDT, een vzw van prins Laurent. De vzw zou een deel van de Libische kust herbebossen, maar de Libische staat zegde het contract eenzijdig op. De rechter oordeelde dat Libië de prins 50 miljoen euro verschuldigd is, maar de prins had de grootste moeilijkheden om dat geld los te krijgen.
Zijn vzw ging intussen in vereffening en Reynders weigerde de interesten op de tegoeden te gebruiken om de prins te compenseren. Verschillende mensen boden vervolgens hun diensten aan prins Laurent aan om het bedrag in Libië los te peuteren, in ruil voor een zeer forse commissie. Een van hen was Robert Claushuis.
Voor Ullens was het verbod van zijn chef om verder te werken op het dossier de druppel. Overal waar hij op Reynders en Fontinoy botste, werd hem het werken onmogelijk gemaakt. Hij nam ontslag bij de Belgische staatsveiligheid en stapte naar het gerecht. Zoals hierboven vermeld: de onderzoeken werden geseponeerd aan de vooravond van de benoeming van Didier Reynders tot Europees Commissaris.
Naast het Libische dossier bevatten de gelekte whatsappberichten ook aanwijzingen over linken tussen Didier Reynders en Rusland?
Er zijn verschillende dossiers die aanwijzingen bevatten over relaties tussen Reynders en Rusland. Zo is er het dossier over de illustere edelman, baron Ernest de Laminne de Bex.
In zijn middeleeuwse kasteel in Wezembeek-Oppem herbergde hij tot voor kort de diplomatieke club Cercle International Diplomatique et Consulaire (CIDIC), een pleisterplaats voor edellieden, ambassadeurs, ereconsuls, bedrijfsleiders, politici, magistraten, advocaten, officieren van het leger, verantwoordelijken van inlichtingendiensten en vertegenwoordigers van het hof.
Jarenlang bracht De Laminne de Bex in zijn kasteel diplomaten en spionnen uit het Oosten samen met hun westerse counterparts, onder het genot van een goed glas wijn.
Er zijn verschillende dossiers die aanwijzingen bevatten over relaties tussen Reynders en Rusland
Apache documenteerde, samen met Humo, de schimmige relaties en duistere activiteiten van De Laminne de Bex in Georgië en Kazachstan, zijn schijnbaar uit het niets opgebouwde vastgoedimperium en de verhalen over wapenhandel en deviezensmokkel.
Hoewel De Laminne de Bex op de radar van de inlichtingendiensten stond en Russisch geld doorsluisde naar de Franstalige extreemrechtse populistische partij Parti Populaire, kreeg hij van Didier Reynders een adellijke titel en werd hij tot twee keer toe erkend als ereconsul in België.
En Ernest de Laminne de Bex appte met Didier Reynders?
Op 5 januari 2020 maakt de Laminne de Bex niet enkel zijn beste wensen over en wenste hij Didier Reynders alle succes als Europees Commissaris, hij meldde hem ook dat hij graag eens persoonlijk met hem zou praten over de aantijgingen van Nicolas Ullens en over “een tegenoffensief om een einde te maken aan de laster”. Opvallend daarbij: De Laminne de Bex ‘tutoyeert’ Didier Reynders in het bericht – “j’aimerais bien t’entretenir de vive voix” - wat getuigt van een nauwe relatie tussen beiden.
Baron-spion de Laminne de Bex wilde Reynders graag persoonlijk spreken over de aantijgingen van Nicolas Ullens en over 'een tegenoffensief om een einde te maken aan de laster'
Reynders stond ook dicht bij de Russische oligarch Oleg Deripaska?
Begin september 2025 heropende het Brussels parket een geseponeerd onderzoek naar witwas waarin de Russische superoligarch Oleg Deripaska centraal staat. Dat gebeurde nadat Apache een reactie vroeg aan het Brussels parket, na een uitgebreid onderzoek over twee stichtingen van Deripaska in Ukkel en de directe relatie met Didier Reynders.
Heropende?
In 2014 tekende de antiwitwascel in haar jaarverslag tot in de kleinste details een witwasschema uit rond een Ukkelse kunststichting. De naam werd niet genoemd maar het ging om de vzw Bruno Lussato et Marina Fédier. Deripaska, een nauwe medestander van de Russische president Vladimir Poetin, had de stichting opgericht en Didier Reynders behoorde tot de nauwe vriendenkring. De antiwitwascel vermeldde toen al “nauwe banden tussen de betrokkenen en politiek prominente personen in Rusland en België”.
Didier Reynders was niet enkel kind aan huis in de kuststichting, zijn voormalige adviseur Constantin Chariot was directeur van het museum van de stichting. Hij had een volmacht op de rekening van de vzw. Het gerechtelijk onderzoek dat daarop volgde stond Deripaska’s aanvraag voor een “gouden paspoort” in Cyprus in de weg. Zo’n paspoort moest de Russische oligarch vrije doorgang binnen de Europese Unie verzekeren.
Ondanks subtiele bedreigingen vanuit de entourage van Deripaska aan het adres van de antiwitwascel werd het dossier snel geseponeerd. Didier Reynders was op dat moment als minister bevoegd voor Buitenlandse Zaken, Buitenlandse Handel en Europese Zaken.
Apache en Humo stelden vast dat de voorbije jaren vanuit de centrale vzw 878.000 euro werd versluisd naar een andere Brusselse vzw. Die werd opgericht en bestuurd door personen die nauw verweven zijn met Russische desinformatiecampagnes of betrokken zijn bij grootschalige financiële operaties die duidelijk het stempel van het Kremlin dragen.
Didier Reynders was kind aan huis bij een museum van een stichting van Oleg Deripaska. De antiwitwascel vermeldde toen al 'nauwe banden tussen de betrokkenen en politiek prominente personen in Rusland en België'
Kunst en antiek lijken een belangrijke rol te spelen in de zaak-Reynders.
Constantin Chariot werd indertijd naar eigen zeggen enkel als getuige verhoord in het onderzoek naar de vzw van Oleg Deripaska, maar antiquair Olivier Theunissen bij wie Jean-Claude Fontinoy om de haverklap antiek aankocht, werd intussen wel in verdenking gesteld. Nicolas Ullens omschreef de techniek om wit te wassen via de aankoop van antiek als de methode-Guéant, genoemd naar de voormalige rechterhand van de Franse ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy die ook prima contacten onderhield met Didier Reynders.
De methode-Guéant komt erop neer dat antiek of kunst wordt aangekocht aan een lage prijs en vervolgens voor een zeer hoge prijs wordt doorverkocht. Die meerprijs is de facto het smeergeld om dingen gedaan te krijgen. Theunissen wordt door Nicolas Ullens expliciet genoemd als verbindingsofficier tussen Didier Reynders enerzijds en Nicolas Sakozy en Claude Guéant anderzijds.
Zijn er andere technieken die Reynders of Fontinoy zouden hebben gebruikt?
Omdat Reynders decennialang een zogezegde PEP (Politically Exposed Person) was waarvan de financiën in principe extra in het oog worden gehouden, zou Reynders al die tijd via Jean-Claude Fontinoy hebben gewerkt.
Een tweede manier van witwassen loopt via vastgoed. Jean-Claude Fontinoy vergaarde de voorbije decennia een zestigtal, vaak zeer dure en indrukwekkende woningen in de buurt van Namen. Daarbij zouden geregeld betalingen, deels in cash zijn gebeurd.
Nicolas Ullens beschrijft onder meer hoe Fontinoy in 2019 een cocktailfeestje hield voor de vzw Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie, met vooral antiquairs onder de genodigden, ter gelegenheid van de viering van het zestigste pand dat hij in zijn bezit had gekregen.
Welke rol speelde die vzw Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie?
Eind 2019 bracht Apache uit dat de vzw rond Fontinoy voor minstens 75.000 euro sponsorgeld had ontvangen van bedrijven die in principe niets te maken hebben met een vzw die zich, zoals de naam zegt, bezighoudt met de opsmuk van de mooiste dorpjes in Wallonië. Het ging onder meer om baggerbedrijf DEME, havenbedrijf Rent-A-Port en projectontwikkelaar Immobel. DEME en Rent-a-port zijn in handen van de Belgische holding Ackermans & van Haaren.
De Paradise Papers leerden onder meer dat de Belgische overheid via investeringsvehikel BMI participeerde in de vennootschap Infra Asia Development Limited, met zetel op de Britse Maagdeneilanden, een notoir belastingparadijs. Via dat vehikel werd een grootschalig havenproject in Noord-Vietnam uitgebouwd. BMI participeerde in de vennootschap op de Britse Maagdeneilanden, samen met Rent-A-Port. De voorzitter van de raad van bestuur van BMI was Jean-Claude Fontinoy.
Een vzw rond Fontinoy die zich bezighoudt met de opsmuk van de mooiste dorpjes in Wallonië.ontving voor minstens 75.000 euro sponsorgeld van bedrijven die daar niets mee te maken hebben
Waarom zou projectontwikkelaar Immobel een toeristische vzw sponsoren?
Twee vennootschappen gelieerd aan de beursgenoteerde projectontwikkelaar stortten elk 1.000 euro op de rekening van de Waalse vzw. Het gaat om Allfin Group en Immobel Group Lotinvest. Het eerder genoemde RAC werd door de Belgische overheid verkocht aan projectontwikkelaar Breevast en Immobel.
In een nota van de staatsveiligheid stond over die aankoop dit: “Bij de Regie der Gebouwen is de man die beslist overduidelijk Jean-Claude Fontinoy, maar zijn inschatting is niet bepaald rationeel: hij koppelt zijn akkoord aan een geheime betaling van een miljoen euro.”
Over het onderzoek dat het parket van Namen startte naar Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie werd niets meer vernomen.
Fontinoy wordt ook genoemd in een soort spin-off van een grootschalig onderzoek naar mogelijke fraude bij de verkoop van Europese overheidsgebouwen
Niet enkel Immobel, ook andere projectontwikkelaars vonden hun weg naar de vzw Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie?
Apache bracht onder meer een getuigenis over drie betalingen van ongeveer 25.000 euro aan de vzw door een projectontwikkelaar. Die moest voor een vastgoedproject enkele vierkante meters terrein van de NMBS – waar Jean-Claude Fontinoy op een cruciale positie zat – overkopen.
Recent werd duidelijk dat de speurders ook een onderzoek voeren naar een andere vzw waar Fontinoy bij betrokken was?
Het gaat om een onderzoek in de schoot van de investeringsmaatschappij van de federale overheid (SFPIM). Jean-Claude Fontinoy was jarenlang voorzitter van dochteronderneming SFPIM International. Er zijn wel wat parallellen met wat er gebeurde binnen de vzw Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie.
De vzw Les Amphitryons, die zich officieel bezighoudt met gastronomie en de kunst van het sigarenroken, ontving stortingen van SFPIM International. De voorzitter van de vzw was ook adviseur van Fontinoy binnen SFPIM International. Volgens de speurders dienden de stortingen als vergoeding van prestaties “voor de voorbereiding van een dossier rond financieringsaanvragen aan de SFPIM door de adviseur van de voorzitter”.
Apache bracht onder meer een getuigenis over forse betalingen door een projectontwikkelaar aan een vzw rond Fontinoy
Het onderzoek is een soort spin-off van een grootschalig onderzoek naar mogelijke fraude bij de verkoop van 23 gebouwen van de Europese Unie aan de Belgische investeringsmaatschappij SFPIM voor in totaal 900 miljoen euro.
Is vastgoed finaal de rode draad in de zaak-Reynders?
Het is zeker niet het enige element, maar wel een belangrijk. Met Fontinoy had Didier Reynders zijn mannetje binnen zowel de NMBS als de Regie der Gebouwen. Met de verkoop van overheidspatrimonium en publieke gronden werden de voorbije decennia in België sloten geld verdiend.
Het kransje ‘Vrienden van het Vastgoed’ dat daarbij telkens weer in beeld komt of kwam, is bekend. Ze dineerden in chique restaurants, en frequenteerden elkaar in de luxueuze villa van wijlen Koen Blijweert in Megève om deals te maken en zaken te bespreken die het daglicht schuwen. Belangrijk daarbij is dat het netwerk telkens opnieuw tracht om zowat alle (traditionele) politieke partijen mee in bad te trekken. De voorbije twee decennia expliciet ook de relatief nieuwe partij N-VA.
Het volstaat om te herlezen hoe die partij haar hoofdkantoor in Brussel verkreeg om zicht te krijgen op de manier van werken. Ook het fameuze etentje in ’t Fornuis op uitnodiging van vastgoedlobbyist Erik Van der Paal – waar naast het bijna integrale toenmalige Antwerpse college een aanzienlijk deel van het netwerk te gast was – maakt duidelijk hoe het werkt. Het is allerminst toevallig dat naast Jean-Claude Fontinoy ook zijn (toenmalige) “socialistische” tegenhanger Luc Joris aanwezig was.
De man waarvan recent geheime opnames uitlekten waarin hij zelf spreekt over de betaling van smeergeld?
Luc Joris stond jarenlang heel dicht bij Elio Di Rupo en de PS. Bij de afwikkeling van de overname van de omstreden projectontwikkelaar Land Invest Group en bij concrete projecten van de groep zou smeergeld zijn betaald, of beter: beloofd smeergeld niet zijn betaald. Land Invest Group was een samenwerking tussen de directe entourage van Bart De Wever en de Luikse PS.
Het dossier illustreert perfect hoe verschillende politieke partijen – ook al zijn ze ideologisch elkaars gezworen vijanden – voor elkaar zwijgen. Die aanpak leidde er indertijd zelfs toe dat N-VA samen met de PS stemde tegen het opheffen van de parlementaire onschendbaarheid van de gevallen Luikse PS-coryfee Alain Mathot.
Die “Belgische methode” maakt dat Didier Reynders anderen in zijn val dreigt mee te slepen, mochten werkelijk alle stinkende zaakjes waarin de naam van Didier Reynders of die van Jean-Claude Fontinoy valt tot op het bot worden uitgespit.
Een dossier zoals Land Invest Group toont hoe verschillende politieke partijen – ook al zijn ze ideologisch elkaars gezworen vijanden – voor elkaar zwijgen
Zijn er dan nog veel andere zaken?
In het boek De clan Reynders lijst de Franstalige onderzoeksjournalist Philippe Engels de schimmige dossiers rond Reynders en Fontinoy grotendeels op. Hij beschrijft daarin onder meer ook hoe Jean-Claude Fontinoy personeel (en geld) van de NMBS zou hebben gebruikt om verkiezingscampagnes van Didier Reynders te ondersteunen.
Ook de rol van Fontinoy bij de investeringen (en de gigantische meerkost) bij de bouw van het NMBS-station Luik-Guillemins wordt uitgebreid belicht. Net als de relatie tussen Fontinoy en Albert Karaziwan, de baas van de Semlex Group die voor honderden miljoenen euro paspoorten en andere identiteitsdocumenten leverde aan verschillende Afrikaanse landen.
Een ander bijzonder gevoelig dossier is dat van de bouw van de Belgische ambassade in Kinshassa door bouwgroep Willemen. Het is een van de dossiers die Nicolas Ullens al in 2019 noemde waarbij Didier Reynders smeergeld zou hebben ontvangen. Net zoals in andere zaken was er sprake van een juridisch vooronderzoek, maar dat leverde niets op.
Jarenlang leken alle affaires van ‘Teflon Didier’ af te glijden, maar zijn in verdenkingstelling maakt ontsnappen deze keer een stuk minder evident
Liggen de kaarten nu anders?
Jarenlang leken alle affaires van ‘Teflon Didier’ af te glijden maar zijn in verdenkingstelling, net als die van Jean-Claude Fontinoy en antiquair Olivier Theunissen, maakt ontsnappen deze keer een stuk minder evident. Ongetwijfeld heeft Reynders nog steeds medestanders, ook binnen het politionele en justitiële apparaat.
Ook de voornoemde “Belgische aanpak” waarbij andere partijen mee in bad worden getrokken, zet gigantisch veel druk op het dossier.
Daar staat tegenover dat de talrijke onthullingen en bewijzen die bovendrijven in verschillende media het bijzonder moeilijk zullen maken om het deksel helemaal op de pot te houden.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-i.title: The candidates who will decide the US midterm elections
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-i.author: Rachel Leingang
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-i.text:
Abdul El-Sayed
Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan
Abdul El-Sayed, a former public health official on the left of the Democratic party, beat a moderate member of Congress to win the party’s nomination for US Senate in Michigan, in a race clouded by tens of millions in outside spending. He is facing Republican former congressman Mike Rogers in one of the country’s most-watched races. Michigan is a swing state: while the Senate seat they are fighting for has been held by a Democrat for 12 years, the state narrowly backed Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election. El-Sayed’s brand of tough talk and the simplicity of his campaign slogan (money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for All) have made him a progressive star – and a frequent punching bag on the right, where prominent figures led by the president have leaned into Islamophobia to criticize him.
Susan Collins
Republican US Senator from Maine
Susan Collins isn’t new to the US Senate. She has been serving since 1997, and is now seeking a sixth term. A moderate Republican, she is a dying breed in the current Maga-tinged Washington during Trump’s second presidency. Maine is a battleground state: Kamala Harris won the state by a clear margin over Trump in 2024. Now Collins, 73, is trying to hang on to her seat in a race that Democrats have targeted as a key to winning back control of the Senate. She initially faced Graham Platner, a Democrat who dropped out of the race after facing rape allegations. Now, Troy Jackson – a former logger who served in the state legislature – is trying to topple the longtime senator.
Adam Hamilton
Democratic nominee for US Senate in Kansas
Kansas’ US Senate election wasn’t on the national radar as competitive at the start of the year. Why would it be? Kansans have not sent a Democrat to the US Senate since 1932. But Adam Hamilton, a megachurch pastor, won a crowded primary and has made the race one to watch this year. While Kansas typically leans right, voters in the state have shown frustration with Republican senator Roger Marshall over inaccessibility and his alignment with Trump, as they struggling to afford fuel and groceries, and grapple with sustained economic instability. Plus, Marshall, who practiced medicine for 25 years, was revealed to have sued hundreds of his patients for unpaid bills, resulting in the arrests of dozens of them. Enter Hamilton, who frequently calls for bipartisan politics that put Kansans first, even if that means standing up to Trump.
Jon Ossoff
Democratic US senator from Georgia
Ossoff, the youngest US senator at 39, is seeking a second term in what should have been a tight race in Georgia, the southern swing state. Polls are suggesting it will not be a close-run thing. The Democrat’s political glow-up and savvy speaking skills, captured in video clips meant to grab voter attention online, have made his reelection seem all but inevitable – and given rise to near-constant murmurs that he’ll run for president in 2028, with regular comparisons to Barack Obama, in tone and in youthfulness. The pair rallied together in Georgia last week. He has accused his opponent, Mike Collins, a Republican congressman, of being aligned with white supremacists – which Collins has vehemently denied.
James Talarico
Democratic nominee for US Senate in Texas
Could Texas finally flip – and could it be a theological Democrat – who does it? James Talarico, a 37-year-old state lawmaker, has been generating buzz – and raising record-breaking sums – in his run for the US Senate. Having fended off the firebrand Democratic congresswoman Jasmine Crockett in the Democratic primary, he now faces the state’s beleaguered Republican attorney general, Ken Paxton, in the general election. With Trump’s backing, Paxton beat incumbent US senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary. The nomination of Paxton – who has faced a host of fraud and misconduct scandals during his time in office – has prompted Republicans to drop tens of millions of dollars to defend a seat they typically win with a clear margin. Talarico, dubbed “Talafreako” by Trump and his allies, has sought to win over independents and Republicans in the red state by appealing to their faith and speaking against corruption in politics.
Max Miller
Republican representative in Ohio
Ohio’s seventh congressional district wouldn’t ordinarily be competitive; Trump won the district by 11 points in 2024. But damaging allegations surrounding Max Miller, the embattled Republican incumbent, have given Democrats hope that they might flip the red seat. The 37-year-old Republican, who worked on Trump’s first presidential campaign, was elected to the seat in 2022. His ex-wife, Emily Moreno, who is the daughter of Republican US senator Bernie Moreno, has alleged Miller physically abused her and their daughter, which he denied. Another of Miller’s ex-partners, former Trump press secretary Stephanie Grisham, has also accused Miller of physical abuse. He denied that allegation, too. The claims have featured heavily in ads against Miller in the district. Brian Poindexter, the Democratic challenger, is a union ironworker focused on addressing the cost of living.
Mary Peltola
Democratic nominee for US Senate in Alaska
Mary Peltola is one of the few prominent Democrats who were deemed to pose a potential threat to incumbent Republican Dan S Sullivan. She entered the race hoping to capitalize on Alaska’s recent independent streak and broad anti-Trump feelings. But in the final stretch, she faced allegations of mistreating staff by using slurs and shoving one aide – which her campaign downplayed, attributing Peltola’s behavior to stress. Her campaign also faced accusations of ballot stacking by recruiting another candidate named Dan J Sullivan to run in the state’s open primary. The New York Times reported that Peltola’s staff worked with the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee to add another Dan Sullivan to the ballot, thereby drawing votes away from the Republican senator. Peltola has said she knew nothing of the plan. Her campaign also denied recruiting candidates into the race.
Angie Nixon
Democratic nominee for US Senate in Florida
Marco Rubio’s elevation from the Senate to Trump’s secretary of state in 2025 left an open seat in Florida, which was filled by Republican Ashley Moody. Now, in the race for a full term, Moody faces Angie Nixon – a progressive and democratic socialist – who staged a surprise victory in the Democratic primary. While the Florida race isn’t seen as super competitive, or a likely win for Democrats, the small business owner and state lawmaker has grabbed attention and seen prominent figures on the left, including congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Bernie Sanders, campaigning for her. Progressives hope that Nixon can make the case that their candidates – and not just moderates – can have broad appeal in red states like Florida. Moody was the state’s attorney general before her appointment to the US Senate.
Darline Graham
Republican US senator in South Carolina
Darline Graham had minimal involvement in politics and had never run for or held public office until this year, when she was appointed to the US Senate seat in South Carolina after her brother’s death. Lindsey Graham served the state in Washington, first in the House and then in the Senate, for decades. She decided – after encouragement from Trump – to seek a full term, and won the Republican primary. But Darline Graham’s inexperience, both in office and with policy itself, has come into sharp focus. Voter frustration with political dynasties have also made the race in this typically red state a toss-up, according to polls. Dr Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, is running against Graham after previously making a run for the US House of Representatives in 2022.
Juan Ciscomani
Republican US representative in Arizona
Juan Ciscomani, a 44-year-old Latino Republican congressman and former gubernatorial adviser, has faced close races for his US House seat in each election, narrowly beating out his Democrat opponent in 2022 and 2024 in the toss-up sixth congressional district in southern Arizona. Ciscomani, who was born in Sonora, Mexico and raised in Tucson, has sought to distance himself from Trump. His reelection campaign is a test of whether Latinos – some of whom swung toward Trump in 2024 and helped deliver his second term – will stick with the president, or side with Democrats, especially after Trump’s aggressive deportation scheme. JoAnna Mendoza, a US Marine Corps veteran and the Democratic challenger, has emphasized her local roots and called out Ciscomani for largely voting with Trump’s agenda.
Rebecca Bennett
Democratic nominee for US House in New Jersey
Rebecca Bennett’s odds of winning this toss-up seat increased when her opponent, the incumbent Republican Tom Kean Jr, disappeared for months from his public office. Kean, 58, was gone for more than three months from his job representing the seventh congressional district. He and his office declined to explain why until he returned, when he told people he had been hospitalized for depression. Before his prolonged absence, Bennett had flown under the radar. As New York Magazine put it: “Tom Kean Jr. needed to vanish to become interesting.” Bennett, a 39-year-old moderate Democrat and former navy helicopter pilot and aircraft commander, hopes to win over voters who are frustrated with Kean’s absence and Trump’s agenda. The district is known for split-ticket voting, whereby voters back candidates from different parties when electing figures to multiple offices in the same election. Bennett, a mother of two, has talked about how affordability concerns affect her household as well, including the cost of childcare.

https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/12ai-came.title: Cameroon: ghost workers in the AI machine
https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/12ai-came.author: Inès Marie Nga
https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/12ai-came.text:
‘There’s no contract, no guarantees. You never know in advance how much you’ll earn’
Cameroon: ghost workers in the AI machine
African states want to develop AI attuned to local needs and cultures. But for educated young Africans, the reality of the AI revolution looks more like poorly paid, precarious work for Western firms.
Boris L was working late into the evening in the gloom of a cramped, dusty Internet café in the Ngoa Ékélé district of Cameroon’s capital, his face bathed in the blue glow from a second-hand screen. Outside, Yaoundé’s university district had been plunged into darkness by yet another of the power cuts for which Cameroon’s electricity company, Socadel, is notorious. But here, an old generator rumbled away in the back room and the Internet connection held up. For the past few months, Boris had spent most of his evenings at the café, one of thousands of invisible ‘microworkers’ in Africa who, for a pittance, help keep the wheels of the global AI industry turning.
Boris performed one microtask after another on Remotasks, a platform run by Scale AI, a US company based in San Francisco and valued at $29bn in 2025. These involved locating, outlining and identifying objects in images to train AI systems to recognise them. Pictures of everyday life in the US and Europe scrolled across his screen. He identified pedestrians, cars and road signs, earning a few cents per task. ‘After four hours, I might have made the equivalent of 500 CFA francs,’ he said – less than $1.
Like all the micro-workers I interviewed, Boris asked for his name to be changed, not because he is ashamed of doing work beneath his level of education, but out of fear of losing this meagre but valuable source of income in a country where 65% of the working population experiences some form of underemployment. Thousands of kilometres away, the data he annotates helps train the algorithms for self-driving cars and computer vision models in the global North.
Officialdom, however, pays scant attention to these precarious working conditions. In July 2025 Cameroon’s minister of posts and telecommunications, Minette Libom Li Likeng, officially launched the country’s national AI strategy: its stated ambition is to make Cameroon Africa’s leading hub for this technology by 2040. Inès Marie Nga is a journalism student at the Advanced School of Mass Communication (ESSTIC) in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: PEC da Segurança Pública vai testar capacidade de coalizão do governo Lula, afirma cientista político
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: José Bernardes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Nesta terça-feira (3), o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), deve colocar a PEC da Segurança Pública para ser votada. A pauta é importante para seu proponente, o governo Lula, pois estabelece penas mais duras e regimes de prisão mais restritos para chefes de facções e milícias e cria um novo pacto federativo entre União, estados e municípios para o enfrentamento ao crime no Brasil.
Em entrevista ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, o cientista político Mateus de Albuquerque, professor da Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF), observa que o debate é central também para as articulações que o Executivo conseguirá travar para garantir a governabilidade a partir do próximo ano, diante de um Congresso hostil.
“Vai ser um dos primeiros testes de fogo da capacidade de coalizão do novo governo. Apesar de falarmos que o PL fez uma grande bancada, o modelo de presidencialismo de coalizão permite que o governo isole o PL”, aponta. “O PL passou a ser uma ameaça para o Centrão, que está se articulando para minar o poder do PL”, reforça.
O analista, no entanto, lembra que a PEC da Segurança Pública obriga o governo a realizar um outro cálculo, que é a relação com os governos estaduais. “Governadores usam muitas vezes a segurança pública como ferramenta eleitoral, destinando esse ou aquele investimento às polícias. Com a PEC, eles vão perder parte dessa moeda eleitoral”, argumenta.
Para Albuquerque, no governo Lula 3 houve distribuição de cargos, em especial ministérios considerados estratégicos, que, no entanto, não garantiram vida fácil para o Executivo. Ainda assim, reforça o especialista, o governo conseguiu emplacar pautas importantes.
“O governo conseguiu seus principais objetivos: a isenção do imposto de renda para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil e, mais recentemente, o fim da escala 6×1. Mesmo com a infidelidade das bancadas, houve sucesso na articulação com o Congresso”, pontua.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: Californian Michelin-starred restaurant serves up book on the art of hospitality and farming
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: The Art Newspaper
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
Kaiseki is a type of Japanese dining offering up multiple courses that together form one long and delicious experience. This is precisely what is on offer at SingleThread, a three-star Michelin restaurant in California’s Sonoma Wine Country, so it’s perhaps no surprise that its proprietors, Kyle and Katina Connaughton, describe themselves as storytellers. But SingleThread is also a 24-acre farm, and a five-room inn, and works closely with nearby ranchers who rear the meat it uses. It’s a multi-volume affair.
Now, all its wisdom, history, instructions for ikebana flower arranging, planting diagrams for the kitchen garden, and a number of recipes are gathered together in one book. As with its restaurant ethos, it’s a publication that assumes you have a great deal of time and inclination to spare: there’s an entire section on the negi onion.
On the other hand, if you’re unlikely to visit Sonoma any time soon, or don’t fancy joining a months-long waiting list, this book is a treat. The photography is stunning and, unlike a ten-course meal—which, however delightful, can feel like being held hostage and will cost a bare minimum of £500—you can dip in and out at leisure in the comfort of your own home.
• SingleThread, DK Alpha, £50 (hb)

https://taz.de/Roman-von-Milada-Souckova.title: Roman von Milada Součková: Der Ausweg aus dem poetischen Labyrinth
https://taz.de/Roman-von-Milada-Souckova.author: Claudia Lenssen
https://taz.de/Roman-von-Milada-Souckova.text:
Roman von Milada Součková: Der Ausweg aus dem poetischen Labyrinth
Der neugegründete Verlag dimidium mundi verlegt fast vergessene Schriftstellerinnen neu. Nun erscheint der Coming-of-Age-Roman einer Prager Avantgardistin.
Schriftstellerinnen schreiben meist biografisch-psychologisch, Schriftsteller konfrontieren die Welt dagegen gern mit ihrer literarischen Experimentierlust, zumindest wenn sie sich auf dem Weg zum männlichen Genie fühlen. So weit das immer noch gültige Klischee, das allerdings seit Jahrhunderten von vielen Frauen kreativ unterlaufen wird. Wir kennen sie nur nicht, weil sie vergessen und aus dem Kanon verdrängt sind.
Nicht erst Virginia Woolf, Gertrude Stein und Ingeborg Bachmann haben mit Erzählperspektiven, Zeitsprüngen und Mischformen jongliert, um ihre Skepsis gegenüber dem falschen Versprechen auszudrücken, realistische Romane würden die Welt, wie sie ist, eins zu eins abbilden.
Obwohl jedoch immer wieder vergessene Schriftstellerinnen neu aufgelegt werden und sich beispielsweise der Aviva Verlag konsequent um die Wiederentdeckung vor allem von jüdischen Autorinnen vor dem Kahlschlag durch das Naziregime verdient macht, braucht es auch heute Initiativen wie www.lueckenliste.de, auf der Interessierte aus dem Literaturbetrieb und der Wissenschaft ihre Hinweise auf vergessene Schriftsteller_innen teilen. Ziel ist nicht weniger als die Sichtbarkeit der Hälfte der (literarischen) Welt.
Der Roman
Milada Součková: „Amor und Psyche“. Aus dem Tschechischen von Doris Kouba. dimidium mundi, München 2026, 320 Seiten, 26 Euro
dimidium mundi, ein von Zarifa Mamedova in diesem Jahr in München neu gegründeter Verlag, zeigt mit seinem aus dem Lateinischen entlehnten Namen an, dass er sich genau diesem Ziel verpflichtet fühlt, die Hälfte des literarischen Kanons für Autorinnen der Weltkultur zu erobern.
Kam im Frühjahr als Debüt der Roman „Die Lust am Manne“ (1928) der österreichisch-ungarischen Schauspielerin, Autorin und Filmregisseurin Olga Wohlbrück heraus, folgt mit „Amor und Psyche“ (1937) nun ein früher Roman der hierzulande (bis auf die 1998 und 2010 edierten Romane „Der unbekannte Mensch“ und „Bel Canto“) viel zu wenig bekannten tschechischen Schriftstellerin Milada Součková.
Avantgardistische Künstlerzirkel
Geboren 1898 in Prag als Tochter eines Bauunternehmers, besuchte Milada Součková das Prager Minerva-Gymnasium, das erste Mädchengymnasium Österreich-Ungarns, dessen pädagogisches Programm auf die freie Entfaltung und Emanzipation der Schülerinnen – darunter die Journalistin und zeitweise Kafka-Gefährtin Milena Jesenská – ausgerichtet war.
Ihr naturwissenschaftliches Studium in Prag und Lausanne schloss Milada Součková 1923 mit einer Doktorarbeit über „Das Seelenleben der Pflanzen“ ab. In der lebendigen Prager Kulturszene der seit dem Ende des Ersten Weltkriegs gegründeten ersten tschechoslowakischen Republik schloss sich Milada Součková den avantgardistischen Künstlerzirkeln der Stadt an, heiratete den Maler Zdenek Rykr und veröffentlichte Gedichte, Reiseberichte über Südeuropa und die zunehmenden politischen Bedrohungen der Epoche in literarischen Zeitschriften.
Als Mitglied der Gruppe 42, einer tschechischen Künstlergruppe, die bis zu ihrem Verbot durch das kommunistische Regime 1948 bestand, teilte Milada Součková das Misstrauen der Avantgarde gegenüber den konventionellen Formen des realistischen Romans. Inspiriert von Marcel Prousts monumentaler Erinnerungsarbeit über die goldene Ära des Bürgertums bis 1914 und angeregt durch André Gides Roman „Die Falschmünzer“ (1925), einer Geschichte schwuler Jugenderfahrungen in wechselnden Erzählperspektiven, begann die Schriftstellerin, sich mit dem Lebensgefühl ihrer politisch wachen Generation auseinanderzusetzen. Die überkommenen literarischen Mittel erklärte sie für nutzlose Fossile, untauglich, um den Wirbel ihrer in Fragmente zerfallenden Erfahrungswelt zu beschreiben.
Herausfordernde Coming-of-Age-Geschichte
„Amor und Psyche“ ist eine fein gesponnene, in Teilen herausfordernde Coming-of-Age-Geschichte im Umfeld junger Frauen aus dem Prager Bürgertum – weder konkret autobiografisch grundiert noch psychologisch als oberflächliches Angebot zur Identifikation erzählt. Das Mädchen Augustina und die Erzählerin verstricken sich in ein amüsiertes, vom Ringen um Nähe und Distanz bestimmtes Spiel um Augustas Tagebuch, das von ihrer Liebe zu der von beiden angebeteten Lehrerin Alsbětă handelt.
Im zweiten Teil des Romans spiegeln sich die Wünsche und Träume der Mädchen aus anderer Perspektive im Tagebuch der Erzählerin. Der dritte Teil, ein poetisches Labyrinth der Erlebnisse beider Mädchen und weiterer Figuren aus ihrem Kosmos, treibt die Fiktion auf die Spitze, sodass das Spiel der Tagebuchfragmente wie eine Parodie auf das Genre wirkt, komödiantischer als beispielsweise in dem ikonischen queeren Film „Mädchen in Uniform“.
Eine Göttin am literarischen Horizont, wie es Psyche, die Braut des Gottes Amor in Apuleios' berühmter Novelle aus dem 2. Jahrhundert, wird, scheint Augusta nicht zu werden – oder doch? Das göttlich-ingeniöse Selbstbild des literarischen Schreibens und seiner Spitzenvertreter ist in Milada Součkovás Augen in Zeiten grundstürzender Disruptionen in Zweifel zu ziehen.
Die Schriftstellerin verlor ihren im Widerstand gegen die NS-Besatzung engagierten Mann, als er sich der Verhaftung durch Suizid entzog. Sie wurde im Prag der Nachkriegszeit zur Außenseiterin, als sie 1945 als Kulturattaché der zweiten tschechoslowakischen Republik nach New York wechselte und 1948 nach der kommunistischen Machtübernahme in den USA blieb. Bis zu ihrem Tod 1983 wirkte sie als Bohemistin und Literaturtheoretikern in Harvard, Chicago und Berkeley, unterstützt vom Netzwerk der tschechisch-amerikanischen Community um Roman Jacobsen, den Linguisten und Freund aus Prager Zeiten. Die englische Übersetzung ihrer Werke kam nicht zustande.
Zarifa Mamedova beweist Mut, mit „Amor und Psyche“ den Weg ihres anspruchsvollen Verlagsprogramms vorzuzeichnen. dimidium mundi plant weitere Neuentdeckungen von Schriftstellerinnen, auch aus anderen, bisher zu wenig bekannten historischen Buchkulturen aller Kontinente. Wie die Bücher von Olga Wohlbrück und Milada Součková werden auch die kommenden Editionen Grafiken von der Hand junger Künstlerinnen enthalten, deren Originale man online über das zweite Standbein des Verlags erwerben kann.
Milada Součková: „Amor und Psyche“. Aus dem Tschechischen von Doris Kouba. dimidium mundi, München 2026, 320 Seiten, 26 Euro

https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/b.title: Bronxites: Don’t Sacrifice Our Waterfront Access For Yet Another Amazon Warehouse
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/b.author: Dave Colon
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/b.text:
Bronx residents are calling on Gov. Hochul to block an Amazon contractor from converting a former New York Post printing plant into a last-mile warehouse they say would inundate the area with trucks and sacrifice a huge chunk of the borough’s waterfront.
Environmental activists with South Bronx Unite say that logistics giant Prologis, which builds warehouses across the city, wants to convert the dormant printing building — located in Port Morris across from Randalls Island — into a last-mile fulfillment warehouse.
Jeremiah Kane, a vice president at Prologis, met with representatives from South Bronx Unite on Oct. 6 and told them that the company planned to tear down the existing printing plant building and replace it with a last-mile warehouse. 
Prologis’s top tenant nationally is Amazon, according to its most recent Securities and Exchange Commission filing.
The South Bronx waterfront, meanwhile, already hosts a large Fresh Direct warehouse in the Harlem River Rail Yard, which abuts the lot right next to the former newspaper plant. Researchers from Columbia University blamed the Fresh Direct warehouse for increasing motor vehicle traffic after it opened in 2018. With 1,000 Fresh Direct diesel trucks driving through the neighborhood each day, residents are understandably hostile to the possibility of another truck-heavy logistics operation opening in the lot directly next door.
“There’s this feedback loop of ‘Oh well, there’s warehouses here, so it’s a great place to put another warehouse’ instead of ‘Oh there’s warehouses here maybe and 60,000 people live here, maybe we should like think about other other things we can do,'” said South Bronx Unite spokesman David Rosales.
Port Morris and Mott Haven are stuffed with warehouses, and the city government so far has failed to regulate their associated emissions and traffic impacts. One option for doing so is an indirect source rule, under which the city would use a points-based system to force  warehouse owners to electrify their fleets and shift some deliveries to cargo bikes.
Researchers with South Bronx Unite believe that New York state has an opportunity to stop the warehouse development because the state Department of Transportation owns part of the land beneath the Post building.
Originally constructed by the defunct New Haven Railroad, the Harlem River Yards stretch from Lincoln Avenue to slightly east of Willow Avenue. The Penn Central Railroad, which acquired the site from NHR in 1969, sold it to New York State DOT in 1982. Nine years later, the state leased the land to a real estate developer, The Galesi Group, which operates the property under a subsidiary known as Harlem River Yard Ventures. The Post building sits on a lot which includes the easternmost piece of the Harlem River Yards, plus a former MTA bus depot, which the state sold to Harlem River Yard Ventures in 1999.
Before anyone builds anything, South Bronx Unite wants the state to investigate whether it has any direct control over how the land can be used, and if it does, to block a new warehouse from materializing.
“There are restrictive covenants that are tied to the lease that give both the city and the state certain enforcement rights over the land, so an ask that we have for the state is to essentially confirm whether or not these covenants are still still active,” said South Bronx Unite’s energy and economic justice advisor, Zoe Voss Lee.
Lee encouraged the state make use of its cumulative impacts law, which legislators intended to dissuade developments if they add more pollution to historically polluted areas.
“Since the plan for this is to become a warehouse, we can anticipate that there will be significant numbers of trucks that will be brought to the area,” she said.
Rather than another warehouse, South Bronx Unite wants the city and state to open the Bronx Kill waterfront to the public. Rosales pointed to the fact that the state Department of Environmental Conservation has highlighted SBU’s own Mott Haven-Port Morris Waterfront Plan in its official Open Space Conservation Plan.
For the former Post facility, South Bronx Unite envisions a hub for community solar power and a green manufacturing and job-training space. Formerly industrial waterfront spaces — such as Brooklyn Bridge Park, the East River waterfront parks in Manhattan and Brooklyn, Hunter’s Point South and Brooklyn Marine Terminal — have experienced, or will soon experience, second lives as mixed-use neighborhoods. 
As the city has shifted so much of the waterfront away from warehouses and heavy industry, Bronxites while they haven’t received the same treatment.
“Brooklyn and Queens and Manhattan have started to move away from that a lot more, and it feels like in the Bronx it’s moving a lot slower,” Rosales said. “At the end of the day, this stuff comes down to the willingness to do it, the willingness to prioritize it, the willingness to fund it.”
The old Post building is a short walk away from the abandoned and crumbling E. 132nd Street Pier. That proximity has led South Bronx Unite to speculate whether Prologis will pitch the warehouse as part of the city’s “Blue Highways” program to move more freight around the city by boat. That could make the project more palatable to decision-makers, but EDC has already identified locations for that program, and none of them include the pier or anywhere else in the Harlem River Yards.
Lee noted that Kane, the Prologis executive, told the trade publication BisNOW that he was interested in using the Blue Highways program to roll trucks onto and off of boats, in contrast to using small vehicles or even cargo bikes or quad bikes. His comments raised the group’s hackles because they suggested Prologis’s plan would invite even more truck traffic.
“We had a call with Prologis, they were positioning this development as part of the Blue Highways program, but we know that this is not formally a part of EDC’s Blue Highways initiative,” she said. “With the roll-on, roll-off model of Blue Highways, it’s likely that there will be increased truck traffic around the places where the hubs or the last-mile warehouses are actually located.”
The activists oppose the E. 132nd Street Pier’s potential conversion to industry because it conflicts with their vision for opening the waterfront. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who subscribes to the same vision, allocated $1 million just this year to the city’s Department of Small Business Services, who can use the grant to put in oyster reefs, clean up the shoreline and eventually rebuild the pier to restore public access to the pier.
“A concern that South Bronx Unite has regarding the potential of this site being a blue highway, has nothing to do with the premise of blue highways, which of course make a lot of sense when it comes to moving trucks off the road,” said Lee. “It has to do with specifically the positioning of this warehouse and the fact that the site for barging would be the 132nd Street Pier, which has been a project that has been prioritized for public access to the waterfront.”
For now, New York State DOT does not consider itself a participant in the fight over the warehouse. An agency spokesperson said the potential project is entirely privately owned. “The State Department of Transportation can confirm that it owns a portion of Harlem River Yards and has a ground lease with Harlem River Yards Ventures (an affiliate of the Galesi Group) on that portion of property,” said New York State DOT spokesperson Rolando Infante.
A spokesperson for Prologis said the company has only looked at a site that includes completely private land. The company spokesperson also denied that it bought the former Post printing plant, and that it is planning on building a warehouse for Amazon on the site.
“Prologis is not currently under contract to buy the former New York Post printing plant,” said spokesperson Mattie Sorrentino. “We are evaluating the site, as we do other potential projects in the region. Prologis has studied maritime freight options at the site, but the site has not been selected for the Blue Highways program. We have been part of the regional business community for years, investing in the local economy. We have and will continue to grow relationships here and be a long-term partner.”

https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/11uzbekis.title: A chill in Uzbekistan's cultural spring
https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/11uzbekis.author: Maya Jaggi
https://mondediplo.com/2026/11/11uzbekis.text:
Behind the turreted façade of a Russian imperial tram depot in the tree-lined Uzbek capital, Tashkent, is the shock of the new: a sensuous spiral staircase in toffee-coloured terrazzo. A tunnel beneath the yellow-brick site opens into a stunning gallery space.
The Centre for Contemporary Arts (CCA) Tashkent, Uzbekistan’s first such permanent hub, opened this autumn, part of an ambitious cultural strategy in Central Asia’s most populous state (39 million people), now marking 35 years of independence. This derelict 1912 diesel power station, which supplied the region’s first trams, was restored by French architects Studio KO (designers of Marrakesh’s Yves Saint Laurent Museum). The Samarkand carpet and ceramic tiles in the upscale restaurant reinvigorate Silk Road artisanship almost lost in the gruelling labour of cotton plantations during tsarist and Soviet rule.
‘Artists are our ambassadors,’ Gayane Umerova, who commissioned the centre, told me over a lunch of modern Uzbek cuisine. A British Museum exhibition on Afghanistan sparked her ambitions for Uzbek culture, as a student in London. She leads the state-run Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF), created in 2017 by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during the ‘Uzbek spring’.
After the dictator Islam Karimov died in 2016, following a 27-year iron rule, Mirziyoyev’s reforms (from reining in the secret police to ending child labour) gave birth to a ‘New Uzbekistan’. Yet, if more open, the country remains authoritarian. Opposition parties are not tolerated in practice. President Mirziyoyev (previously Karimov’s prime minister) changed the constitution – so he could rule until 2037. Press freedom is ranked a dismal 147th out of 180 countries. Since 2021, ‘insulting the president online’ has been a crime. https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Unesco: 189 jornalistas foram mortos no mundo em 2024 e 2025
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Vitor Abdala
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Levantamento divulgado nesta segunda-feira (2) pela Organização das Nações Unidas para a Educação, a Ciência e a Cultura (Unesco) mostra que 189 jornalistas foram assassinados no mundo em 2024 e 2025. Esse é o maior número de mortes registrado pela Unesco desde o biênio 2014/2015, ou seja, dez anos antes, quando foram observadas 215 ocorrências.
De acordo com o Relatório sobre a Segurança de Jornalistas e o Perigo da Impunidade, a maior parte das mortes (127) ocorreu em país que são zonas de conflito, ou seja, 67% do total. Houve um aumento de 24% em relação ao biênio 2022/2023.
Cinquenta dessas mortes foram por drones. Ataques a escritórios de veículos de imprensa ou instalações que abrigavam jornalistas também foram registrados nessas áreas de conflito. Pelo menos 36 morreram nessa situação. Em um dos casos, nove profissionais morreram de uma só vez.
O levantamento mostra ainda que, em pelo menos 15 casos, há indícios de que os jornalistas tenham sido alvejados mesmo usando coletes com a identificação de “imprensa” ou estando em carros claramente identificados como sendo de jornalistas.
O número de profissionais de imprensa que foram mortos em países fora de zonas de conflito no biênio 2024/2025 (62 casos) é o menor em 18 anos. Desses 62, 17 foram assassinados em seus escritórios; 33, em seus veículos; e 20, na própria casa, em alguns casos junto com membros de suas famílias. Quatro morreram em ataques terroristas e sete foram mortos em situações de manifestações, seja por manifestantes seja por forças policiais.
Em relação ao contexto das mortes, o levantamento mostrou que 104 delas ocorreram enquanto jornalistas cobriam conflitos armados. Mas houve também 38 mortes daqueles reportavam sobre política, 22 dos que trabalhavam em histórias sobre atividades criminais e outras daqueles que noticiavam sobre corrupção.
“Isso mostra que fazer reportagens sobre alguns assuntos pode ser tão perigoso quanto reportar em uma zona de guerra”, afirma a diretora de Liberdade de Expressão e Desenvolvimento da Mídia e Alfabetização Midiática e Informacional da Unesco, Sylvie Couldray.
Dentre os 189 mortos, cinco tinham entre 15 e 24 anos e 20, entre 25 e 29 anos. Foram mortas 14 mulheres, ou seja, 7% do total, o menor percentual desde o biênio 2012/2013. Treze dessas jornalistas foram mortas em países zonas de conflito.
A Palestina, que desde 2023 vem sofrendo ataques de forças israelenses, foi o local onde houve mais mortes de jornalistas (62), ou seja, um terço do total registrado no biênio.
No Brasil, foi registrada apenas uma morte, Luís Augusto Carneiro da Costa, conhecido como Luisinho Costa, assassinado no estúdio da Rádio Guarany, em Abaetetuba, no nordeste do Pará, em maio de 2025. De acordo com a Polícia Civil do Pará, o inquérito foi concluído e remetido à Justiça, com quatro pessoas indiciadas.
Impunidade
Segundo a Unesco, desde 2006, 1.641 jornalistas foram assassinados em todo o mundo, mas apenas 223 dessas mortes foram solucionadas pelo sistema judiciário (14% do total). A maioria dos assassinatos (1.013 ou 66%), no entanto, continua impune, com processos ainda em andamento ou não solucionados. Em 321 casos (20%), a organização não recebeu respostas das autoridades.
De acordo com a Unesco, o nível de impunidade (a soma dos casos não solucionados com aquelas situações em que as autoridades não responderam) chegou a 86% neste ano, um ponto a mais que em 2024. Essa foi a primeira alta desde 2012.
“O relatório é uma ferramenta importante para monitorar as tendências globais, além de nos lembrar que proteger jornalistas e acabar com a impunidade são essenciais para salvaguardar a liberdade de expressão e o direito do público à informação”, afirma a diretora de Comunicação e Informação da Unesco, Mariya Gabriel.
Apesar de apresentar apenas dados relacionados a assassinatos, o relatório também reforça que os jornalistas estão sujeitos a outros tipos de violência não letal, como sequestros, desaparecimentos forçados, detenções arbitrárias, ataques online baseados no gênero do jornalista e a limitação ao movimento desses profissionais.
A Unesco também entrou em contato com autoridades dos 78 países com registros de violência contra jornalistas. Desse total, 38 forneceram informações sobre medidas adotadas para promover a segurança desses profissionais e combater crimes contra eles.
O Brasil, de acordo com o relatório, informou que adotou o Protocolo Nacional para a Investigação de Crimes contra Jornalistas e Comunicadores Sociais, iniciativa lançada em abril deste ano, pelo Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública. O protocolo foi incluído no repositório de mecanismos nacionais de segurança da Unesco.

Les cookies et technologies similaires que nous utilisons sur Mediapart sont de différentes natures et nous permettent de poursuivre différentes finalités. 
Certains sont nécessaires au fonctionnement du site et de l’application mobile (vous ne pouvez pas les refuser). D’autres sont optionnels mais contribuent à faciliter votre expérience de lecteur ou de lectrice et d’une certaine façon à soutenir Mediapart. Vous pouvez les refuser ou les accepter ci-dessous, selon leurs finalités. 
Acceptez-vous que Mediapart utilise des cookies ou technologies similaires pour les finalités suivantes ? 
Vous pouvez faire votre choix, pour chaque catégorie, en activant ou désactivant le bouton interrupteur.
                    
                            
                                Nécessaires au fonctionnement
du site ou de l’application
                            Connexion des abonné·es, mesure d’audience anonymisée, envoi des notifications push, suivi des pannes, mise en avant de nos services : ces outils sont nécessaires au suivi de l’activité de nos services et à leur bon fonctionnement.
                                    Voici les différents cookies et technologies similaires compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Cookies d’authentification : connexion des abonné·es.
- Batch (uniquement sur l’application) : envoi de notifications push et de messages in-app.
- Affichage de contenus éditoriaux multimédias : vidéos (YouTube, Dailymotion, Vimeo, INA), réseaux sociaux (Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Twitter), documents (Scribd, Document Cloud, Slideshare), sons (SoundCloud, Spotify, Deezer), cartes (Google Maps, Mapbox, CartoDB, uMap), infographies (Highcharts, GitHub, Datawrapper, Flourish, Infogram, ThingLink, jQuery, Google Fonts, Bootstrap), live blogs (24liveblog, CoverItLive), aide à l’intégration de média dans les publications Journal et Club (Embedly).
- Datadog (uniquement sur le site web) : indicateurs techniques et équilibrage de charge.
- Firebase Cloud Messaging (uniquement sur l’application) : nécessaire au fonctionnement des notifications push sur Android.
- Microsoft App Center (uniquement sur l’application) : système de mise à jour et de suivi des pannes de l’application.
- Piano : mesure d’audience anonymisée
- Selligent (uniquement sur le site web) : communication avec l’abonné·e, mise en avant des services, offres et avantages.
- Typeform : questionnaires facultatifs pour recueillir les avis des lecteurs sur nos produits numériques.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Ces outils nous permettent de recueillir des statistiques de fréquentation du site et de l’application mobile pour comprendre les usages, détecter d’éventuels problèmes et optimiser l’ergonomie de nos produits.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Batch (uniquement sur le site web) : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- CrazyEggs (uniquement sur le site web) : analyse de parcours client.
- Nonli (uniquement sur le site web) : permet à notre équipe des réseaux sociaux de publier les contenus Mediapart sur les réseaux sociaux.
- Piano : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- Qiota (uniquement sur le site web) : gestion du système de datawall.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Il n’y a pas de publicité sur Mediapart. Mais nous faisons la promotion de nos contenus et services sur d’autres sites et réseaux sociaux. Pour cela, nous utilisons les technologies mises à disposition par certains acteurs publicitaires.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Facebook (uniquement sur le site web) : ciblage d’audience sur les réseaux sociaux pour faire la promotion de Mediapart.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                                Gestion de l’accès aux contenus
                            Nous utilisons le service Qiota d’Opper Marketing Suite pour configurer l’activation d’un datawall sur certains de nos contenus (uniquement sur le site web). Ce dispositif destiné aux utilisateur·ices non abonné·es requiert la saisie d’une adresse email pour accéder aux contenus concernés. En fournissant cette information, l’utilisateur consent à sa collecte, son stockage et son utilisation à des fins statistiques. Conformément à la réglementation en vigueur, les utilisateurs disposent d’un droit d’accès, de rectification et de suppression de leurs données, qu’ils peuvent exercer en contactant dpo@opper.io.

https://taz.de/Forsa-Umfrage-zu-Jugendpr.title: Forsa-Umfrage zu Jugendprotesten: 83 Prozent haben Verständnis für die Proteste
https://taz.de/Forsa-Umfrage-zu-Jugendpr.text:
Forsa-Umfrage zu Jugendprotesten: 83 Prozent haben Verständnis für die Proteste
Die bundesweiten Demonstrationen junger Menschen stoßen in der Bevölkerung auf großes Verständnis. Zugleich sorgt Dobrindts Aussage über ein „migrantisches Milieu“ für Kritik.
kna/afp | Die bundesweiten Demonstrationen junger Menschen am Samstag haben laut einer Umfrage offenbar großen Rückhalt in der Bevölkerung. Eine Mehrheit von 83 Prozent über alle Altersgruppen hinweg hat grundsätzlich Verständnis für die Proteste, wie aus einer Forsa-Umfrage im Auftrag von Stern und RTL hervorgeht. Lediglich 16 Prozent der Befragten hatten demnach kein Verständnis dafür. Letztere Ansicht sei besonders unter Anhängern von CDU/CSU (28 Prozent) und AfD (33 Prozent) verbreitet gewesen.
Bei den deutschlandweiten Protesten, die unter anderem von der Bewegung „Gen Z regelt“ organisiert wurden, gingen in über 30 Städten den Angaben zufolge insgesamt rund 100.000 vornehmlich junge Menschen auf die Straße. Sie demonstrierten für bessere Bildung, mehr soziale Gerechtigkeit und Klimaschutz sowie gegen eine Wehrpflicht. Trotz erhöhter Sicherheitsvorkehrungen kam es in einigen Städten am Rande der Demonstrationen zu Ausschreitungen und Plünderungen.
Für die Umfrage befragte das Meinungsforschungsinstitut Forsa laut Bericht 1.006 Bundesbürger am vergangenen Donnerstag und Freitag – also bevor die Demonstrationen stattfanden. Für den 20. November ist bereits zu neuen Protesten aufgerufen worden.
Merz kritisiert Gewalt bei Protesten
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) hat Verständnis für die Forderungen der protestierenden Jugendlichen in Deutschland gezeigt, zugleich aber die Gewalt am Rande der Kundgebungen scharf kritisiert. Die jungen Menschen verträten „legitime Anliegen“, die er „sehr ernst“ nehme, ließ Merz am Montag über seinen Sprecher Stefan Kornelius mitteilen. Die Reformpolitik seiner Regierung verfolge das Ziel, der jungen Generation „neue Chancen“ zu eröffnen – etwa durch eine Stabilisierung der Staatsfinanzen und eine Reform des Rentensystems.
Zugleich gelte aber: „Gewaltexzesse haben in unserem Land nichts verloren“, sagte Kornelius. Die Polizei habe „zu Recht“ in aller Härte reagiert. Der Bundeskanzler habe „festgestellt, dass sehr viele junge Menschen friedlich demonstriert haben“, betonte der Sprecher. Diese Friedfertigkeit sei dann aber „im Laufe des Abends gekippt“, was „auf das Schärfste“ zu verurteilen sei.
Inhaltlich sehe sich der Kanzler durch die Forderungen der jungen Demonstrierenden in seinem Reformkurs bestätigt: Die „Botschaft der jungen Leute“ decke sich mit der Reformbotschaft, die der Kanzler „seit Monaten wiederholt“, sagte Kornelius.
Kritik nach Dobrindts Aussage zu Gewalt bei „GenZ“-Protesten
Für Diskussionen sorgte die Formulierung von Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), wonach „gewaltbereite linke Gruppen und Chaoten aus dem migrantischen Milieu“ für die Gewalt in der Nacht zu Sonntag verantwortlich seien. Kritiker monierten eine pauschale Schuldzuweisung an Menschen mit ausländischen Wurzeln. Linken-Chef Luigi Pantisano etwa kritisierte dies als „billigen Versuch, einer Gruppe etwas zuzuschreiben, um wieder gegen Migranten in diesem Land zu hetzen“.
Kanzler Merz stellte sich ausdrücklich hinter Dobrindts Äußerung. Dessen Einschätzung zum Tätermilieu speise sich „aus den Beobachtungen der Ermittlungsbehörden und der Einsatzkräfte vor Ort“, sagte sein Sprecher Kornelius. Sie decke sich auch „mit dem Bildmaterial, das viele gesehen haben“. Die Sprecherin des Bundesinnenministeriums räumte ein, dass noch „keine validen bundesweiten Zahlen“ zu den Tatverdächtigen und deren Hintergrund vorlägen. Mit dem Verweis auf das „migrantische Milieu“ seien ganz generell „Personen mit Migrationshintergrund“ gemeint – ungeachtet der Frage, seit wie vielen Generationen deren Familien in Deutschland lebten.
Der CDU-Außenpolitiker Norbert Röttgen hat Innenminister Dobrindt bei dessen Einstufung der Gewalttäter widersprochen. „Es sind Einzeltäter, immer Einzeltäter“, sagte Röttgen am Montagabend in der ntv-Sendung „Pinar Atalay“. Zwar seien unter den Gewalttätern viele gewesen, „die entweder Ausländer sind oder Deutsche ausländischer Abstammung“. Daraus lasse sich aber kein gemeinsames Milieu ableiten. „Es gibt in Deutschland nicht das eine Milieu von Migranten“, sagte Röttgen.
Zugleich betonte Röttgen, dass zwischen friedlichen Demonstranten und Gewalttätern klar unterschieden werden müsse. „Wenn Menschen auf die Straße gehen und demonstrieren, dann ist das ihr Recht“, sagte er. Das sei „die Wahrnehmung unserer Demokratie“. Gewalt hingegen sei durch nichts zu rechtfertigen und erfordere „die Härte des Rechtsstaates“. Es dürfe nicht zugelassen werden, dass Gewalttäter das Demonstrationsrecht friedlicher Teilnehmer für ihre Taten ausnutzten.
Auch Grünen-Chef Felix Banaszak hat der Bundesregierung vorgeworfen, sich nicht mit den Anliegen der protestierenden Jugendlichen zu beschäftigen. Es sei „ein erkennbares Manöver“ von Kanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) und Innenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), „weiterhin sich nicht mit diesen Forderungen auseinanderzusetzen“, sagte Banaszak am Montag in Berlin. „Und damit signalisiert man den Menschen im Kern: Egal wie friedlich am Ende diese Demonstrationen stattfinden, eure Anliegen werden sowieso nicht gehört.“
Das Bundesfamilienministerin kündigte an, dass sich Ministerin Karin Prien (CDU) für diese Woche mit Vertreterinnen und Vertretern der Bundesschülerkonferenz sowie der Gewerkschaft Erziehung und Wissenschaft (GEW) zum Austausch verabredet habe. Prien selbst rief dazu auf, die Interessen jüngerer Menschen stärker zu berücksichtigen. „Das sind genau die Debatten, die wir jetzt führen müssen, die auch die jungen Menschen sehr zu Recht einfordern“, sagte sie im RBB.

https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/t.title: Tuesday’s Headlines: Empire State Wilting Edition
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/t.author: Gersh Kuntzman
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/03/t.text:
Just in time for today’s election, Transportation Alternatives has put out a new report revealing that Department of Transportation projects take too long to go from public presentation to completion.
The group reviewed all bike lane projects announced between 2022 and 2025, and found that an average of 527 days passed between that presentation and completion, which is a lot of time when you consider that it famously took 410 days to build all 102 floors of the Empire State Building nearly a century ago.
Setting aside whether the bike lane vs. Empire State Building comparison is apt (it’s not) — 527 days is a very long time between telling a community board the plan and finishing said project. Yes, there’s usually an intermediate step — defending the plan against the inevitable (and inevitably fruitless) lawsuit — but it still takes too long to make roadways safe.
During those long interregnums, people have been injured and killed, as the group points out:
On Tremont Avenue in the Bronx, safety improvements proposed in June 2024 were not completed until September 2026. In that time, 17 New Yorkers were seriously injured on the street.
On Third Avenue in Brooklyn, safety improvements proposed in 2023 have yet to be installed. Since 2022, three pedestrians have been killed, and 14 people have been seriously injured.
In Sunset Park, safety improvements proposed in 2020 have still not been installed. In 2025, two elderlywomen were killed while walking in separate incidents on Seventh Avenue.
“Red tape is killing New Yorkers,” said Ben Furnas, the group’s executive director. (For another reminder of why timely safety projects are important, check out Erik Engquist’s tweet below):
Delays were also an issue in a report issued last week by Comptroller Mark Levine, whose office that more than half of restaurants that received outdoor dining licenses since the program began in March 2024 waited more than 19 months for approval — far longer than the Department of Transportation’s eight-month timeline.
The good news? DOT started doing a much better job in 2026, after the swearing in of a new mayor. Before that, DOT submitted roughly 29 permits per month to the Comptroller’s office, but starting in February 2026, that number rose to an average of 228 permits per month, rising to 475 permits in July 2026.
“While this increase represents meaningful progress, it does not erase the lengthy delays experienced by applicants or establish whether the program can consistently deliver timely approvals going forward,” Levine’s office wrote. “As of mid-June, when data was collected as part of this investigation, only one roadway application filed in 2026 had resulted in a license within six months. DOT was still working through large numbers of older applications, and 2,115 applications remained pending.”
The takeaway from both these reports: We need city government to be more nimble so that it can better serve the public. Fortunately, there are two referenda about that on today’s Election Day ballot (we’ve covered them, and Gothamist and The City Reporter did yesterday, too): Proposal 1 will make it easier to open outdoor dining setups. And Proposal 3 will cut down the time it takes for the city to redesign roadways for safety.
As a non-profit, we’re not allowed to endorse candidates, but we can endorse ideas — and both of these proposals have our support (as well as the support from the more-eloquent Open Plans). In any event, please vote and remember to turn over your ballot for the referenda. (And find your polling place here.)
In other news:
Game on? When will the MTA restore the basketball court near our office? (Gothamist)
Non-starter: The Citizens Budget Commission is already putting it out there that the MTA should cut some jobs to save money. (Gothamist)
Mayor to ICE: Stop using our parking lots. (NY Times, NYDN)
Subway ridership soared during the Marathon on Sunday. (NYDN)
The plutocratic populists at the New York Post are at it again: an editorial board that believes that congestion pricing is a “tax” on the middle class now want you to believe that they care about bus riders. Fact: The Post’s editors don’t care about bus riders; they just want to undermine public faith in transit so that less public money is allocated to transit, starving it further and serving their larger anti-urban agenda of encouraging more car ownership and use.
Case in point: The Post thinks the PATH train is too expensive. Now do cars, Rupert!

He's also the writer and producer of "Murder at the Food Coop," which was a hit at the NYC Fringe Festival in 2016, and “SUV: The Musical” in 2007. https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.title: Carrie at 50: Brian De Palma’s fiery masterpiece still has the power
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.author: Jesse Hassenger
https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/no.text:
Often when a pop culture figure, whether real or fictional or somewhere in between, is described as an eternal teenager, it refers to an image of youthful vitality. Carrie White, the wallflowery, telekinetic, sort-of heroine at the center of Stephen King’s book and its multiple adaptations, is a sadder case. She’s forever a teenager because until recently, every version of the story ends with her demise – a turn that would qualify as a spoiler if not for the universal familiarity of her story, or the fact that the book heavily implies her fate within the first 30 pages or so.
That fate is poised to change with Mike Flanagan’s TV series, which was recently renewed for a second season (though even then, there’s still plenty of room for poor Carrie to die young). The new show updates and expands the story of the 1974 novel, taking its inspiration from a combination of 2020s social trends and details from the original text. In other words, it’s a new adaptation, not a remake of the Brian De Palma film from 1976. As such, it’s the first truly successful version of Carrie in half a century. (Previous iterations popped up in a 1999 movie sequel, a 2002 miniseries and another film in 2013.) It’s arguable, however, that the reason such a high-profile new version of Carrie exists in 2026 is that first film, which was released 50 years ago on 3 November.
In fact, King’s book was not a bestseller when it first came out in 1974. His subsequent novel, Salem’s Lot, sold better out the gate in 1975; Carrie didn’t hit the New York Times bestseller list until December 1976, in paperback form. This was a month or so after the release of De Palma’s film, which had become an unexpectedly strong holiday-season hit. Though a willowy Sissy Spacek wasn’t a precise match for King’s description of Carrie as a more full-figured and less ethereal teenager (nor was her mid-20s age a match for Carrie’s teenage status), the image of her drenched in blood, wide-eyed with shellshocked vengeance at the film’s prom-set climax became indelibly associated with the simple story.
De Palma’s film is even more streamlined than King’s novel. It retains the basic structure – the first half taking place over a week or so leading up to the high school prom, the second following that evening, where Carrie is unexpectedly crowned queen before suffering a planned humiliation, followed by an extremely brief survey of the aftermath – as well as many of the book’s details and some of its dialogue. But King also intersperses excerpts from various (fictional) outside texts written after the story’s deadly climax, both hinting (sometimes more than hinting) at the carnage to come and filling in various backstories and flashback anecdotes about Carrie White, her telekinetic powers and her religious fanatic mother Margaret (Piper Laurie in the movie).
Without these digressions, De Palma’s film seems ruthlessly efficient, especially compared to the recent series. While King’s imaginative array of academic explorations, magazine articles and fake tell-alls lend the proceedings a slight detachment (if a frequently mournful one), De Palma uses his pure-cinema immediacy to put the audience into the movie’s hair-trigger adolescent-hothouse atmosphere. That most of the actors were actually well into adulthood only makes their aggression pop more. Some have accused De Palma’s opening sequence, where the camera tracks around a girls’ locker room in anticipation of the famous inciting incident where Carrie gets a late-onset period and is terrorized by her cruel classmates, of crossing the line into lasciviousness. But when his camera lands on a showering Carrie White, alone with her thoughts and a vaguely sensual look on her face, De Palma keys into all that is discomfortingly intimate about the story, fraying at that image immediately when Carrie notices her menstrual blood and panics.
That raw-nerve discombobulation is a hallmark of the film, which traffics in familiar settings (high school, teenagers in cool cars, a glittery dance) while making them feel distorted and intense. To this end De Palma makes heavy use of split-diopter shots, a camera-lens trick that creates the ability to sharply focus on objects in the foreground and background simultaneously, with a blurry, out-of-focus line separating the two. In an English-classroom scene, for example, De Palma keeps popular, cheerful Tommy (William Katt) in closeup while Carrie, quietly besotted with the poem he wrote for class, remains in focus several rows behind him. They’re occupying the same space, but Carrie – bedeviled by her classmates, yes, but also the haranguing of her impossible-to-please, God-fearing mom – looks impossibly distant, too.
Later, after repentant popular girl Sue (Amy Irving) has Tommy, her boyfriend, ask Carrie to prom to give her a taste of social acceptance, De Palma’s camera follows the not-quite-couple to the dancefloor. As they dance in circles, the camera rotates around them, which in conjunction with the colorful lighting creates a dizzying, carnival-like effect. It’s a lead-up to a classic De Palma uncorking, where vengeful mean girl Chris (the terrific Nancy Allen, who later married and divorced De Palma) dumps a bucket of pig’s blood on to poor Carrie, unleashing the girl’s nascent telekinetic powers. An entire gymnasium’s worth of students suffers her split-screened, fiery wrath, with Psycho-style string stings accompanying the bursts of power. (It’s probably not a coincidence that the main location has been rechristened Bates high school by Alfred Hitchcock-loving De Palma.)
Watching De Palma’s treatment of this sequence soon after Flanagan’s is striking: in part because De Palma’s version is scarier (while Flanagan’s somewhat mitigates Carrie’s participation), and in part because it’s so evocative without the torrents of dialogue that Flanagan favors. There are about 15 minutes from Carrie’s prom-queen coronation to her arrival back at home to have it out with her mother that involve only incidental chatter. For that matter, there isn’t a whole lot of dialogue in the ensuing final 15 minutes, either. This does mean that both King’s book and Flanagan’s series have a bit more nuance to various characters. The 1976 movie portrays the world around Carrie as both beautiful and unceasingly harsh; her moments of respite, even joy, have a pleading quality. That quality only makes Spacek’s performance – Oscar-nominated, alongside Laurie’s – all the more heartbreaking. In the end, the White house collapses on to Carrie and her mother; it crumbles from her psychic powers, but she seeks cover all the same, toting her lousy mother’s body with her, surrendering to her power as uncontrollable.
De Palma can’t resist one last sting that wouldn’t make much sense in the book: a dreamy scene where Sue visits the razed site of the White house, whereupon a bloody arm bursts out of the ground and grabs hold of her, before she awakes screaming in fright. This could be read as a cheap horror-movie trick to rattle audiences just a little more on their way out the door, or a nasty rebuke to Sue’s mother who claims a doctor said Sue will probably forget all about the Carrie White incident in time. Fifty years later, though, it feels most like an acknowledgment of how this particular version of Carrie has lingered in the public imagination as a nightmare reflection of the adolescent experience. Flanagan brought Carrie White into the 21st century, but she didn’t have to travel far to get here.
