https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: A collection of intimate interviews with the late Jo Spence provides further texture to her life and legacy
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: Beth Williamson
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
Jo Spence (1934-92) was a London-born and based British photographer, writer, class and health activist and educator. She is best known for challenging the assumptions of what photography could be, for example, by using her own image to question common tropes around female beauty, health, identity and societal expectations. Spence’s achievements centred on the small home and studio on Islington’s Upper Street that she shared with her partner and collaborator Terry Dennett (1938-2018).
The Unknown Recordings is an intimate self-portrait in text form. There are pictures, but surprisingly few. Still, in that respect, Spence’s disarmingly frank autobiography Putting Myself in the Picture (1986) could not be surpassed. Forty years on, this publication makes sense of a textual account largely in the form of transcripts of key historic recordings made with the artist.
The verbatim transcript of Spence’s interview for the British Library’s Oral History of British Photography, recorded in 1991, extends to more than 100 pages. It covers every aspect of her life from childhood experiences to early working life, before progressing to her photographic work, collaborations and politics, as well as her experience of breast cancer and leukaemia.
The conversation between Spence and the interviewer flows, with few fragments and diversions, in a manner that allows us (almost) to hear it. Generous in her sharing of extremely personal ideas and experiences, Spence does not shy away from difficult topics, least of all her own experience of chronic illness and her attempts to regain power over her own body and identity. Her friendship with artist Rosy Martin and their development of phototherapy, a form of psychological therapy centred on photography, is especially raw.
Distress, tears and self-analysis
The transcript of a short personal recording made in 1982, after the breast cancer diagnosis, is more unsettling. This is Spence recording her own thoughts, filled with distress, tears and self-analysis: while it became part of her archive and she often blurred the line between private and public, it does feel a little like eavesdropping. Recorded over two days, it is intensely emotional, as Spence struggles to process and come to terms with the various stressors in her life. In a particularly poignant moment, Dennett is recorded shouting words of support, presumably from another room.
Spence’s interview with visual activist and educator Andrew Dewdney and curator Shirley Read has a political slant. Recorded in the Cockpit Arts Workshop in London in 1989, this conversation gives acute insight into Spence’s commitment to a political as well as photographic practice. It ranges across her ideas relating to different areas of her work, such as the Photography Workshop, Hackney Flashers, Half Moon Photography Workshop and Camerawork magazine. Ultimately, these projects perhaps coalesced around Spence’s focus on people’s right to speak and be seen. It is a powerful conversation.
A series of four appendices act as a kind of postscript to Spence’s voice. There is the documentation of Spence’s sacking from Half Moon over ideological differences; recently discovered images of Spence’s retrospective of 1994; photographs, thoughts and exchanges with artist Pru Clements; and Spence’s CV from March 1987.
This section also includes Dennett’s reworked introduction to Spence’s Putting Myself in the Picture. Here, he makes it clear that Spence’s work was done under difficult circumstances but that she remained focused on the importance of empowering others. Rather than concluding in some fashion or other, together these last documents point the reader to other rich visual and textual archival material that surrounds Spence’s life and legacy. She extended the possibilities of photography to speak about the unspeakable and photograph the unphotographable. Spence was not within the cultural elite, but found a way to tell her own story and hoped it would be a model for others to follow.
• Jo Spence: The Unknown Recordings, Museums etc, 256 pp, 30 colour and 8 b/w illustrations, £35 (pb), £25 (e-b), 1 January

https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio.title: They fell in love on The Simpsons and married in real life. Meet the French Homer and Marge
https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio.author: Hannah J Davies
https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio.text:
The Simpsons is the biggest cartoon comedy in the world, with suburban couple Homer and Marge at its heart. From their beginnings as high-school sweethearts to the travails of married life, they’re an unbreakable pair. Gag-heavy as it may be, it’s also a series with plenty of sentimental plots, from Homer giving up his beloved Duff beer for a month to prove his love to Marge, to Marge composing a heartfelt poem to a dying Homer (miraculously, he makes it through his sushi-induced food poisoning).
Not even the temptations of a brunch-loving bowling instructor called Jacques or a doughnut-guzzling redhead called Mindy could get between them. Plus, of course, they enjoy the occasional “snuggle” (even on a miniature golf course … ).
Now in its 38th season, The Simpsons has also been a huge hit across the globe, meaning hundreds of international actors have voiced this much-loved couple. Among them are Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau, who – as well as playing Marge and Homer in the French dub of The Simpsons since 1990 – met through the show and ended up getting married.
“Matt Groening called us the second most famous couple in the history of animation,” says Peythieu. “There were the actors who voiced Minnie and Mickey Mouse [the late Wayne Allwine and Russi Taylor], and then there was us. Meanwhile in Los Angeles, he said, everyone he worked with was getting divorced …”
The pair record their scenes together with a director in a Paris dubbing studio over 10-12 days a year. But clearly The Simpsons is a 365-day-a-year commitment, from appearances at galas and conventions to the gifts they receive from adoring fans. Both are adamant that they wouldn’t carry on without the other, which means a definite non to AI taking over in the future. “We’re not for artificial intelligence – we’re for artistic intelligence!” says Augereau. There will always be roles that require a human soul, she adds, and – for Peythieu and Augereau – this role has given them each a soulmate to boot.
Do you remember meeting for the first time?
Philippe Peythieu: We met at a casting call in 1989 – it was only six months after The Simpsons had debuted in the US, so it wasn’t a success there yet. We auditioned, and then six months later – by fax – we found out we had got the roles.
Véronique Augereau: Philippe and I didn’t know each other well at all. When we were trying out, we crossed paths in the hallway at the dubbing offices and greeted each other but we were just colleagues – we weren’t even friends at that stage. There’s a video of us at a wrap party for the first series and we’re just walking right past each other, not even speaking, let alone stealing any glances!
PP: Voilà, that’s how this beautiful story began. The recording process brought us closer together, since we were working in the darkness of the studio, and so we became more than friends … We had to be very discreet in the beginning, because this was a professional setting, but eventually word got out and we were inseparable from that point on. As for the series, we never imagined it would last so long. But the success also contributed to the success of our relationship.
VA: In terms of what actually attracted us to each other, it’s hard to say, but I think the atmosphere around the recording sessions helped – there was always a friendly, funny vibe. Personally, I find the show and the storylines extraordinary, and incredibly intelligent. I think we really loved this show and were enthusiastic about it from the get-go. We liked the spirit of the series, and that humour that could be quite biting.
What do Homer and Marge love about each other?
VA: Marge isn’t a fan of Homer’s over-the-top antics, but deep down she knows that he is her one and only love in life. Ultimately, she has a lot of tenderness and affection for this man, whom she knows is devoted to her and to their children. He is completely in love with his family – even if he doesn’t remember his children’s names all the time …
PP: Through the seasons there have been rifts, but every time they’ve found their way back to each other. If you look at the film [The Simpsons Movie, released in 2007], Marge decides to leave Homer, but ends up forgiving all of his foolish mistakes in the end. Their love grows stronger – they’re able to separate then find each other again.
VA: A critic in France, Romain Nigita, actually wrote a book called Les Simpson ou le paradoxe du donut intemporel (The Simpsons, or the Paradox of the Timeless Doughnut), to which we wrote the preface. [The book is about the show’s relationship with time, and how it never changes yet always seems relevant.] He writes about Marge and Homer’s first meeting in high school – Homer smoking in the bathroom with Barney, Marge burning her bra at a feminist protest, before the pair cross paths at the high-school prom. That’s when Homer says: “I’m sure we were meant to be together. Usually when I have a thought, there’s a lot of other thoughts in there ... something says yes, something says no ... But this time, there’s only yes! How can the only thing I’ve ever been sure about in my life be wrong?”
When did you realise this was a love story for the ages?
VA: Across all of these seasons (we will soon be dubbing season 38), this couple is still standing!
PP: Despite his doubts, his worst gaffes and the tests of time, Homer is certain of one thing: Marge is the love of his life!
What have been your favourite romantic moments between them?
VA: We love the bedroom scenes when they’re in their room with the lights off and you can only see their eyes moving around.
PP: Those scenes that can be a bit cheeky but they’re handled very well – the show addresses sexuality but with a lightness of touch, affection and humour.
Is there anything you wish Marge and Homer did differently?
PP: When you’re this hooked on The Simpsons, it’s hard to be critical of the show. It would also be difficult to rewrite its history – it’s a show that has defined an era. Besides, we love these characters unconditionally, so whatever they do we would always forgive them! Homer also resembles us – I think, as a man, I’m a bit like him, and he’s a bit like me in some ways. What you see is what you get with Homer, and yet he still manages to surprise us …
VA: I don’t love the Halloween specials, personally.
PP: She finds them scary. There was a Halloween episode where they sent up The Shining – I loved that one.
What is your real relationship like off camera?
VA: We share the same values in life and move forward together, bound by a very strong connection.
How romantic are you in real life?
VA: We often stroll down the street arm in arm, and people always say, “Hello, lovebirds!” or – if I’m alone – “Oh, not with your husband today?” I don’t want to say that people have this idealised vision of us, but when we meet fans at conventions they always say the same sorts of things to us too. Whether in The Simpsons or in real life, it seems that many people see us as this devoted couple that they enjoy spending time with.
PP: We’ve had the opportunity to meet Matt Groening and the team several times, and they’ve always told us that the French version is one of the best, because we’ve understood the spirit of the series, and the fact that we’re husband and wife has added that little extra something to it.
What has been the most intense fan reaction to Marge and Homer?
VA: People tell us, you were the soundtrack to our childhood. Fans will tell us that we represent this perfect couple in their eyes – every Saturday night we were in their homes, on their TVs, so for some people we were almost like surrogate parents.
Did you keep something from set that reminds you of Marge and Homer?
VA: It’s not from set, but at a charity gala in Switzerland we were given a huge portrait of Marge as a Playboy bunny [a callback to the episode The Devil Wears Nada].
PP: I’ve lost count of the amount of times I’ve been given doughnuts.
What can Marge and Homer teach us about love?
PP: What they teach us is that – come what may – it’s all about this strong bond that they have. It’s a bond that’s almost indestructible despite life’s difficulties and the differences that sometimes come between them.
VA: They show us that love is about forgiveness.
PP: And accepting the differences between both people.
VA: You have to be on the same page in life too … with us, we have the same tastes, like contemporary art, food …
PP: We’re bon vivants! We love life. We rarely argue, and if we do it’s usually about trivial things.
VA: That’s why it’s lasted all these years – we’ve been together nearly as long as The Simpsons!

https://taz.de/USA-beschiessen-Ziele-in-.title: USA beschießen Ziele in Iran: Der nächste Irankrieg steht vor der Tür
https://taz.de/USA-beschiessen-Ziele-in-.author: Lisa Schneider
https://taz.de/USA-beschiessen-Ziele-in-.text:
USA beschießen Ziele in Iran: Der nächste Irankrieg steht vor der Tür
Ob die USA diese Tür öffnen, dürfte sich nach den Midterm-Wahlen zeigen. Aufgerüstet wird massiv, jetzt wurde auch eine iranische Insel beschossen.
Es war der erste bestätigte US-Angriff in Iran seit Anfang September: Mehrere Geschosse wurden in der Nacht zum Dienstag auf die iranische Insel Keschm in der Straße von Hormus abgefeuert, die größte Insel im Persischen Golf. Getroffen wurde nach Angabe des US-Präsidenten Donald Trump eine Luftabwehreinrichtung. Den Angriff begründete das US-Militär mit einem vorangegangenen Angriff Irans auf ein US-Flugzeug.
Der Angriff kurz vor Beginn der Midterm-Wahlen in den USA am Dienstag ist laut Wall Street Journal nicht der erste dieser Art in den vergangenen Wochen. Bereits am Montag wurde von Explosionen auf Keschm berichtet; Ende Oktober von Explosionen in Teheran und im Norden des Landes. Ob es sich dabei um die nun berichteten kleineren US-Angriffe handelte, wurde allerdings nicht bestätigt.
Ist das nun also der erneute Ausbruch des Krieges zwischen den USA, Iran und potenziell auch Israel? Auch wenn formal eine Waffenruhe gilt – Frieden ist seit dem Ausbruch des Kriegs Ende Februar 2026 nicht mehr eingekehrt.
Das US-Militär blockiert die Ein- und Ausfahrt iranischer Schiffe in der Straße von Hormus seit Mitte Juli. Gleichzeitig haben immer mehr Schiffe aus anderen Anrainerstaaten des Persischen Golfs, den die Straße von Hormus mit den Weltmeeren verbindet, die Durchfahrt mit US-Unterstützung gewagt. Die International Maritime Organisation zählte im Oktober eine Rekordziffer von 31 Zwischenfällen; ein getroffenes Schiff sank.
Konzessionsbereit ist weder Teheran noch Washington
Aus diesem Grundrauschen könnte bald wieder ein heißer Krieg erwachsen. Indikatoren gibt es einige. So scheint der indirekte diplomatische Prozess zwischen den USA und Iran, mit Katar als Mediator, weiterhin an denselben Punkten zu stocken wie zuvor. Der Analyst Dennis Citrinowicz schreibt auf X: Weder Washington noch Teheran wollten eine erneute Kriegsrunde, doch keiner von beiden sei zu den nötigen Konzessionen bereit. Und damit wohl lieber bereit, die Risiken einer militärischen Konfrontation zu tragen.
Außerdem wirkt die Blockade der Straße von Hormus im Sinne Washingtons – je länger, desto besser. Da durch den Stopp des Ölhandels kaum mehr Devisen aus dem Ölexport an Iran fließen, entwertet die iranische Währung Rial immer weiter. Der Wechselkurs hat ein Allzeittief erreicht: 2,72 Millionen Rial kostet 1 US-Dollar. Im Dezember 2025 waren es etwa 1,5 Millionen pro US-Dollar.
Der zweite Indikator ist die anhaltende Verlagerung von US-amerikanischem Equipment und Truppen Richtung Iran. Wer sich heute auf dem Gelände des Flughafens Ben Gurion in Tel Aviv bewegt, sieht eine ganze Reihe von Betankungsflugzeugen aufgereiht. Auch aus Jordanien und Katar gibt es solche Berichte. Hinzu kommt die Marine: Rund 20 US-Kriegsschiffe befinden sich derzeit im Einsatzgebiet. Auch etwa 50.000 Soldatinnen und Soldaten der USA sind bereits in der Region stationiert.
Weitere Verstärkung ist auf dem Weg: Der Flugzeugträger „USS Theodore Roosevelt“ verließ Ende September die USA und soll Ende November nahe Iran eintreffen. Außerdem ist eine amphibische Einsatzgruppe mit über 2.000 Mann auf dem Weg, sie soll ebenfalls Ende November ankommen. Diese Gruppe könnte unter anderem auf Inseln landen. Der massive Aufbau erinnert an den Vorlauf des Irankriegs im Frühjahr.
Der dritte Indikator sind die beteiligten Politiker selbst: Washington hat Berichten zufolge bereits die Golfstaaten informiert, dass es nach den Midterms eine „Kampagne“ geben werde. Israels Noch-Premier Benjamin Netanjahu lobbyierte bereits vor der Wahl in Israel am 27. Oktober für einen erneuten Angriff der USA auf Iran. Nun, da seine bisherige Koalition keine Parlamentsmehrheit geholt hat, dürfte sein Interesse daran wachsen.
Ein erneuter heißer Krieg mit Iran steigert die Chancen für ein Kriegskabinett in Israel und die Bildung einer Einheitsregierung der größten Parteien – an der Bibi wohl wieder beteiligt wäre. Der Weg der Eskalation ist vorgezeichnet.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Quando saem os resultados das eleições nos EUA? Apuração em estados decisivos pode levar semanas
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
As urnas das eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, conhecidas como midterms, encerram a votação nesta terça-feira (3), mas a definição de qual partido controlará a Câmara dos Representantes e o Senado pode levar dias ou até semanas.
Diferentemente do modelo brasileiro, o sistema eleitoral estadunidense não conta com um órgão centralizador da apuração, ficando a contagem a cargo de cada um dos 50 estados e de suas respectivas legislações locais.
Os primeiros locais de votação encerram o atendimento às 20h (horário de Brasília) em partes dos estados de Indiana e Kentucky. Já os últimos boletins de urna serão encerrados no Alasca e no Havaí às 3h de quarta-feira (4) no horário de Brasília.
Apesar de algumas disputas locais com margens amplas poderem ser projetadas ainda na noite de terça, o equilíbrio acirrado em estados decisivos inviabiliza anúncios imediatos do resultado final.
A contagem é impactada pela elevada adesão ao voto antecipado. Mais de 56 milhões de eleitores estadunidenses enviaram suas cédulas por correio ou votaram presencialmente antes do dia oficial do pleito. Em estados populosos como a Califórnia e o Arizona, a conferência de assinaturas, a validação de envelopes e o processamento do alto volume de correspondências que chegam no dia da votação estendem o trabalho das autoridades eleitorais.
Processamento por estado
Na Califórnia, a legislação estadual permite a contabilização de votos enviados pelo correio que cheguem até sete dias após a eleição, desde que tenham o carimbo postal datado até terça.
Em eleições anteriores, a apuração completa das vagas mais disputadas para a Câmara dos Representantes no estado exigiu até três semanas para a confirmação dos vencedores.
No Alasca e no Maine, o uso do sistema de votação por escolha ranqueada adiciona etapas ao processo. No Alasca, cédulas de eleitores residentes no exterior podem ser recebidas até 15 dias após o pleito.
Caso nenhum candidato alcance mais de 50% dos votos na primeira contagem, as autoridades iniciam uma segunda rodada de apuração com o reprocessamento das opções dos eleitores.
Projeções da imprensa
Diante da falta de uma apuração oficial unificada, a imprensa internacional utiliza modelos estatísticos para projetar os prováveis vencedores à medida que os dados são checados. Nas eleições de meio de mandato de 2022, a confirmação da maioria no Senado levou quatro dias, enquanto a definição do controle da Câmara dos Representantes demorou oito dias.
Em 2020, a projeção do resultado da eleição presidencial foi anunciada quatro dias após a votação. A demora na contagem oficial tem sido explorada por setores da extrema direita para espalhar alegações sem provas sobre a integridade das urnas.
Renovação no Congresso
As eleições de meio de mandato renovam a totalidade dos 435 assentos da Câmara dos Representantes, cujos deputados cumprem mandatos de dois anos, e 35 das 100 cadeiras do Senado, com mandatos de seis anos, além da escolha de 36 governadores estaduais. Atualmente, o Partido Republicano mantém a maioria nas duas Casas Legislativas.
Para obter o controle da Câmara dos Representantes, os democratas precisam conquistar três cadeiras adicionais. No Senado, onde os republicanos mantêm uma vantagem de 53 a 47 assentos, o Partido Democrata precisa de quatro novas vagas para formar maioria.
De acordo com a Constituição dos Estados Unidos, os mandatos dos parlamentares eleitos começam no dia 3 de janeiro de 2027. Como a data cairá em um domingo, o início das sessões do novo Congresso poderá ser alterado por lei federal para o primeiro dia útil subsequente.

- Warnstreiks IG Metall
Verhärtete Fronten in der Metallindustrie
Die Industriegewerkschaft Metall stellt sich auf lange Verhandlungen und viele Warnstreiks ein. Die Kampfbereitschaft zeigt sich in NRW.
Im Tarifkonflikt in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie plant die Industriegewerkschaft Metall (IG Metall) bis Ende der Woche Warnstreiks in mehr als 2000 Betrieben bundesweit. Am Montag beteiligten sich nach Gewerkschaftsangaben bereits rund 38.000 Beschäftigte an 220 betrieblichen Aktionen, unter anderem in Koblenz und Berlin, bei Mercedes-Benz, Rheinmetall und Siemens Mobility. Dienstag weitete die IG Metall die Warnstreiks mit Schwerpunkten in Baden-Württemberg, Nordrhein-Westfalen und im Bezirk Mitte mit Hessen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Saarland und Thüringen aus. Am Mittwoch folgen weitere Standorte.
Die Gewerkschaft hat bei einer Laufzeit von zwölf Monaten fünf Prozent mehr Lohn sowie die Sicherung von Jobs und Standorten für 3,7 Millionen Beschäftigte gefordert. Die Arbeitgeber haben in der zweiten Verhandlungsrunde ein Angebot vorgelegt, das zunächst eine Einmalzahlung und eine Stufenerhöhung von 1,3 Prozent im Juli 2028 bei einer Laufzeit von 26 Monaten vorsieht. Begründet wurde die Offerte mit der schwierigen wirtschaftlichen Lage und den hohen Kostenbelastungen für die Industrie in Deutschland.
Kritik der Gewerkschaften aus NRW
Die IG Metall und Beschäftigte der Metall- und Elektroindustrie in Nordrhein-Westfalen stellen sich auf zähe Verhandlungen und langanhaltende Streiks in der jüngsten Tarifauseinandersetzung ein. Dort wird seit Anfang dieser Woche in etwa 270 Betrieben gestreikt. Von Dienstag an wurden die Warnstreiks nochmals ausgeweitet.
Die IG Metall kritisiert das Angebot der Arbeitgeber massiv. Es liegt laut dem IG-Metall-Verhandlungsführer in NRW, Knut Giesler, »weit unter der Inflation, obwohl die Wirtschaft erste Signale der Erholung« sende. »Das werden wir nicht akzeptieren.« Das Angebot gleiche weder die gestiegenen Lebenshaltungskosten aus, noch biete es Perspektiven für Investitionen, Beschäftigungssicherung und die Zukunft der Industriestandorte. Tatsächlich wächst die Wirtschaftsleistung in Nordrhein-Westfalen erstmalig seit neun Jahren wieder. Für dieses Jahr macht das RWI-Leibniz-Intitut für Wirtschaftsforschung ein leichtes Wachstumsplus von 0,6 Prozent, im nächsten Jahr von rund 0,9 Prozent aus.
Deshalb und auch weil insbesondere die durch Aufrüstung in Deutschland gutverdienenden Rüstungsunternehmen wie Rheinmetall immer mehr Umsatz und Gewinn machen, wertet die IG Metall das Angebot als unzureichend, einige Gewerkschafter sprechen gar von einer Frechheit. Die IG Metall fordert daher für die rund 640.000 Beschäftigten in der nordrhein-westfälischen Metall- und Elektroindustrie von den Arbeitgebern »ein deutlich besseres Angebot«.
Unternehmen sehen »falsches Signal«
Die Unternehmen in der Branche geben an, unter den hohen Energie- und Lohnstückkosten sowie der allgemein lahmenden Wirtschaft zu leiden. Zwar veröffentlicht der Gesamtverband Metall die offiziellen Gewinnzahlen nicht, aber seit drei Jahren sinken Umsatz und Produktionsumfang und die Lohnstückkosten sind um knapp elf Prozent gestiegen.
Sie warnen die IG Metall, die Tarifrunde mit Warnstreiks zusätzlich anzuheizen – dies sei »das völlig falsche Signal«. »In der schwersten Strukturkrise dieses Industriezweigs brauchen die Unternehmen keine Eskalation, sondern möglichst zügig eine tragfähige und vernünftige Lösung«, sagte ein Sprecher von Metall NRW der dpa.
Aus Betrieben und von Betriebsräten, mit denen »nd« sprechen konnte, hört man, dass die Beschäftigten von langen Verhandlungen und vielen Warnstreiks ausgehen. »Wir werden weiter kämpfen, denn die Forderungen der IG Metall sind mehr als gerechtfertigt«, sagen etwa Mitarbeiter eines metallverarbeitenden Betriebes am Dienstagmorgen in Mülheim an der Ruhr.
Engin Karakurt, Betriebsrat aus Bochum, rechnet mit einem »langen Arbeitskampf« und »harten Verhandlungen, um annähernd an unsere Forderung von fünf Prozent« zu kommen. Die Friedenspflicht der bundesweiten Verhandlungen endete mit Ablauf des 31. Oktober. Die nächste Verhandlungsrunde ist für den 9. November angesetzt.
Kein Milliardär im Rücken
Andere Medien haben Konzerne oder Milliardäre im Rücken. Wir haben die nd.Genossenschaft und Leser*innen wie dich. Das macht uns unabhängig und genau das wollen wir bleiben. Aber es heißt auch: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Du kannst direkt hier spenden, einmalig oder regelmäßig, damit nd bleibt.

https://gothamist.com/news/2026-midterm-.title: 2026 Midterm Election Day is here: What to know in NY and NJ
https://gothamist.com/news/2026-midterm-.author: Verónica Del Valle, Brittany Kriegstein, Brigid Bergin, Mike Hayes
https://gothamist.com/news/2026-midterm-.text:
Polls are open across the country today as voters cast their ballots in elections that will decide the balance of power in Congress, along with several high-profile races for governor and other races down-ballot. The midterm election is often considered a referendum on the party in control of the White House. But with spiking costs at the grocery store and gas station, the cost of living has consistently ranked among the top concerns of voters.
Shrey Panda of Fort Greene voted during his morning run Tuesday and said, like most Americans, that affordability was top of mind.
"It's very expensive here and I think in the country," Panda, 33, said before going in to vote. "I think the economy is always going to be number one."
In New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr. is fighting for his political life against Democratic challenger Rebecca Bennett who leads most polls in the race. But Dean Seda, a DJ with DJ's at the Polls, was spinning some tunes at a polling site in the district Tuesday morning, to give the electoral fight a more festive atmosphere.
"It's a unique opportunity to be a part of a very important day in New Jersey and the U.S.A.," Seda, 35, said, adding he's part of a national initiative at thousands of polling sites across the country, "to provide a little more of an energetic environment at the polls."
What to know today
Polls open at 6 a.m. in New York and New Jersey on Tuesday.
Find out where your Election Day poll site in New York is here. Polls close at 9 p.m.
Find out where your Election Day poll site in New Jersey is here. Polls close at 8 p.m.
What if I have a mail ballot?
In New York, you can complete your mail ballot and drop it off at your county Board of Elections office or any poll site open on Tuesday. Your mail ballot will count if the Board of Elections receives it by Election Day, or it arrives within a week of Election Day but has a postmark of Election Day. The United States Postal Service does not always apply a postmark the day an item is received, so it may be too late to put a ballot into the postal mail to ensure timely delivery.
In New Jersey, you can drop off mail-in ballots at a secure drop box or your county Board of Elections office. You can find a drop box location in your county here. For those returning ballots via mail, ballots must be postmarked no later than Election Day at 8 p.m. and received no later than six days after the election. Note: Polling sites DO NOT accept vote-by-mail ballots.
What is on the ballot in New York?
New York voters will choose their governor, state attorney general, state comptroller, along with federal and state legislative representatives.
Read more about the candidates in our New York voter guide.
What about New York City specifically?
In New York City, voters will also be asked to decide five ballot questions. A guide to the ballot questions is here.
Who is on the ballot in New Jersey?
Congressional races are dominating this year’s election cycle in New Jersey. You can find our early voting guide here.
First-time Democratic nominee Rebecca Bennett is attempting to unseat Republican Rep. Tom Kean in New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District in what’s expected to be New Jersey’s most competitive midterm race.
Unlike some other rising Democrats in the state, like progressive Rep. Analilia Mejia and Dr. Adam Hamawy, Bennett has run as a middle-of-the-road Democrat in a typically conservative district that has leaned Republican since 2020. The 39-year old former healthcare executive and Navy helicopter pilot has focused on affordability issues like rising costs for gas, grocery, childcare and healthcare. Read more about her attempt to court independent and Republican voters in the red-leaning district in North Jersey.
Kean, the political heir of one of the Garden State’s most well-known political dynasties, is seeking a third term in Congress. The 58-year old Republican is the son of a popular former governor and served in the state Legislature for nearly two decades. He is running in the shadow of President Donald Trump’s sinking poll numbers in the state and has faced lingering questions about a 100+ day absence from Congress earlier this year when Kean was hospitalized for serious depression.
Who else is running in New Jersey?
In the closing days of the midterm season, the race in South Jersey’s 2nd Congressional District has emerged as a surprisingly close contest between four-term incumbent Republican Rep. Jeff Van Drew and Democratic challenger Zack Mullock, a small-town Jersey Shore mayor from Cape May. Early voting showed Democrats building a large lead in the vote heading into election day.
Democratic congressional candidates Rep. Analilia Mejia, first-time candidate Dr. Adam Hamawy, and Rep. Nellie Pou are all expected to be victorious Tuesday in districts around the state, according to political analysts like Cook Political Report and Decision Desk HQ. Republican Rep. Chris Smith is also favored to win a 24th term in New Jersey’s ruby red 4th district.
Democratic Sen. Cory Booker is also heavily favored to win a fourth consecutive term amidst rumors he’s teeing up a run for president in 2028.
Are federal law enforcement or immigration agents allowed at poll sites?
No. Federal law enforcement officials are not legally allowed at poll sites. Every New York City poll site does have NYPD officers assigned to it under state law.
If a voter has a problem in New York or New Jersey, the person can call 1-866-OUR-VOTE to speak with a volunteer with the nonpartisan Election Protection hotline.
This story has been updated with additional information.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3.title: How US midterms have cost a record $12bn as cost of living soars
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3.text:
How US midterms have cost a record $12bn as cost of living soars
Candidates, donors and super PACs are spending more than ever on political campaigns.
The US midterm elections are on track to be the most expensive for candidates and political donors in history. According to OpenSecrets, a research group that tracks money in US politics, close to a record $12bn has been spent by candidates and outside political groups on campaigning.
The world’s richest man, Elon Musk alone has given $445 million to the Republicans, according to campaign finance records.
Critics have questioned the huge sums of money being spent to sway voting during an election cycle in which the cost of living and affordability have been the key issues in most campaign agendas.
They argue that campaign spending policy gives wealthy donors, corporations and special interest groups outsized influence over candidate and policy selection.
Why has so much been spent on these elections?
US elections are funded in two ways. Firstly, candidates can directly raise money for their campaigns. In the lead-up to these midterms, Democratic candidates are expected to have spent more than $2.2bn compared with $1.4bn by Republican candidates, according to OpenSecrets.
Secondly, corporations, unions and other associations can spend money on election campaigns, independently of individual candidates’ campaigns, in a process known as “outside spending”.
Previously, these organisations were barred from funding adverts close to elections in order to prevent corruption or the appearance of corruption. But in 2010, the US Supreme Court overturned that rule, treating election communications as protected political speech.
In a related ruling, a lower court struck down limits on the size of contributions these groups could raise, provided they did not coordinate directly with candidates.
Since then, Federal Election Commission disclosure data shows such spending on elections has increased hugely, nearly tripling in the past decade alone from $4.12bn in 2016 to an estimated $11.9bn for 2026’s midterm elections.
This “outside spending” is largely driven by groups called independent expenditure-only political action committees – better known as super PACs – which organise the funding and then spend it on advertising or other initiatives in support of candidates or parties.
How do super PACs operate?
There are no limits on the amount of money donors can give to outside spending groups such as super PACs.
That has been the case since the Supreme Court ruled that unlimited contributions to groups which do not coordinate directly with candidates are protected under free speech laws.
The majority of super PACs are politically aligned and organised in line with either the Democratic or Republican Party.
Among the largest super PACs are the Senate Leadership Fund, which has spent $489 million, and MAGA Inc, with $353 million, both for Republican candidates. The Senate Majority PAC and the House Majority PAC have spent $248 million and $192 million respectively on Democratic candidates.
Other super PACs are organised by individuals and special interest groups, such as the Republican-supporting America PAC founded and funded by Elon Musk and the Democracy PAC funded and organised by George Soros which backs Democratic candidates.
Super PACs report on their direct contributors as well as financial activity to the Federal Election Commission (FEC) every month during election years, and every six months during non-election years. But contributors may include organisations whose own funding sources are not publicly disclosed.
This means that funds can pass through multiple organisations – sometimes through other PACs, known as “shell PACs” – before they are spent on campaign-related activities or advertising, making it difficult to trace contributions back to their original source.
When an original source of political spending cannot be identified, the funds are commonly described as “dark money”. According to OpenSecrets, “dark money” contributions will surpass a record $1.5bn in these midterm elections. That is up from the previous record of $1.35bn set in 2024 and has prompted concerns about the transparency of funding for political candidates.
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has accused the nonprofit lobbying group, American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), of spending “millions in dark money”, for example, on pro-Israel candidates.
Public records reviewed by Al Jazeera found that AIPAC has channelled millions of dollars through shell PACs ahead of the US midterm elections.
What do we know about AIPAC?
AIPAC is one of the best-known super PACs and has attracted criticism in recent years, particularly in light of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. The lobbying group decided to end endorsements and direct campaign contributions after a challenging year.
AIPAC was founded as the American Zionist Committee for Public Affairs by American journalist and lawyer Isaiah Kenan in the 1950s. It was renamed American Israel Public Affairs Committee in 1959 and has grown to more than 6 million members. On its website it says “AIPAC helps pro-Israel candidates no matter their race, religion or background, and opposes anti-Israel candidates no matter their race, religion or background”.
Much of the money AIPAC spends has been channelled through the United Democracy Project (UDP), another registered super PAC affiliated with it. AIPAC has spent money on both Republican and Democratic campaigns, and has been accused of using money raised by Republican donors to fund adverts for “moderate” Democratic candidates in the hope of unseating or blocking progressive candidates, particularly those with pro-Palestine views.
That includes nearly $15 million spent on advertising and campaigning for pro-Israel Democrat George Latimer to stand against progressive Jamaal Bowman in New York’s 16th congressional district Democratic House primary in June 2024. Latimer ultimately won that vote.
AIPAC also spent $5.24 million on advertising for Wesley Bell against Cori Bush, who has criticised Israel’s war on Gaza, in the St Louis, Missouri primary which Bush lost. UDP has also spent $20.7 million to campaign against Abdul El Sayed in the Michigan Senate race.
Reject AIPAC, a coalition of progressive advocacy groups, launched a campaign calling on candidates for federal office to promise not to take endorsements or contributions from AIPAC or aligned PACs in 2024.
The coalition includes Justice Democrats and the Working Families Party, as well as organisations focused on Palestinian rights, including the US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Jewish Voice for Peace (JVP) Action and the IfNotNow Movement.
Where has the most money been spent?
The greatest amounts of money have been spent in “toss-up” states – where candidates face a close race – including Georgia, Texas and Michigan, which has seen record spending in its Senate contest between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
In Michigan, an estimated $333m has been spent on the campaign. Rogers has raised about $23m in direct contributions, while El-Sayed has brought in approximately $54m. Outside groups, however, have spent about $169m supporting Rogers and roughly $94m supporting El-Sayed.
But multiple polls have shown that the cost of living and the economy are the key current concerns for both Republican and Democratic voters.
This spending comes as the US is in the grip of a cost-of-living crisis, with fuel prices in particular soaring as a result of the Trump administration’s war on Iran. Prices have skyrocketed since February after shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz caused the cost of diesel to spike by 65 percent and fertiliser costs rose by up to 40 percent causing food prices to rise.
El Sayed, in particular, has campaigned on reforming election funding and taking “money out of politics”.
But a football fan on X responded: “$12 billion in political ads for the midterms, amaze me. Spending that much in such a useless way while saying we don’t have money for schools and/or healthcare.”
What else could $12bn have paid for?
According to the Iran War Energy Cost Tracker, Americans have spent at least $150bn on petrol and diesel since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February, 30 percent more than they would have spent without the war raising prices. $12bn could cover 8 percent of those fuel costs or roughly $92 per household.
The Trump administration included $12bn in spending cuts for the Department of Education as part of the 2026 fiscal budget. That $12bn could pay for roughly 1 percent of the federal government budget for public schools.
There have also been spending cuts in medical and science research funding, including to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). $12bn could increase the NIH research funding budget of $47bn by one-quarter.

https://jacobin.com/2026/11/brazil-hilto.title: A Fight for Workers’ Rights Turned the Tide in Brazil
https://jacobin.com/2026/11/brazil-hilto.author: Cruz Bonlarron Martínez
https://jacobin.com/2026/11/brazil-hilto.text:
A Fight for Workers’ Rights Turned the Tide in Brazil
Erika Hilton, one of Brazil’s first trans legislators, has brought new energy to the Brazilian left. The socialist congresswoman helped lead the fight to establish a 40-hour workweek that also gave a vital boost to Lula’s presidential campaign.
As Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his historic victory over far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, he embraced trans congresswoman Erika Hilton and kissed her on the cheek in celebration. The video circulated on social media, with many users pointing to it as evidence of Brazil’s acceptance of trans identity and the key role that the LGBTQ+ community plays within Lula’s coalition.
It is important to note that Hilton and other LGBTQ+ politicians are more than simply a piece of a diverse coalition. They are the force behind a piece of legislation that will reduce the Brazilian workweek from forty-four to forty hours, a historic achievement that contributed to Lula’s victory and helped keep fascism at bay.
Life Beyond Work
One day in 2023, after finishing his shift, a pharmacy assistant in Rio de Janeiro called Rick Azevedo decided to record a video railing against the six-day work schedule to which much of the Brazilian working class are subject, including a disproportionate number of black workers. In the video, he referred to the 6 x 1, the colloquial name for this work regime, as a “modern form of slavery” and asked when the working class was going to make a revolution to put an end to it.
Azevedo went on to note that if he, as a single man, had no time to do anything, he could only imagine how bad things are for others with kids. He ended the video with a call to revolt, warning that if ordinary workers like him did not organize behind the issue, things would never change. He originally archived the video, but after his manager called him in to work early the next day, he decided to post it on TikTok during his shift.
The video quickly went viral, with thousands of interactions shortly after it was posted. Azevedo, who already had a following on TikTok for posts about pop culture and Beyoncé Knowles, received messages from others who felt the same way. In response, he founded the social movement Vida Além do Trabalho (VAT, “Life Beyond Work”), organizing first through live streams and WhatsApp groups, then through petitions to change the law.
Azevedo, who had spent much of his life jumping from job to job but never finding enough time to finish formal university studies, became a movement leader overnight. The movement soon spread to other states and crowdfunded a protest in São Paulo to organize around the issue, gaining the attention of Erika Hilton, a rising star in the Socialism and Liberty Party (PSOL). Because of his newfound popularity, Azevedo decided to run for Rio’s City Council in 2024 with PSOL’s support, further popularizing the movement and solidifying his alliance with Erika Hilton.
The Fight in Congress
After the initial 2024 protests and news of Azevedo’s election in Rio, calls to change the workweek gained momentum and were taken up by some of Brazil’s progressive members of Congress. However, under Brazilian law, a change of this kind could not be made through a simple legislative process; it required an amendment to the Brazilian Constitution.
In Brazil, a constitutional amendment requires one-third of members in both houses to sign on. This seemed very hard to achieve at the time because many of those in Congress belonged to right-wing and center-right parties that initially opposed the change.
In February 2025, Hilton got 234 members of Congress to sign on to the constitutional amendment proposal, well over the third needed, allowing her to bring the amendment up for formal debate in Congress. The initial proposal also proved to be quite ambitious, calling for a thirty-six-hour workweek spread over four days without any cut to pay, which would have transformed Brazil’s labor regulations into some of the most progressive in Latin America.
The thirty-six-hour workweek met opposition from sectors on the center and Right who chose to side with capital and oppose it. Azevedo’s VAT movement and the Brazilian labor movement mobilized around the demand on May 1, and President Lula made the end of the 6 x 1 work schedule a centerpiece in his May Day address in 2025.
Lula stated that this change was necessary to build a balance between workers’ professional lives and their well-being. But despite the pressure, the legislation sat in Congress for the rest of 2025. In April 2026, the president sent his own proposal to Congress to keep the issue in the media cycle and continue putting pressure on the lower chamber.
The End of 6 x 1
The combination of pressure from above and below worked, and in May the proposal finally passed the lower chamber and moved to the Senate. By this point, the reform had been modified so that it would establish a forty-hour workweek with two days off instead of the four-day workweek Hilton had initially proposed.
The timing now meant that labor reform would be a key part of the national debate in Brazil’s presidential election. The right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro was a sitting senator at the time, and he felt obliged to support the proposed constitutional change for fear of losing working-class voters. This essentially meant conceding that the Right had been wrong to oppose the labor reform.
After the first round of elections on October 4, it seemed that Bolsonaro’s compromise might have sufficed to shore up support for his candidacy, as he topped the polls and his far-right Liberal Party made significant gains in both houses of Congress. However, Rick Azevedo was elected to Congress on the same night, and Erika Hilton became the female deputy with the highest number of votes in Brazilian history: 1,596,472. This demonstrated how the fight for a shorter workweek connected with diverse sectors of the Brazilian electorate.
On October 14, a week after the first round of the election, the Brazilian Senate voted 75–1 to end the forty-four-hour workweek. This promised a change to the lives of sixteen million Brazilians who previously had only one day off a week. Although the legislation that eventually passed was less ambitious than Hilton’s original proposal, it still lowered the work week to forty hours with two days off. This promises to empower millions of workers by making Brazil into one of the few countries in Latin America, a region where businesses are notorious for exploiting workers, to have a forty-hour week.
Winning the Culture Wars
The debate around the forty-hour week became a key space for Lula’s campaign to regain momentum after it initially fell behind Bolsonaro in the first round, shifting the focus to what was at stake for the Brazilian working class and the possibility of future reforms. The issue forced the Right to concede that Lula and his coalition had the best interests of workers at heart.
The debate also revealed the hypocrisy of the Right’s homophobic and transphobic rhetoric around the family, with a gay man and a trans woman leading the fight for working-class families to be able to spend more time together, get an education, and watch their children grow. Now, as Lula enters his fourth (and surely final) term, the global left should watch closely to learn how to take back the narrative from the Right and connect working-class interests with the diverse forms of oppression that workers face.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120363.title: Fußball | VfL Wolfsburg: Bissige Wölfinnen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120363.author: Frank Hellmann
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120363.text:
- Sport
- Fußball
VfL Wolfsburg: Bissige Wölfinnen
Die behaupten sich nach dem großen Umbruch. Das 8:0 im DFB-Pokal gibt Rückenwind für die Duelle mit Frankfurt und München.
Eindrucksvoller kann der Einzug in das Viertelfinale des DFB-Pokals gegen einen Ligakonkurrenten kaum gelingen. Die Fußballerinnen des VfL Wolfsburg traten am Montagabend im Heimspiel gegen die TSG Hoffenheim dermaßen fest aufs Gaspedal, dass am Ende ein 8:0 von der Anzeigetafel leuchtete. Etlichen Hoffenheimerinnen standen Tränen in den Augen, während die Siegerinnen ihre Freude nicht verbargen. »Es hat eine Menge Spaß gemacht. Wenn es nach zwölf Minuten 2:0 steht, dann hat man viel richtig gemacht«, sagte Torhüterin Stina Johannes, die wettbewerbsübergreifend zum achten Mal in dieser Saison zu null spielte. »Das gibt uns eine große Sicherheit. Wir haben mit der Eintracht und Bayern jetzt zwei echt krasse Kracher vor uns«, meinte die 26-Jährige.
Bereits am Freitag (18.30 Uhr) wartet das Verfolgerduell bei Eintracht Frankfurt, ehe der Spitzenreiter aus München am 14. November beim Vizemeister vorspielt. »Das Selbstvertrauen müssen wir mitnehmen«, forderte auch Trainer Stephan Lerch, der erstaunt war, wie konsequent seine »Wölfinnen« auf Torejagd gingen. Für den im Vorjahr aus dem Kraichgau zurückgekehrten Coach diente das Schützenfest als Werbung in eigener Sache: Sein Vertrag läuft am Saisonende aus. Der 42-Jährige befindet sich nach eigener Aussage in »guten Gesprächen«, würde dem VW-Klub jedoch raten, für die VfL-Fußballerinnen »noch mehr zu machen«, was angesichts der Krise des Autobauers natürlich leicht gesagt ist. »Man muss festhalten, dass es uns hier in Wolfsburg schon sehr gut geht. Aber der Frauenfußball dreht sich immer weiter, und da müssen die Weichen gestellt werden«, sagte Lerch bei Sky.
Die Konkurrenz investiert
Sonst zieht die nationale Konkurrenz vorbei. Neben Union Berlin verstärkt auch Bayer Leverkusen die Anstrengungen, Frankfurt erhöhte laut Vorstandschef Axel Hellmann den Etat für die Frauen um eine Million Euro. Und was passiert erst, wenn Borussia Dortmund mit dem ehemaligen Wolfsburger Macher Ralf Kellermann und der Ikone Alexandra Popp die Regionalliga verlässt?
International sind die englischen Vereine sowie die spanischen und französischen Topklubs bereits enteilt. Für den Werksverein war das Ausscheiden in den Champions-League-Playoffs gegen Inter Mailand bitter. Immerhin hat sich das Team mit dem Europa Cup arrangiert. Nach dem 7:0 im Hinspiel gegen Feyenoord Rotterdam ist der Viertelfinaleinzug im Rückspiel am 10. November nur noch Formsache. Zuvor wird das Kräftemessen beim »ewigen Dritten« Frankfurt Aufschluss darüber geben, wo der VfL jetzt steht. In der Vorsaison lag er 16 Punkte hinter den Bayern und erhielt im Pokalfinale (0:4) eine Lehrstunde.
Leistungsträgerinnen brauchen Perspektiven
Führungsspielerin Svenja Huth erinnerte daran, dass dieser Wettbewerb nun mal »der kürzeste Weg zu einem Titel« sei. Die unverwüstliche 35-Jährige reizt es, erneut jene Trophäe zu holen, auf die der VfL von 2015 bis 2024 ein Abonnement besaß. Doch zwei Umbrüche mit dem Verlust der meisten Topspielerinnen blieben nicht folgenlos. Nun zeichnet sich ab, dass die niederländische Topscorerin Ella Peddemors über den Sommer hinaus kaum zu halten ist. Daher braucht es Perspektiven, damit beispielsweise Cora Zicai länger bleibt. Die 21-Jährige hat in ihrer zweiten Saison am Mittellandkanal einen Sprung gemacht und dürfte mit zur WM 2027 nach Brasilien fahren. Zuvor unternehmen die DFB-Frauen noch eine nicht unumstrittene Südamerika-Reise mit Testspielen gegen Argentinien in La Plata (30. November) und gegen Peru in Rio de Janeiro (4. Dezember).
Gemeinsam gegen die Playoff-Pläne
Vorerst blicken viele auf den live in der ARD übertragenen Gipfel gegen die Bayern in der VW-Arena. Vermutlich wird am Rande auch über jene Playoffs diskutiert, die bereits für die nächste Saison im Gespräch sind. Sie könnten die Vormachtstellung der Münchnerinnen gefährden. Der VfL Wolfsburg ist sich mit dem FC Bayern vor der Mitgliederversammlung des Ligaverbands FBL am 30. November einig, dass mit dem »revolutionären Szenario«, wie es in der Ausschreibung der Medienrechte heißt, der Wesenskern des Ligabetriebs ruiniert würde. Weil über die Meisterschaft dann letztlich ein einziges Spiel entscheiden würde. Wie im Pokal.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Gwyn Topham and Jamie Grierson
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
At least seven planes around Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats to passenger flights on Tuesday.
Two UK departures and a number of Ryanair flights were threatened in what the government called “malicious hoaxes”, after all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
It was not clear if the incidents were linked, although authorities in both Bulgaria and Italy said the threats were made against two incoming Ryanair flights.
One of Warsaw’s two main airports was briefly closed after receiving a diverted plane, with Polish officials confirming that they had received bomb threats involving two flights coming into the capital.
The threats followed an incident on Monday when another flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted, apparently without substance.
Airlines are used to dealing with fake threats, and while none of the incidents and subsequent searches threw up any evidence of terrorist activity, authorities appear to have responded to an unusual number of reported threats in one day.
Security fears around aviation have been reignited with the recent FlyDubai incident when a co-pilot attempted to crash a Tel Aviv-bound plane.
Tuesday’s series of incidents started with a flight from London Heathrow operated by the Polish carrier LOT, which was scheduled to arrive at Warsaw’s Chopin airport but was diverted to the second airport, further from the Polish capital, Modlin. Authorities closed that airport after the alert and the Boeing 737 Max landed without incident.
“The passengers were evacuated and the plane underwent security checks. Nothing was found,” spokesperson Adam Szablowski told AFP. “The airport has been reopened and is operating normally.”
An Scandinavian Airlines plane from Copenhagen to Warsaw was also the subject of a threat but landed at Chopin, where a security inspection that did not turn up any explosive devices closed part of the airport.
Another UK departure, a Ryanair plane from Manchester, was met by emergency vehicles on landing at its destination, Murcia in southern Spain after another threat. Spanish regionals authorities confirmed on social media that no explosives were found on the flight.
A UK government spokesperson said of the threats to two departures from Britain: “The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
“Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.”
In Italy, two Ryanair flights were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following potential bomb threats, according to the airport operator ADR. The first was a flight from Lisbon, while a second later in the morning from Dublin was escorted in by Italian air force fighter jets until landing.
Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters that threats were made against a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo and a Ryanair flight from Dublin to the capital Sofia. Both flights were carrying about 180 passengers and landed safely, with no devices found on inspection.
The separate incidents came the day after a Wizz Air service from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet.
The plane, which was due to depart from Luton at 8.15am on Monday for Sofia, was diverted after a bomb threat was received “during the flight”, Wizz Air said.
 
Ryanair did not respond to requests for comment.
Airlines abide by a regulated process to assess and manage bomb threats, although virtually all are fake. In the UK, airlines file a mandatory occurrence report to the Civil Aviation Authority.
Philip Baum, visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, said that the industry had to deal with bomb threats “on a daily basis” around the world. He said: “Most are from individuals who think it is funny or want to delay a flight for some reason. If the industry was to respond to every unsubstantiated threat, flights would grind to a halt. The reality is that terrorist organisations who might like to smuggle a bomb on to a flight don’t tell people, they claim responsibility after the attacks.”
However, the fact that some aircraft did divert would “imply that the threats are credible and specific in nature, and therefore one has to respond accordingly”, he said.
Baum added: “Obviously we don’t ignore anything but we have to differentiate between the hoax call and the specific threat. In the vast majority of instances the aircraft carries on without diverting because it is regarded as a non-specific threat.”

https://taz.de/Reiches-Entwurf-fuer-Spri.title: Reiches Entwurf für Spritpreisdeckel: Hohe Hürden bei der Preisbremse für Benzin und Diesel
https://taz.de/Reiches-Entwurf-fuer-Spri.author: Anja Krüger
https://taz.de/Reiches-Entwurf-fuer-Spri.text:
Reiches Entwurf für Spritpreisdeckel: Hohe Hürden bei der Preisbremse für Benzin und Diesel
Die Pläne für einen Spritpreisdeckel von Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche werden harsch kritisiert. SPD-Vizechefin Rehlinger fordert eine Überarbeitung.
Der von Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) vorgelegte Gesetzentwurf für einen Spritpreisdeckel stößt auf harsche Kritik – auch aus der SPD. Die saarländische Ministerpräsidentin und SPD-Vizevorsitzende Anke Rehlinger fordert, dass der Entwurf überarbeitet wird.
Die Spritpreise sind infolge des Irankriegs drastisch gestiegen. Die Bundesregierung hat deshalb zunächst im Frühjahr, dann für die letzten drei Monate dieses Jahres die Energiesteuer auf Benzin und Diesel herabgesetzt. Das ist der sogenannte Tankrabatt. Studien zufolge haben die Ölkonzerne die Preise viel stärker angehoben als angesichts der Weltmarktlage gerechtfertigt und damit Milliarden an sogenannten Übergewinnen eingefahren. Den Tankrabatt geben sie nicht komplett weiter.
Im September hatten Union, SPD und die Bundesländer vereinbart, dass der Bund Gespräche mit der Mineralölwirtschaft führt, „mit dem Ziel, spätestens zum 1. Januar 2027 einen Spritpreisdeckel nach dem Vorbild Luxemburgs oder Belgiens einzuführen“. Dort legt der Staat generell eine Obergrenze für den Benzin- und Dieselpreis fest. Das sieht Reiches Entwurf aber nicht vor.
Nach ihren Vorstellungen soll es im Anschluss an den zum 1. Januar auslaufenden Tankrabatt überhaupt keinen Preisdeckel geben. Ihr Gesetzentwurf schafft lediglich die Grundlage für die Einführung. „Die Bundesregierung wird ermächtigt, durch Rechtsverordnung ohne Zustimmung des Bundesrates Höchstpreise für die Abgabe von Otto- oder Dieselkraftstoffen an Letztverbraucher an öffentlichen Tankstellen festzulegen“, heißt es in dem Entwurf. Die Hürden für die Einführung sind allerdings extrem hoch: Nur wenn die Preise in Deutschland an drei aufeinanderfolgenden Wochen um 5 Prozentpunkte mehr steigen als im EU-Schnitt, könnte er eingeführt werden. Das ist in den vergangenen zehn Jahren nicht vorgekommen.
Rehlinger: Deckel ohne Wirkung
In der SPD ist der Unmut über den Entwurf groß. „Das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium hat dem Spritpreisdeckel alle Zähne gezogen“, sagte SPD-Vizechefin Rehlinger der taz. „Eine Entlastung der Autofahrer kann dieser Gesetzesentwurf nicht bringen, deshalb muss er überarbeitet werden.“ Er sei „erkennbar darauf angelegt“, dass der Spritpreisdeckel niemals Wirkung entfalte. Das sei nicht das, was verabredet worden sei.
Der wirtschaftspolitische Sprecher der SPD-Bundstagsfraktion Sebastian Roloff fordert ebenfalls Nachbesserungen. Dass es zum 1. Januar keinen Spritpreisdeckel gebe, sei den Menschen und Unternehmen, die unter den hohen Preisen leiden, weder zu vermitteln noch zuzumuten. „Ministerin Reiche muss entscheiden, ob sie Bürger und Mittelstand entlastet oder ob sie die Schutzpatronin für die Abzockgewinne der Mineralölkonzerne sein will“, betonte er.
Das von SPD-Chef Lars Klingbeil geführte Bundesfinanzministerium äußerte sich mit Hinweis auf die laufenden regierungsinternen Abstimmungen zu dem Gesetzentwurf nicht.
Opposition fordert Übergewinnsteuer
Die Opposition empört der Entwurf. „Für die Verbraucher wird das Konzept von Katherina Reiche wahrscheinlich zur wirkungslosen Enttäuschung“, sagte die Co-Vorsitzende der grünen Bundestagsfraktion Katharina Dröge. „Währenddessen machen die Ölkonzerne, dank freundlicher Zuarbeit von Frau Reiche, weiter Übergewinne.“ Dröge fordert eine Übergewinnsteuer, „die die Milliardengewinne der Konzerne an die Menschen zurückgibt“.
Die Linksfraktion im Bundestag sieht in Reiches Entwurf eine „Beihilfe zur Wegelagerei“. Die Ministerin sabotiere den Auftrag des Koalitionsbeschlusses zum Spritpreisdeckel, sagte die Fraktions-Vizevorsitzende Janine Wissler. „Damit stellt sie sich auf die Seite der Ölkonzerne, die Milliarden an Übergewinnen auf dem Rücken der Menschen erzielen“, sagte sie. Die Linkspartei fordert ebenfalls eine Übergewinnsteuer.
Der Entwurf soll nach derzeitigem Zeitplan am Mittwoch vom Kabinett verabschiedet werden. Das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium wollte zu der Kritik ebenfalls mit Hinweis auf die regierungsinterne Abstimmung nicht Stellung nehmen.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse

Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. https://gothamist.com/news/trump-adminis.title: Trump administration sends election monitors to NYC, NJ
https://gothamist.com/news/trump-adminis.author: Catalina Gonella
https://gothamist.com/news/trump-adminis.text:
The United States Department of Justice said Tuesday it’s sending election monitors to polling sites in Manhattan and Brooklyn in New York, and three counties in New Jersey.
It’s the first time the DOJ is sending election monitors to all 50 states, according to the federal agency. The Trump administration has previously said it planned to deploy about 1,000 monitors nationwide, but hadn’t announced specific locations.
The DOJ said election monitors would be in Manhattan and Brooklyn as well as Westchester, Albany and Erie counties in New York. In New Jersey, they’ll be monitoring polls at Middlesex, Bergen and Union counties. Portions of Union County are in the 7th Congressional District, where Republican Tom Kean Jr. is hoping to fend off a challenge from Rebecca Bennett. The race is considered among the most competitive in the country as Democrats try to take control of the House.
Local Democratic leaders, including New York Attorney General Letitia James, have issued statements in recent weeks, urging voters not to be intimidated by federal authorities near the polls and warning that election interference and voter intimidation are illegal.
James said in a statement last week that while it is normal for the DOJ to send election monitors to polling sites, they can't demand identification from voters, interfere with poll workers or engage in political activity near the polls. She said if poll workers encounter people identifying as DOJ monitors without advance notice, they should contact county election officials.
The DOJ said the monitors would include workers from its Civil Rights Division, U.S. Attorney’s Offices and Office of Personnel Management observers.
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill said during last week’s installment of WNYC’s “Ask Governor Sherrill” call-in show that state officials have been working to ensure those running elections throughout the state know how to protect voters’ rights.
“We have been briefing all of the poll workers, all the municipalities and the counties to make sure that they understand all their rights and that they are alerting us,” she said. “If there are any concerns at their polling place, we will be in court very, very quickly to shut down any attempt to interfere with our elections.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘Respeito ao tempo dos mais velhos’: multiartista analisa estética e desafios do cinema indígena
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Afonso Bezerra
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Uma pesquisa inédita ouviu 60 mulheres cineastas indígenas com o objetivo de sistematizar os modos de criação, as trajetórias, as relações com os territórios, as dificuldades enfrentadas e as necessidades dessas realizadoras. O levantamento “Ler o vento, filmar o mundo” será lançado na Mostra Internacional de Cinema de São Paulo.
Ao É de Manhã, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, a multiartista Larissa Duarte Tukano explica que há uma imensa diversidade de territórios indígenas, e cada um traz particularidades. “Apesar de eu ser indígena, eu não conheço muito bem as outras culturas indígenas. E no cinema a gente aproxima e conhece, conversa, dialoga. Tem questões comuns e tem questões específicas de cada cultura, de cada povo”, argumenta.
Na visão dela, a pesquisa é importante para trazer a realidade da produção indígena para o público em geral, especialmente da perspectiva das mulheres. “É necessário trazer esses dados para as pessoas que fazem políticas públicas, editais, essas coisas, para reconhecer que nós existimos e fazemos cinemas”, avalia.
Tukano conta que o fazer audiovisual dos povos indígenas passa por um respeito à ancestralidade. “Quando uma pessoa indígena vai fazer um documentário ou um filme de ficção, como ela já conhece a sua realidade, ela vai respeitar o tempo dos mais velhos. Não é só uma coisa bonita, uma paisagem, mas o que é importante mostrar sobre o dia a dia dela. Então, eu acho que são perspectivas diferentes”, afirma.
A multiartista também critica o fato de editais voltados a apoiar a produção indígena muitas vezes desconsiderarem a realidade da produção e a particularidade de cada povo. “Há territórios que não têm internet, que não têm um meio de comunicação e o edital abre, mas há pouco tempo para se inscrever. Além disso, exige experiência e documentos que a gente não vai possuir. A linguagem técnica também é bem difícil de utilizar, porque há mulheres como eu, cuja primeira língua é o tukano. O português que eu falo é a segunda língua para me comunicar, e tem essa dificuldade. O edital não atende às diferentes realidades. Por exemplo, no Amazonas, o território é extenso e, se você preencher os custos, eles serão diferentes dos custos daqui do Sudeste, onde as coisas são bem mais próximas. Então, eles não vão conseguir entender isso no projeto que eu for fazer”, observa.
Para ouvir e assistir
O É de Manhã vai ao ar de segunda a sexta-feira, às 7h da manhã, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM, na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.title: An expert’s guide to Pierre-Auguste Renoir: five must-read books on the French Impressionist
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.author: José da Silva
https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/.text:
• Click here for more reading lists on the world's greatest artists
The French Impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir is a surprisingly divisive artist, from some of his peers denigrating him to the so-called Renoir Sucks at Painting movement a decade ago and a critic recently labelling him “the chocolate boxiest” of the Impressionists. But the recently opened exhibition Renoir and Love at the National Gallery in London (which debuted at the Musée d’Orsay in Paris earlier this year and will travel to Boston in 2027) has had—for the most part—rave reviews and robust ticket sales. Its co-curator Christopher Riopelle, who is also the author of Renoir: The Great Bathers (1990), has selected five key books for anyone wanting to go beyond first impressions.
Renoir, My Father (1962) by Jean Renoir
“Father and son, both artistic geniuses—a rare combination. That the great cineaste Jean Renoir should have penned an idiosyncratic, anecdote-filled life of the father is more than we deserve. Moreover, it is a film-maker’s biography, countless scenes set up visually, in flowing time. No surprise to learn that the loving son wrote it in far-off Hollywood!”
Renoir’s Portraits: Impressions of an Age (1997) by Colin B. Bailey
“Colin B. Bailey is our leading Renoir scholar. It is invidious to choose which of his several publications to include; I settle on this study of 69 portraits. Bulging with new information, it is every bit as indispensable to social historians as to art historians. As Renoir studies resurge, let us hope it returns to print.”
Renoir in the 20th Century (2010) with essays by Roger Benjamin, Claudia Einecke, Guy Cogeval, Isabelle Gaëtan, Emmanuelle Héran, John House, Virgine Journiac, Martha Lucy, Laurence Madeline, Monique Nonne and Sylvie Patry
“Late Renoir: Marmite. But the period includes among its admirers Henri Matisse, Pablo Picasso and the collector Albert C. Barnes. Sylvie Patry guides us through the final two decades with concision, deep respect and an unfailing eye for bravura painting. More than that, she demonstrates why the allusive Classicism of the late works played a key role in Modernism.”
Renoir in the Barnes Foundation (2012) by Martha Lucy and John House
“The Renoir scholar John House wrote this assessment of the largest and greatest of all Renoir collections with a passionate and utterly engaged eye. Martha Lucy was with him all the way; it’s as if we eavesdrop on a wickedly clever conversation between receptive student and brilliant, probing master.”
Auguste Renoir: Lettres choisies (2026), edited by Augustin de Butler and Anne Distel
“At last, a meticulous scholarly edition of 314 key Renoir letters tracing his career from 1865 to 1919. Helped in shaping by the consummate Renoir scholar Anne Distel, finally we can ‘hear’ the master’s voice. The wit is clear but so, too, the anxiety. Let us have a translation soon, to stand beside the newly translated Claude Monet letters.”
• Renoir and Love, National Gallery, London, until 31 January 2027; Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, 28 February 2027-13 June 2027
